procnotices.notice_text:
AVIS D’APPEL D’0FFRE NATIONALE  

   N° 2026/002/MAPA/FSRP-KM/AO/TRX

Objet : Marché de Construction d'un magasin de stockage des provendes avec bureaux vitrés, Structure métallique et bâtiments annexes en maçonnerie Restaurant — Vestiaires — Douches

Le Gouvernement de l’Union des Comores, à travers le Ministère de l’Agriculture, de la Pêche et de l’Artisanat, a mis en œuvre le Projet de Résilience des Systèmes Alimentaires aux Comores (FSRP-KM) financé par la Banque mondiale.

Dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre des activités du Projet (FSRP), la Coordination nationale lance un Appel d’Offre pour  la Construction d'un Magasin de stockage des provendes avec bureaux vitrés, Structure métallique et bâtiments annexes en maçonnerie Restaurant — Vestiaires — Douches  , destiné à contribuer à l’amélioration des capacités de stockage ainsi qu’ en  à renforcer la disponibilité et la conservation des aliments pour volailles dans le cadre du développement des chaînes de valeurs agricoles.

Pour avoir plus d’informations sur l’Appel d’Offre, veuillez télécharger le Dossier d’Appel d’offre sur notre site internet à partir de ce lien : https://fsrp-km.org/appel-doffre/

La date limite de soumission ainsi que d’ouverture des plis est fixée au 30 / 09 / 2026 à 14h00.

Pour soumissionner, veuillez déposer votre offre technique physiquement au siège du FSRP_KM, sis au Ministère de l’Agriculture à Mdé – Ex Cefader.

                                                                 Lancé, le 10 Septembre 2026

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES - FIRMS SELECTION)

Country:                       Mozambique

Name of Project:         Climate Resilient Roads for the North (CRRN - P500488)

Grant No.:                  E315-MZ

Assignment Title:        Consultancy Services for Preparation of Feasibility Study, Conceptual design, Environmental and Social Impact Assessment and bidding documents for Civil Works under Design, Build and Transfer Methodology for the Roads N361: Lichinga – Lago Niassa (98.0 km), and R733/R1211/R1215 Lussimbesse – Matchedje (206 km) in Niassa Province”

Reference No:             47A003041/CP/ 28/2026

Client:                          National Roads Administration/ Administração Nacional de Estradas,IP (ANE, IP)

1. The Government of Mozambique (GoM) has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Climate Resilient Roads for the North (CRRN), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consultancy Services for Preparation of Feasibility Study, Conceptual design, Environmental and Social Impact Assessment and bidding documents for Civil Works under Design, Build and Transfer Methodology for the Roads N361: Lichinga – Lago Niassa (98.0 km), and R733/R1211/R1215 Lussimbesse – Matchedje (206 km) in Niassa Province, hereafter designated the “Services”.

2. The objectives of the Services are:

a) To prepare a feasibility study and Conceptual design based on international standards and concept engineering designs, which will be a basis for a prospective contractor to develop detailed engineering designs;

b) To prepare the ESIA for the road project sites to ensure the project conceptual design incorporates the mitigation measures for the potential negative impacts and maximizes the positive impacts of the project in a manner consistent with all applicable requirements of the World Bank Group Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and the relevant national laws.

3. The Terms of Reference (ToR) can be obtained through the following link  https://www.fe.gov.mz/storage/app/uploads/public/6a9/023/b4b/6a9023b4bec16361581863.pdf or alternatively at the address below, however these ToR may be subject to changes and the final version will be issued in the Request for Proposals.

4. The Government of Mozambique represented by ANE, IP now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to express their interest in providing the services as summarized in paragraph 2 above. Interested Consultants shall provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. They shall include in their Expressions of Interest the name, address and contact information of the firm and its ownership details. 

5. The evaluation of expressions of interest will be made on a qualitative basis and the short-listing criteria are:

a) Profile of the Firm/Core business demonstrating experience in roads and bridge surveys, economic analysis and design experience.

b) Experience in conducting at least one project of feasibility study/preliminary design/preparation of detailed engineering designs of the minimum two-lane road/highways in similar geographical conditions during the last five years.

c) Experience in conducting climate vulnerability risk assessment for infrastructure projects, particularly road infrastructure, including bridges.

d) Experience in conducting at least one Environmental and Social Impact Assessments (ESIA) and Environmental and preparing Social Management Plans (ESMPs) using World Bank standards and description during the least five (5) years.

e) Experience in preparing design and build bidding documents using the World Bank guidelines:

f) Technical and managerial capability of the firm;

g) Experience in handling externally aided projects such as the World Bank and AfDB will be an advantage; and

h) Experience in fragility, conflict, and violence affected countries is an added advantage.

Note that firms must attach the certificate(s) of completion for each reference of completed project.

Key experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

6. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.13, 3.15, and 3.16 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

7. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

8. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

9. Further information can be obtained at the address below during working hours, from 07:30 - 15:30 hours local time, Mondays to Fridays, except Public Holidays.

10. Expressions of interest in English language, clearly marked RFP Nº 47A003041/CP/28/2026 “Consultancy Services for Preparation of Feasibility Study, Conceptual design, Environmental and Social Impact Assessment and bidding documents for Civil Works under Design, Build and Transfer Methodology for the Roads N361: Lichinga – Lago Niassa (98.0 km), and R733/R1211/R1215 Lussimbesse – Matchedje (206 km) in Niassa Province” must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, by mail or by e-mail) on or before 15:00 hours (local time), on  7th October 2026.

REPUBLIC OF SOUTH SUDAN

MINISTRY OF INFORMATION, COMMUNICATION TECHNOLOGY AND POSTAL SERVICES (MICT&PS)

PROJECT IMPLEMENTATION  UNIT (PIU)

Specific Procurement Notice

Request for Bids

Non-Consulting Services

(Two-Envelope Bidding Process)

Employer: Ministry of Information Communication Technology and Postal Services (MICT&PS)

Project: Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project (EARDIP) – SOP-1

Contract title: Capex for Fibre Deployment for Route A-B

Country: South Sudan

Grant No.: E1780

RFB No: SS-MICT&PS-544330-NC-RFB

Issued on: September 14 2026

1. The Government of South Sudan (GOSS) has received financing from the World Bank to participate in the first series of projects for the Eastern Africa Regional Digital Integration Project (EARDIP-SOP-1). The project development objective is to increase access to broadband and digital services through the development and integration of digital markets in the Eastern Africa Region.

2. Government of South Sudan (GOSS) intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for the Fiber Optic Network Backbone. For this contract, the Borrower shall process the payments using the Direct Payment disbursement method, as defined in the World Bank’s “Disbursement Guidelines for Investment Project Financing”.

3. The Ministry of Information Communication Technology and Postal Services (MICT&PS) now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for matching investments from EARDIP for the design, supply and owner operation of the approximately 397 km backbone terrestrial fibre optic cable (FOC) along the Juba–Nadapal road corridor (to the border with Kenya), with a minimum 17 Points of Presence (POPs) and aggregation points along the route that are designed to support the interconnection of commercial traffic from several major cities and communities served by Mobile network operators (MNOs) and to facilitate last-mile connectivity by MNOs and Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to a number of named public institutions (schools, health centres and governmental locations) within a 10 km radius on both sides of the corridor. The total contract duration between the commencement date and contract completion date is 12 months.

4. Key Qualification Criteria include:

Specific Experience

The Bidder shall demonstrate that it has successfully completed, or substantially completed, during the last three years, at least one of the following:

  • One contract for fiber optic or similar telecommunications/connectivity infrastructure with a value of not less than US$6,000,000; or
  • Two similar contracts, each with a value of not less than US$3,000,000.

The contracts shall be of a nature, scale, and complexity comparable to the works required under this procurement. For each contract submitted, the Bidder shall provide documentary evidence, such as a client-issued completion or performance certificate, indicating the contract value, scope of works, completion status, and dates of execution

Average Annual Turnover

The Bidder shall demonstrate an average annual turnover from contracts of fiber-optic, telecommunications, or similar connectivity infrastructure works of at least US$3,000,000, calculated over any three of the last five financial years. The Bidder shall submit certified financial statements, audited accounts, or other acceptable documentary evidence to substantiate the reported turnover.

Liquid Assets and/or Credit Facilities

The Bidder shall demonstrate access to liquid assets and/or confirmed lines of credit, net of other contractual commitments, of not less than US$1,500,000. Acceptable evidence may include recent bank statements, bank certificates, or a letter from a regulated financial institution confirming the availability of the required funds or credit facilities. The evidence shall be issued no earlier than the period specified in the Bidding Documents.

5. Bidding will be conducted through an international competitive tender using a Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, July 2016” as amended from time to time and is open to all bidders with public telecommunications services experience who are the licensed in South Sudan, as well as potential new entrants who must qualify and eligible for this competition. All bidders may collaborate with any licensed subcontractors, so long as full responsibility for meeting the requirements of this Procurement Document rests fully with the eligible prime contractor. Bidders may also form joint ventures in accordance with the rules of this Procurement Document.

6. Bids will be evaluated in accordance with the evaluation process set out in the procurement document. The following weightings shall apply for Rated Criteria (including technical and non-price factors): 30% and for Bid cost: 70%.

7. Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from the Senior Procurement Specialist, Ministry of Information Communication Technology and Postal Services, Project Implementation Unit (PIU) and inspect the bidding document during office hours from 10.00 hrs to 16:00 hrs at the address given below.  The bidding document in English may be purchased by interested Bidders upon the submission of a written application to the address below and upon payment of a non-refundable fee of United States Dollars three Hundred ($300) or its equivalent in South Sudanese Pounds at prevailing rate. The method of payment will be by cash. The document will be sent by email to those who have paid. Bids must be delivered to the address below on or before 2:00pm South Sudan local time on October 26, 2026. Electronic Bidding will not be permitted. Late Bids will be rejected. The outer Bid envelopes marked “ORIGINAL BID”, and the inner envelopes marked “TECHNICAL PART” will be publicly opened in the presence of the Bidders’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend, at the address below at 2:15pm or immediately after the deadline time for bid submission on October 26, 2026. All envelopes marked “FINANCIAL PART” shall remain unopened and will be held in safe custody of the Employer until the second public Bid opening.

8. All Bids must be accompanied by a Bid-Securing Declaration

9. Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring the Borrower to disclose information on the successful bidder’s beneficial ownership, as part of the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form as included in the bidding document.

Montenegro

Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT)

 

 

Name of Project: CLIMATE RESILIENT FISHERIES AND AGRIFOOD SECTOR DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (CRFASD)

Loan No: IBRD-98890

Assignment Title: PMT SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT SPECIALIST (FULL – TIME)

Reference No. MNE-CRFASD-98890-ME-IC-CS-26-3.2.6

Publication date: September 10, 2026

 

The Montenegro has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of CLIMATE RESILIENT FISHERIES AND AGRIFOOD SECTOR DEVELOPMENT PROJECT (CRFASD), and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this Loan for consulting services for PMT SOCIAL DEVELOPMENT SPECIALIST (FULL – TIME).    

 

The overall objective of this consultant service (“the Service”) is to provide support in managing social risks directly or indirectly attributable or identified as a consequence of the Project, materially compliant to the ESF. The Social Development Specialist will assist MAFWM in ensuring that the Project is carried out in accordance with the Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs) and this Environmental and Social Commitment Plan (ESCP), in a manner acceptable to the World Bank.

 

The Social Development Specialist shall be engaged to deliver all the needed support on a full-time daily basis (8 hours per day, working days, from Monday to Friday). The consultancy is expected to start in September 2026 and continue up to the project's implementation (end of March 2031), including a probation period of three months.

 

The Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management, through Technical Service Unit, now invites eligible individual consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Service. Interested consultants must provide Cover Letter and CV representing description of similar assignments, experience in similar conditions and availability of appropriate skills (scanned diplomas to be sent with CV). Individual consultants may be offered through firms or other organizations, but the qualifications of the individual consultant will be the basis of selection. Contract will be signed with proposed individuals.

 

The criteria for selection are following:

  • Graduate/Advanced Degree (Master’s Degree) in the environment & social safeguard area, Social Sciences, Law, or related discipline.
  • Minimum 5 (five) years of relevant professional experience in social safeguards, community engagement, stakeholder processes, and risk management in investment projects (international and local).
  • Experience in at least 2 internationally funded projects in the field of social risk management under ESF or other IFI standards.
  • Direct involvement in preparation and implementation of ESMF, ESMP, ESMP checklists, RAPs.
  • Knowledge of international good practice for management of E&S risks, including World Bank ESF/Safeguard’s policies and International Finance Corporation (IFC) Sustainability Framework and supporting documents such as Guidance Notes.
  • Previous experience with World Bank-funded projects as a social reviewer and an understanding of their requirements would be an advantage.
  • Knowledge of domestic social and labor legislation would be an advantage.
  • Good analytical skills, ability to think strategically, analyze and synthesize diverse qualitative and quantitative socially related data and information.
  • Excellent spoken and written Montenegrin and English.
  • Computer skills, including word processing and spreadsheets.
  • Driving license, no obstacles for traveling within Montenegro for various field trips.

 

The evaluation criteria will be the following:

(i)         General Qualifications, including education, trainings and qualifications (40 points).

(ii)        Specific experience relevant to the Assignment (60 points).

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers - Procurement in Investment Project Financing Goods, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, February 2025 (Procurement Regulations), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 08,00 to 14,00 hours.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form, only by e-mail, to the address below by September 24, 2026, 12,00h.

Government of Nepal

Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB)

Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project (KV WaSIP) –

Sisneri Water Supply Project

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL)

 

First Date of Publication: 27th August 2026

Senior Dam Specialist - Ref No. KVWaSIP-IC-01-083/84

 

1.0 Background

The Government of Nepal (GoN) has received financing from the World Bank toward the preparation and implementation of the Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project (KV WaSIP) – Sisneri Water Supply Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The consulting services include providing technical, procurement, financial management, environmental and social, contract management, and other professional support required for effective implementation of the Project through the Project Management Unit (PMU)

The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB) now invites eligible Individual Consultants to indicate their interest in providing the above consulting services. Interested Consultants shall provide a detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV) demonstrating that they possess the required educational qualifications, professional experience, and technical competence to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria for each assignment are specified in the respective Terms of Reference (TOR), which may be obtained from the address or website indicated below

The Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board (KVWSMB) intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring Senior Dam Specialist and requests applications from suitably qualified and interested candidates to fill the position.

2. The Objectives of the Assignment

As a team member of the Project Management Unit (PMU), Senior Dam Specialist shall provide senior-level technical leadership, independent review, and quality assurance for the feasibility confirmation, detailed design, and implementation readiness of KV WaSIP – Sisneri Water Supply Project, with a focus on ensuring that the proposed dam, reservoir, intake, source augmentation works, and associated bulk water supply infrastructure are technically sound, safe, climate-resilient, operable, constructible, and fit for long-term service.

 

3. Duties and Responsibilities

The duties of the Specialist is mentioned in the Terms of Reference in detail.

4. Qualifications and Experience

All applications will be evaluated against the assignment’s required qualifications below.  

Candidates who comply with the qualifications will be scored according to predefined criteria. A minimum of three candidates will be shortlisted and interviewed. The candidate with the highest score will be invited to negotiate a contract. Referees of the selected candidate may be contacted to verify prior experience, performance, and interpersonal skills. 

 The Senior Dam Specialist shall possess strong academic qualifications and demonstrated professional experience relevant to dam engineering, bulk water supply systems, and multidisciplinary technical review of major water infrastructure projects. The expert should have proven capability to provide strategic technical leadership, assess the adequacy of feasibility studies and detailed designs, review engineering assumptions and system interfaces, and advise on dam safety, implementation readiness, operational reliability, and long-term asset performance across the full bulk water supply chain.

Qualifications and Relevant Experience

  • Education:
    • The expert shall hold at least a bachelor’s degree in civil engineering, water resources engineering, hydraulic engineering, structural engineering, or a related discipline.  A master’s degree in dam engineering, water resources, hydraulic structures, geotechnical engineering, structural engineering, or a closely related field is required, and a PhD will be considered an added advantage.
  • Work Experience:
  • At least 15 years of relevant professional experience in dam engineering, bulk water supply infrastructure, feasibility and detailed design review, and implementation support for major water resources or water supply projects.
  • Substantial experience in planning, design review, or technical supervision of large dams and associated infrastructure, including reservoirs, intakes, spillways, outlet works, and diversion arrangements.
  • Proven ability to review multidisciplinary engineering studies and technical outputs, with sound knowledge of dam safety principles, reservoir operation, flood handling, instrumentation, emergency preparedness, and risk-informed design and operational review.
  • Interpersonal Skills
  • Strong analytical, report writing, and communication skills, and shall be able to communicate clearly and effectively in spoken and written English.

5. Evaluation and Selection Method

The Senior Dam Specialist will be hired by the PMU using the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method following “World Bank Procurement Regulations for Investment Project Financing Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services” (July 2016) Seventh Edition 2025. 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations”.

6. Duration of the Assignment

The Senior Dam Specialist is expected to provide support to the project team for an expected input of 144 person days during the 17 months grant implementation period on an intermittent basis. The consultant and the client shall plan the inputs of the specialist based on the project schedule and report deliverables of the Design Consultant to be selected.

7. Remuneration

A market-based salary package commensurate with the candidate's experience and qualifications will be offered.

8. Reporting

The Senior Dam Specialist will report directly to the Project Director, PMU.

9. Location

  • The consultant will be based at the PMU office and may be required to travel outside the valley as needed for project-related procurement activities.
  • The Project shall provide following facilities to consultant during his tenure of service:
  • Office space
  • Email and internet access
  • Required office stationery and other materials
  • Photocopying/printing facilities

10. Application Process

Interested candidates shall submit a complete application package comprising:

  1. Up-to-date curriculum vitae (CV).
  2. Copies of academic and professional certificates.
  3. Contact details for at least three (03) professional references familiar with the candidate’s relevant work.

Applications shall be submitted electronically no later than 17.00 PM on 18th September 2026 to the following e-mail address: sisnerikvwsmb@gmail.com. Only complete applications received by the deadline will be considered.

Kathmandu Valley Water Security Improvement Project – Sisneri Water Supply Project

INDEPENDENT STATE OF SAMOA

PACIFIC REGION PREPAREDNESS, ADAPTATION AND RESILIENCE – Samoa Project (PREPARE - Samoa)

 

GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

 

Loan No./Credit No. IDA 7990-WS /TF No. D1619 /Grant No. IDA E636-WS

Project ID No. P507749

 

The Government of Samoa has received financing in the amount of US$ 35 million equivalent from the World Bank toward the cost of the PREPARE-Samoa Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services to be procured under this project. This project will be financed by the International Development Association (IDA) and the Systematic Observations Financing Facility (SOFF).

 

The project will include the procurement of consulting services for technical assistance, design and construction supervision, construction of public buildings and urban infrastructure, and procurement of early warning instrumentation. It will include the following components:

 

Component 1: Hazard Monitoring and Early Warning Systems. This component will strengthen Samoa’s multi-hazard early warning systems through investments in hazard monitoring and forecasting equipment, decision-support systems, communication networks, and technical capacity building. Activities include the supply and installation of meteorological, hydrological, and geophysical monitoring equipment, ICT systems, software, technical assistance, and training services.

 

Component 2: Emergency Preparedness and Response. This component will enhance national and community-level emergency preparedness and response capacities through investments in emergency management infrastructure, equipment, information systems, and community outreach programs. Activities include the construction and fitting out of emergency management facilities, procurement of emergency response equipment, development of digital emergency management systems, and delivery of training and awareness programs.

 

Component 3: Resilient Infrastructure. This component will support climate- and disaster-resilient urban development through risk-informed planning, technical studies, and investments in resilient public infrastructure and public spaces. Activities include consultancy services for urban planning and engineering design, as well as civil works for waterfront improvements, streetscape upgrades, drainage, coastal protection, and resilient public facilities.

 

Component 4: Project Management. This component will finance project implementation support, including procurement, financial management, environmental and social risk management, monitoring and evaluation, communications, audits, and capacity building. Activities include consulting services, training, operational support, and project management functions required for effective implementation.

 

Component 5: Contingent Emergency Response Component. This component will provide a mechanism for rapid access to financing following an eligible disaster or emergency event. Funds may be used to support emergency response, recovery and reconstruction activities, and the procurement of critical goods, works, and services required to address the impacts of the event.

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (CONSULTANT QUALIFICATIONS-BASED SELECTION- CQS) SHORTLISTING

 

 

COUNTRY:                       Botswana

 

NAME OF PROJECT:       REGIONAL STATISTICS PROJECT (RSP)

 

PROJECT ID:                     P175731

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:      CONSULTANCY TO HIRE A FIRM FOR UNDERTAKING OF NATIONAL TRAININGS ON PYTHON IN TEN (10) SADC MEMBER STATES

 

REFERENCE NUMBER:       SADC/3/5/2/462

 

DATE OF ISSUE: 10th September 2026

 

 

Background

 

The SADC Secretariat through the SADC Regional Statistics Project has received a grant. The aim of this grant is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC and participating countries to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonization and collaboration.

 

The main guiding frameworks are SADC Vision 20250 and the SADC Regional Indicative Strategic Development Plan 2020-2030 (RISDP 2020-2030). The Regional Infrastructure Development Master Plan (RIDMP), the SADC Regional Agricultural Policy (RAP), the Industrialisation Strategy and the Roadmap, among others, are complementary guiding frameworks for achieving the regional integration agenda. SADC has also developed various Protocols for domestication and implementation by Member States including the most recent one, the Protocol on Statistics, to enhance harmonization of statistics. The operating framework for implementing statistical activities as priorities for the region is the Regional Strategy for Development of Statistics (RSDS) and is aligned to SADC Vision 2050 and RISDP 2020-30.

 

Demand for quality and harmonized statistics has been on the rise to monitor progress in developmental agendas at national, regional, continental, and global level. The scope of data demand cuts across economic, social, and on emerging issues such as climate change, disaster-risk, environment and others related.

 

The SADC Secretariate intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for hiring a FIRM FOR UNDERTAKING OF NATIONAL TRAININGS ON PYTHON IN TEN (10) SADC MEMBER STATES

 

 

The SADC Secretariat invites submissions from suitably qualified and interested firms to conduct the trainings, recruited following World Bank Procurement Regulations dated September 2023.

 

Title             : CONSULTANCY TO HIRE A FIRM FOR UNDERTAKING OF NATIONAL TRAININGS ON PYTHON IN TEN (10) SADC MEMBER STATES

Duration of Assignment:  20 months

The detailed scope of work can be obtained from the terms of reference.

The consulting firm should have significant in-depth expertise and knowledge in Python with experienced master trainers on Python in statistical data processing and analysis, spatial data analysis, big data, quantitative and quantitative data analysis, modelling and data visualization, especially for official statistics. The consultancy firm should also have in depth experience in design and implementation of training materials for official statistics.  Training and capacity building conducted under this assignment must align with the World Bank’s Environmental and Social Framework (ESF) and its applicable Environmental and Social Standards (ESSs), Work under this consultancy is also expected to incorporate gender-sensitive approaches in all project activities and conduct a GBV/SEA/SH risk assessment.

  1. BACKGROUND INFORMATION
    1. Partner country

The Southern African Development Community (SADC).

 

    1. Contract authority

The Contracting Authority is SADC Secretariat, represented by its Executive Secretary.

 

    1. Background

The Southern African Development Community (SADC) is a Regional Economic Community comprising 16 Member States, namely; Angola, Botswana, Comoros, Democratic Republic of Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Seychelles, South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia, Zimbabwe. Established in 1992, SADC is committed to Regional Integration and poverty eradication within Southern Africa through economic development and ensuring peace and security.

 

Article 14 of the SADC Treaty establishes the SADC Secretariat as the principal executive institution of SADC. The Secretariat performs its mandate and functions within the policy, strategic and programme provisions outlined in the Regional Indicative Strategic Development Plan (RISDP) and the Vision 2050. The SADC Vision 2050 earmarks Statistics a priority cross-cutting sector whereby by 2050, the region strategic objective in statistics is to realize a robust and responsive regional statistical system to underpin regional integration processes, including measurement of progress and impact.

 

    1. Current situation in the sector

In the discipline of Official Statistics there is an absolute necessity of evolving towards programming languages oriented to modern data science to face new challenges such as fast prototyping innovative ideas, standardizing production processes and automatizing manual tasks. The implementation of statistical techniques, methods and methodologies can be done with Python functions and scripts in a more efficient way.


The Secretariat is prioritizing statistical capacity building as part of its implementation plan guided by the Regional Strategy for Development of Statistics (RSDS) 2020-30. With the Regional Statistics Project funded by the World Bank, capacity building shall basically come in the form of development of practical guidelines in specific domains; rolling out national and regional training programmes and; assisting Member States through technical assistance. Data management and processing is within the sub-component 1.1 on improving capacity for data production, management and dissemination of the World Bank project.

 

With the growing need of analysing voluminous and complex survey data on a timely basis, open-source statistical softwares play a significant role. Thus, Secretariat is recruiting a consultancy firm which may include but not limited to research centres or universities to train SADC Member States statisticians on Python for beginners and intermediate level.

 

    1. Needs assessment

Member States were also requesting training on Python for official statisticians involved or not in Big Data and Data Science activities having no specific knowledge on the subject.

 

 

  1. OBJECTIVES, PURPOSE AND EXPECTED RESULTS
    1. Overall objective

The overall objective of this exercise is to train Member States on the use of statistical software for management of large database and analysis of complex surveys.

    1. Specific objectives (Purpose)

The specific objective of the assignment is to undertake a national training on Python  for processing of data for official statistics, especially:

  1. to introduce participants to the Python language and ecosystem and to make them able to write basic Python programs for data processing, analysis and visualization; and

 

  1. to provide participants with intermediate level knowledge on Python language and ecosystem and to make them able to write Python programs for official statistics.

 

    1. Results to be achieved by the Consultancy Firm

The Consultancy Firm is expected to achieve the following result:

  1. Python component: Strengthened technical capacity of Statisticians from National Statistics Offices to have a good understanding of Python language and its ecosystem for use for Official Statistics purposes and to be familiar with syntax of Python for reading of a file, processing of data, modelling, aggregation and visualization.

 

  1. SCOPE OF WORK FOR TRAINING ON PYTHON
    1. Scope of work

The selected service provider is expected to deliver in-person technical training workshop on Python to process and analyze official statistics for data producers of official statistics at national level for respective Member State for 10 working days (5 working days for Beginners and 5 working days for intermediate levels)

The training includes theoretical and practical sessions to help participants understand Python syntax and its ecosystem for data management, statistical analysis, tabulations, graphics, and maps from complex census, survey data, and big data. The training report should contain summary of topics covered during training week. Training materials should also be shared to all participants and annexed to be training report

It is expected that the training to be done with real anonymized data obtained from censuses, survey and administrative data undertaken by National Statistics Offices.

 

    1. Geographical area to be covered

The assignment will be carried out in 10 selected Member States of SADC Region, namely (Botswana, Democratic Republic of Congo, Eswatini, Lesotho, Madagascar, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Seychelles, Zimbabwe).

    1. Target groups

This consultancy is expected to target the National Statistics Office and other stakeholders, in particular, statisticians involved in processing and analysis of official statistics, large data and complex surveys.

    1. Specific work

The assignment will be carried out primarily through a national training in five selected Member States of SADC Region.

In particular, the consultant will be required to:

  1. Inception report detailing approach, methods, assumptions, risks, timelines and content of topics covered and training programme
  2. Develop a generic training materials to cater for practical training on Python.
  3. To tailor the programme to the needs of each Member State for intermediate level.
  4. To deliver the training at mutually agreed dates
  5. To give training on application of Python in data processing, management and analysis in survey data and census and other complex data, big data, satellite image data and to cover at least the following topics for beginners’ level:
  • Essentials of Python environment and knowledge about the individual aspects of data processing pipeline (reading file, processing data, saving results, modelling, aggregation, visualization and saving results)
  • Essential syntax of Python; functions, main data structures (tuples, lists, dictionaries)
  • Importing data in Python
  • Creating, manipulating and converting common data structures
  • Merging data from different data sources or different questionnaires
  • Writing functions and using pre-existing functions
  • Introduction to the NumPy library
  • Creation and handling of arrays
  • Packages like Pandas, Matpotlib, Seaborn, Scikit-learn, Geopandas,

 

  1. To give training on application of Python in data processing, management and analysis in survey data and census and other complex data, big data, satellite image data and to cover at least the following topics for intermediate level:

 

  • Performance and differences with respect to Python lists
  • Object-oriented programming
  • Mathematical operations and broadcasting
  • Use of Encapsulation with Python for official statistics and big data
  • Use of Inheritance with Python for official statistics and big data
  • Usage of universal functions (ufuncs)
  • Polymorphism applied to official statistics
  • Python and production of official statistics
  • Sampling and weighting with Python
  • Statistical models with Python
  • Python and processing of big data
  • Python and satellite image/GIS
  • Python and automation/machine learning

 

 

  1. Produce well documented Training Materials to be shared with participants with step-by-step indication for all the topics covered
  2. Produce a Training Report for each Member State with a summary of topics covered during the training and recommendations for implementation
  3. To do a pre- and Post-Training Surveys assessment of participants knowledge and identifying areas of improvement

The experts from the Firm shall assist participants in first handling of Python on the first day of the training for them to use it correctly.

 

    1. Reserve for continuation of contract

The assignment is for training in 10 SADC Member States. The Firm shall be subject to evaluation after each training in a Member State. Continuation of contract is upon satisfactory completion and quality of the previous assignment.

 

    1. Eligible entities

Eligible entities for the current assignment are consultancy firm which may include but not limited to research centres or universities.

  1. QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

This assignment is expected to be carried out by experienced Master Trainers from University, Research Centres and Consultancy Firms and there should be evidence of in-depth knowledge with the open-source softwares (R and Python among others) and trainings at national, regional and international level.  The specific profile of Experts is provided below:

Profiles of Experts

Qualifications and Skills

General Experience

Specific Experience

TWO (2) Expert Trainers

  • A minimum Masters Degree in statistics, economics, IT, Data Science or related field. PhD degree in the above mentioned field shall be an advantage

 

  • Written and oral fluency in the English language is essential. 

 

  • Excellent oral and written communication, analytical, presentation and report writing skills in English Language.

 

  • Excellent time management and organizational skills to prioritize workload and deliver needful during the training week.

 

  • French and Portuguese fluency shall be highly desired for undertaking training in French and Portuguese speaking countries

 

The Expert Trainers Must have at least ten (10) years of experience using Python

  • Demonstrated experience in statistical data processing and analysis, spatial analysis, modelling and data visualization using Python for at least 10 years continuous and for at least 3 surveys for Official Statistics;

 

  •  7 years experience in data analysis and data visualization for both quantitative and qualitative data and Big Data;

 

  • 5 years experience using Python to analyse geospatial data/satellite imagery required;

 

  • Experience in the design and implementation of training materials during at least 3 trainings for the conduct of statistical data analysis training in Official Statistics using Python;

 

  • Extensive experience in as a resource person in delivering at least 5 training on Python at national/regional/international stages, particularly using household and census data.

 

  • Experience in working with  national statistics agencies, and other government institutions

 

 

The expert must be independent and free from conflicts of interest in the responsibilities they take on.

Note that civil servants and other staff of the public administration, of the partner country or of international/regional organizations based in the country, shall only be approved to work as experts if well justified. The justification should be submitted with the tender and shall include information on the added value the expert will bring as well as proof that the expert is seconded or on personal leave. 

 

  1. REPORTING REQUIREMENTS AND TIME SCHEDULED FOR DELIVERABLES
    1. Reporting requirements

The consultant shall operate under the oversight of the Senior Officer – Research & Statistics and direct supervision of Officer – Research and Statistics.

All the deliverables shall be delivered to the Officer – Research and Statistics who shall assess and review the deliverables in line with the requirement of the Term of the References; and approved by the Senior Officer- Research and Statistics.

All reports / training materials shall be in electronic format in MS Word, Excel or PowerPoint format as the case may be. Scripts and commands for Python should be shared with SADC Secretariat and participants. The training materials including power point presentations and Python scripts will be the property of SADC Secretariat and will be used for additional training if required.  The Expert shall work with the Secretariat up to the end of the assignment, shall have delivered the following in electronic format within three (3) months:

Name of report

Content

Time of submission

Inception report

The inception should demonstrate how the training will be organised and its effectiveness towards impactful results. It should have include the objectives,  expected outcome, methods, assumptions, risks, timelines of the training as well as topics to be covered and training programme

 

No later than 7 calendar days after the signing of the contract.

Training reports

For each Member State trained, each  report should cover:

- summary of topics covered during training week;

- pre and post training assessment; and

-  Final Training Materials

No later than 10 calendar days after the completion of the national training workshop for each Member State.

 

 

    1. Submission and approval of report

The reports referred to above must be submitted to the project manager identified in the contract. The reports must be written in English. The project manager is responsible for approving the reports.

    1. Project management

Overall responsibility for supervision of the Consultancy will lie with the Senior Officer – Research and Statistics. The Consultant shall be responsible for the operational day-to-day management and coordination of the consultancy work. 

    1. Management structure

The Consultant shall report to the Senior Officer – Research and Statistics and perform the assigned tasks.

  1. LOGISTICS AND START DATE
    1. Location

The assignment will involve traveling to selected SADC Member States.

    1. Office accommodation

None required

    1. Facilities to be provided by the contracting authority

For the expert working on this consultancy, the Contracting Authority shall facilitate for visa entry in SADC Member States, if required.

    1. Facilities to be provided by the contractor

The contractor must ensure he/she is adequately prepared and equipped for delivery of the training and drafting of deliverables. Moreover, the Firm is expected to be fully self- sufficient in terms of international travel associated expenses, laptop and related device connectivity for projector for this consultancy.

    1. Equipment

No equipment is to be purchased on behalf of the contracting authority / procuring entity as part of this service contract or transferred to the contracting authority / procuring entity at the end of this contract. Any equipment related to this contract that is to be acquired by the procuring entity must be purchased by means of a separate supply tender procedure.

    1. Start date and period of implementation

The intended start date is as soon as both parties have signed the contract agreement and the period of implementation of the contract will be for 20 months from the date of signing the agreement. Please see Article 3 of the specific contract for the actual start date and period of implementation.

  1. MONITORING AND EVALUATION
    1. Definition of indicators

The indicators to be used are timeliness, technical coverage and analytical quality of the Reports as detailed in 5 above. In addition, assessment of the effectiveness of the training to be done using pre and post-test surveys with recipients of the capacity building activity.

    1. Special requirements

The Consultant must declare any potential conflict of interest between the provision of the requested services, and other activities in which, a member of their consortium of group (s), or any expert proposed in their offer is engaged.

 

  1. ASSUMPTIONS AND RISKS
    1. Assumptions underlying the project

It assumed that the consultant would be procured within the reasonable timeframe and activities implemented within 20 months after signature of the contract.

    1. Risks

The nature of the assignment presents negligible risks associated with the consultancy. Some of the risks foreseen are the following:

9.1  Financial proposal

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY CYBERSECURITY LEVEL PROTECTION ASSESSMENT SERVICE AND COMMERCIAL CRYPTOGRAPHY APPLICATION SECURITY EVALUATION SERVICE

for 

China Food Safety Improvement Project Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project

Country: People's Republic of China

Name of Project: China Food Safety Improvement Project

Loan No.: IBRD-92130

Assignment Title: Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project Information Technology Third-Party Service Package II (Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment Service and Commercial Cryptography Application Security Evaluation Service)

Reference No.:  GD-FSS-GAMR-CS13

The Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the China Food Safety Improvement Project Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The total estimated amount for this project is RMB 0.56 million.

(I) Scope of Service

The service scope of this project covers the Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment and Commercial Cryptography Application Security Assessment services required for four informatization projects, specifically including:

  1. The "Scan-to-Trace" Full-Chain Traceability Platform Project for Food in Key Fields (Categories);
  2. The "Yue-Shi-An Internet Plus Open Kitchens" System Construction Project;
  3. The Upgrade, Renovation, and Operation Project of the Emergency Real-Time Dispatch and Command System;
  4. The Capacity Building Project for Food-Related Personnel in Market Regulation.

(II) Service Contents

1. Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment Services

Based on the assessment results of security technology and security management controls, as well as the overall system assessment, the service agency shall conduct a comprehensive assessment of the information system in accordance with the corresponding level standards and provide relevant security review opinions. This specifically includes two aspects: First, security control assessment, which primarily evaluates the implementation and configuration of basic security controls required by the cybersecurity level protection standards within the information system. Second, overall system assessment, which primarily analyzes the overall security of the information system. The security control assessment serves as the foundation for the overall security assessment of the information system.

2. Commercial Cryptography Application Security Assessment Services

The service agency shall provide security assessment services for systems upgraded with domestic cryptography. For the upgraded national cryptographic systems, the agency shall formulate an assessment plan, conduct the assessment, propose rectification opinions, and track the rectification progress in accordance with national specifications, thereby providing a basis for project acceptance. Through this assessment service, the agency will comprehensively understand the current status of cryptography application in the relevant information systems and evaluate the gap between the current status and the corresponding levels stipulated in the Information Security Technology—Basic Requirements for Cryptographic Application of Information Systems (GB/T 39786-2021). This aims to achieve the goals of promoting construction, rectification, and application through assessment. On-site assessments and technical verifications will be conducted covering physical and environmental security, network and communication security, equipment and computing security, application and data security, key management, and security management. The agency will identify weak links and potential risk hazards in cryptographic applications, propose targeted rectification recommendations, and ensure the compliance, correctness, and effectiveness of cryptographic applications. Furthermore, cryptographic security protection measures will be precisely implemented to guarantee the authenticity, confidentiality, integrity, and non-repudiation of the information systems.

(III) Service Period

The service period for this project shall commence from the date of contract signing and continue until the project closing date (March 31, 2029). The specific service timeline will be implemented in phases based on the system launch schedule of the four informatization projects.

Report

Within the past three years, the agency must have independently undertaken no fewer than five service projects for Cybersecurity Level Protection Assessment and Commercial Cryptography Application Security Assessment. I. Background and Description

The World Bank Loan China Food Safety Demonstration Project officially entered into force on March 21, 2024, with an implementation period until March 31, 2029. It aims to comprehensively enhance the modern governance capacity for food safety at both national and local levels. As a key implementer of this project in Guangdong Province, the Guangdong Administration for Market Regulation plans to apply for a World Bank loan of 10 million US dollars and will precisely support the achievement of the project goals through the construction of six core sub-projects:

i. Develop a full-chain traceability platform for "coding, tracing, and recalling" food in key areas, enabling whole-process traceability and risk early warning with 15 functional modules and 359 functional points;

ii. Build the "Internet + Clear Kitchen and Bright Stove" system under the Guangdong Food Safety initiative, covering intelligent video supervision of scenarios such as elderly care and campus canteens;

iii. Upgrade and transform the emergency real-time dispatching and command system, and improve the accident emergency response mechanism;

iv. Carry out a capacity improvement project for food-related personnel in the market supervision field, including the development of a learning and assessment system, the production of 75 course videos, and the organization of skill competitions;

v. Establish a high-quality food standard system and conduct promotion activities, developing no less than 30 standards and carrying out quality monitoring within two years;

vi. Provide professional consulting services throughout the entire project implementation process.

To ensure the high-quality implementation of the above-mentioned construction content, we plan to refer to advanced practices from other World Bank projects to further optimize procurement management and improve service coordination efficiency; in the next phase of actual procurement operations, while keeping the total project budget unchanged, we intend to integrate the network security level protection assessment services and commercial cryptography application security assessment services for these 4 projects—the "Coding, Tracing, and Recalling" Full-Chain Traceability Platform Project for Food in Key Areas (or Key Varieties), the Guangdong Food Safety "Internet + Clear Kitchen and Bright Stove" System Construction Project, the Emergency Real-Time Dispatching and Command System Upgrade, Transformation, and Operation Project, and the Capacity Improvement Project for Food-Related Personnel in the Market Supervision Field—into a single package for unified procurement and management, so as to ensure the smooth achievement of the project's construction goals.

Additionally, the food-related personnel capacity improvement learning and assessment system will enable systematic training for regulatory personnel and quantify the participation proportion of female regulatory personnel.

The core purpose is to conduct a comprehensive and objective security assessment of the above-mentioned information systems in accordance with relevant national standards and norms, accurately identify and locate risks and weaknesses in the systems' network security and cryptographic applications, and propose targeted rectification suggestions accordingly. Pemerintah Republik Indonesia melalui Kementerian Kelautan dan Perikanan telah menerima/telah mengajukan permohonan/berencana mengajukan permohonan pembiayaan dari Bank Dunia untuk membiayai proyek Kemakmuran (INSAN TERANG – LAUTRA, selanjutnya disebut LAUTRA). dan berencana menggunakan sebagian dari dana tersebut untuk jasa konsultasi. 
Layanan konsultasi (“Layanan”) mencakup Konsultan Perorangan Validasi Kerangka Kerja Evaluasi Efektivitas dan Kualitas Penyelenggaraan Penataan Ruang Laut, dengan periode pelaksanaan selama 4 (empat) Bulan, dengan periode pelaksanaan diperkirakan dimulai pada bulan Agustus s.d Desember 2026 
Term of Reference (TOR) terperinci untuk penugasan ini Konsultan Perorangan Validasi Kerangka Kerja Evaluasi Efektivitas dan Kualitas Penyelenggaraan Penataan Ruang Laut sebagaimana terlampir 
Kementerian Kelautan dan Perikanan mengundang konsultan perorangan yang memenuhi syarat (“Konsultan”) untuk menyatakan minatnya dalam menyediakan Jasa tersebut. Konsultan yang berminat diharapkan menyerahkan informasi yang menunjukkan bahwa mereka memiliki kualifikasi yang diperlukan dan pengalaman yang relevan untuk melaksanakan Jasa tersebut (lampirkan curriculum vitae yang memuat deskripsi pengalaman dalam penugasan serupa, kondisi serupa, dan sebagainya, termasuk surat lamaran dan surat referensi). Kriteria kualifikasi adalah sebagai berikut: 
1. Minimal bergelar S3 dalam bidang Manajemen Sumber daya Perairan, Kebijakan Publik, Ilmu Lingkungan, Kelautan, Perencanaan Wilayah, atau bidang sosial lainnya yang relevan. 
2. Memiliki pengalaman minimal 5 tahun dalam melakukan evaluasi kebijakan, penelitian terapan, atau perencanaan strategis, khususnya di sektor kelautan, perikanan, atau tata ruang, atau pekerjaan sejenis.
3. Memahami secara mendalam tentang kebijakan dan regulasi penataan ruang laut di Indonesia. 
4. Memiliki kemampuan analitis yang kuat dalam merumuskan indikator kinerja dan metodologi evaluasi. 
5. Memiliki pengalaman dalam memfasilitasi lokakarya dan berinteraksi dengan multi-pemangku kepentingan.

Para Konsultan yang berminat dihimbau untuk memperhatikan Bagian III, paragraf 3.14, 3.16, dan 3.17 dari Peraturan Pengadaan Bank Dunia untuk Penerima Pinjaman tertanggal September 2023, yang mengatur kebijakan Bank Dunia mengenai konflik kepentingan. 
Informasi lebih lanjut dapat diperoleh di alamat email di bawah ini selama jam kerja (pukul 08.00 hingga 16.00 WIB). 
Pernyataan minat harus disampaikan secara tertulis ke alamat email di bawah ini paling lambat pada 31 Juli 2026 pukul 16.00 WIB.

procnotices.bid_description: Sélection d'un Consultant Individuel, Bibliothécaire de formation, chargé de la création d'un fonds de lecture dédié à la santé sexuelle et reproductive dans les bibliothèques scolaires

procnotices.notice_text:
RÉPUBLIQUE DE CÔTE D’IVOIRE

                                                                                                      Union-Discipline-Travail

                                                                                                            ------------------------

                           MINISTERE DE L’ÉDUCATION NATIONALE, DE L’ALPHABETISATION ET DE L’ENSEIGNEMENT TECHNIQUE

                                                                                                            -------------------

                                                    PROJET DU PROGRAMME DE RENFORCEMENT DU SYSTÈME ÉDUCATIF DE BASE

                                                                                    Volet Financement de Projet d’Investissement (IPF)

                                                            AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊTS N° 023CI/PRSEB-PROJET/IDA-2026

       SELECTION D’UN(E) CONSULTANT(E) INDIVIDUEL(LE) NATIONAL(E), BIBLIOTHÉCAIRE DE FORMATION, CHARGÉ(E) DE LA CRÉATION D’UN FONDS DE LECTURE DÉDIÉ À LA SANTÉ SEXUELLE ET REPRODUCTIVE DANS LES BIBLIOTHÈQUES SCOLAIRES

I.    CONTEXTE ET JUSTIFICATION

Le Gouvernement de Côte d’Ivoire a reçu un financement conjoint de l’Association Internationale pour le Développement (IDA-Banque mondiale) et du Partenariat Mondial pour l’Éducation (GPE) pour la mise en œuvre du Programme de Renforcement du Système Éducatif de Base (PRSEB). Ledit financement s’élève à 425,35 millions de dollars (US$). Ce programme utilise un mécanisme de financement axé sur les résultats concrets, tout en intégrant les réformes des États Généraux de l’Éducation Nationale et de l’Alphabétisation (EGENA) pour créer une école plus juste et inclusive.

Cependant, la santé sexuelle et reproductive (SSR) freine le maintien des filles à l’école, comme en témoignent les 4 266 grossesses scolaires enregistrées en 2024-2025, les mariages précoces et le manque d’informations fiables. Ce déficit est renforcé par les tabous socioculturels et l’absence totale d’ouvrages dédiés dans les bibliothèques scolaires, ce qui pousse les jeunes vers des canaux informels à risque.

Pour y remédier, la Direction de l’Égalité et de l’Équité du Genre (DEEG) du Ministère de l’Éducation Nationale, de l’Alphabétisation et de l’Enseignement Technique (MENAET) souhaite transformer les bibliothèques scolaires existantes en espaces d’information fiables et discrets sur la SSR.

C’est pourquoi, les présents Termes de Référence (TDR) sont produits en vue de sélectionner un(e) consultant(e) individuel(e) national(e), bibliothécaire de formation, pour conduire cette mission dans les établissements secondaires bénéficiaires du Paquet d’Appui Minimum Favorable pour la Rétention des Filles au Collège.

II. OBJECTIF GÉNÉRAL DE LA MISSION

L’objet général de la mission est de fournir au MENAET un catalogue de ressources documentaire, un fonds de lecture fonctionnel consacré à la santé sexuelle et reproductive dans le respect des normes de bibliothéconomie et des orientations nationales en matière d’éducation et de santé.

III. OBJECTIFS SPÉCIFIQUES DE LA MISSION

De manière plus spécifique, le ou la consultant(e) individuel(le) aura pour mission de :

  • établir un diagnostic de la disponibilité des ressources documentaires sur la SSR dans les bibliothèques scolaires ciblées ;
  • recenser et cataloguer les ressources documentaires existantes sur la SSR, en leur appliquant un système de classification exploitable par les gestionnaires de bibliothèque ;
  • sélectionner, sur la base de critères scientifiques, pédagogiques, culturels et financiers, les ouvrages et supports à intégrer au fonds de lecture ;
  • élaborer à l’attention du personnel chargé de l’animation de la bibliothèque dans les établissements ciblées, un guide très simplifié de gestion du fonds (classement, prêt, conservation) ;
  • élaborer des messages pour sensibiliser la communauté éducative pour garantir l’utilisation effective et durable du fonds documentaire.

IV. RÉSULTATS ATTENDUS DE LA MISSION

Au terme de la mission, les résultats suivants sont attendus :

  • un diagnostic de la disponibilité des ressources documentaires sur la SSR dans les bibliothèques scolaires des établissements bénéficiaires est réalisé ;
  • un répertoire catalogué des ressources documentaires existantes sur la SSR (ouvrages, guides, bandes dessinées, supports numériques) est élaboré, classé selon un système de classification adapté ;
  • une liste nationale des ouvrages et supports prioritaires à acquérir est validée, avec spécifications techniques et quantités par établissement ;
  • un guide simplifié pratique de gestion du fonds documentaire est disponible ;
  • une banque de messages pour sensibiliser les communautés éducatives est sensibilisés et outillés pour assurer l’appropriation et la pérennité du dispositif.

V.    LIVRABLES

Le (la) consultant(e), choisi(e), produira les livrables suivants :

  • Livrable(s) 01 : rapport de démarrage présentant la méthodologie, les outils de diagnostic et le chronogramme.
  • Livrable(s) 02 : rapport de diagnostic technique des bibliothèques scolaires, établissement par établissement, validé par la DEEG.
  • Livrable(s) 03 : répertoire catalogué et classé des ressources documentaires existantes ; grille et rapport d’évaluation.
  • Livrable(s) 04 : liste nationale validée des ouvrages et supports à acquérir, par établissement.
  • Livrable(s) 05 : guide pratique de gestion et de pérennisation du fonds documentaire ; note de sensibilisation des communautés éducatives.
  • Livrable(s) 06 : compte rendu de l’atelier ; versions validées du répertoire catalogué, de la liste nationale et du guide de gestion.
  • Livrable(s) 07 : rapport final de la consultance.

VI.   PROFIL DU/DE LA CONSULTANT(E) INDIVIDUEL(LE) 

Le profil recherché est celui d’un(e) bibliothécaire confirmé(e). Le ou la consultant(e) doit respecter les critères ci-dessous :

  • être titulaire d’un diplôme de niveau Bac+3 minimum (Master ou équivalent) en bibliothéconomie, sciences de l’information et de la documentation critère éliminatoire) ;
  • justifier d’une expérience générale d’au moins dix (10) années ;
  • justifier d’au moins sept (07) années d’expérience professionnelle en gestion de bibliothèque, centre de documentation ou service d’archives, décomptées à partir de l’obtention du diplôme requis ;
  • avoir conduit ou participé, au cours des dix (10) dernières années, à au moins trois (03) missions de diagnostic, de catalogage ou de constitution de fonds documentaires, dont le nombre exact doit être précisé et justifié dans le CV ;
  • justifier d’au moins deux (02) années d’expérience dans le système éducatif ivoirien ou dans un contexte de bibliothèque scolaire comparable en Afrique de l’Ouest.
  • avoir réalisé au moins une (01) mission portant sur des ressources documentaires en santé, éducation à la vie familiale ou santé sexuelle et reproductive.

VII. DURÉE DE LA MISSION ET CALENDRIER

La mission est prévue pour une durée de trente (30) jours étalés sur soixante-dix (70) jours.

VIII. PROCÉDURE POUR LA SOUMISSION DES MANIFESTATIONS D’INTÉRÊTS

Le ou la consultant(e) sera choisi(e) conformément au Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’investissement (FPI), édition de septembre 2025 et relatif à l’acquisition de Fournitures, Travaux, Services Autres que des Services de Consultants et Services de Consultants.

La Sélection du Consultant Individuel sera fondée sur les qualifications et l’expérience du Consultant en rapport avec la mission. Le Consultant individuel sera sélectionné parmi ceux ayant répondu à l’AMI.

Le dossier de soumission devra être composé de :

  • Une lettre de manifestation d’intérêts dûment signée ;
  • Un Curriculum Vitae détaillé indiquant clairement les qualifications et expériences similaires ou pertinentes ;
  • Une copie des diplômes mentionnés dans le Curriculum Vitae (CV) ;
  • Une copie de(s) certificat(s) ou attestation(s) de travail ou une attestation d’exécution d’études ou missions similaires qui justifient des expériences et qualifications figurant dans le Curriculum Vitae (CV).

Les manifestations d’intérêt comportant des informations de nature financière seront rejetées.

La date limite pour le dépôt des manifestations d’intérêts est prévue pour le 23 septembre 2026 à 11 heures précises. L’enveloppe du Consultant Individuel devra porter la mention « AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTÉRÊTS N° 023CI/PRSEB-PROJET/IDA-2026 – SELECTION D’UN(E) CONSULTANT(E) INDIVIDUEL(LE) NATIONAL(E), BIBLIOTHÉCAIRE DE FORMATION, CHARGÉ(E) DE LA CRÉATION D’UN FONDS DE LECTURE DÉDIÉ À LA SANTÉ SEXUELLE ET REPRODUCTIVE DANS LES BIBLIOTHÈQUES SCOLAIRES »

Les manifestations d’intérêts devront être soumises en français et en cinq (05) exemplaires don’t un (1) original et quatre (04) copies (le tout dans une grande et même enveloppe) et déposées sous plis fermé à l’adresse ci-dessous ou transmis par DHL, CHRONOPOSTE, FEDEX, etc.

Les soumissions par voie électronique ne seront pas acceptées.

Les manifestations d’intérêts seront ouvertes en présence du Comité d’évaluation et des représentants des soumissionnaires présents, à l’adresse mentionnée ci-dessous le même jour le 23 septembre 2026 à 11 heures 30 minutes.

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (REOI)

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Country: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia

Name of Project: Health Emergency Preparedness, Response, and Resilience (HEPRR) MPA Project (P180127)

Loan No /Credit No./Grant No.: IDA-E2290

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the assessment of Ethiopia Digital Health regulatory framework for EFDA

Reference No. ET-MOH-526428-CS-QCBS

The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received financing from the World Bank towards the cost of the Health Emergency Preparedness, Response, and Resilience (HEPRR) MPA Project (P180127) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for Consulting Services. The consulting services (“the Services”) include to provide EFDA with a comprehensive, evidence-based analysis of its current digitalization maturity and to develop a detailed, phased, and cost-implementable strategic roadmap directly supporting the strategic goals of Digital Ethiopia 2030. In addition, the service includes a detailed evaluation of EFDA’s digital ecosystem across its Head Office, branch offices, entry and exit ports, and operations in 12 regions and two city administrations.

To achieve the overall objective, the consultancy will fulfil the following specific aims:

  • To conduct a thorough evaluation of all existing IT systems and infrastructure e.g., eRIS, IFMIS, eGP, ICSMI, etc; assessing their technical performance, operational effectiveness, user adoption levels, scalability, and interoperability.
  •  To assess the adequacy and maturity of existing regulatory digital systems and the prevailing national policy and legal frameworks governing data protection, data sharing, and data security.
  • To review the role, influence, and interplay of other government institutions and national policies/strategies that impact or shape the authority's digitalization exercise.
  • To evaluate the authority's readiness and alignment with data sharing, interoperability, and digitalization requirements arising from regional regulatory harmonization efforts through entities such as IGAD and the African Medicines Agency (AMA).
  • To critically assess the strategic design, readiness, and integration potential of planned system deployments (PMS, medicine track and trace system, AI, eCTD.etc) within the envisioned future-state architecture.
  • To identify, analyses, and priorities gaps, bottlenecks, and risks across four key pillars: (i) Technology and Infrastructure, (ii) Data Governance and Management, (iii) Human Capacity and Organizational Structure, and (iv) Policy and Legal Frameworks.
  • To define a future-state digital architecture blueprint that ensures seamless data flow, system interoperability, robust security, and scalability to meet future regulatory demands.
  • To design the IT infrastructure, system architecture, and blueprint covering hardware, networks, platforms, workflows, interoperability, and data governance to meet current and future regulatory needs for EFDA’s Center of Excellence.
  • To produce a strategic, prioritized, and time-bound digital transformation roadmap for the 10 years, complete with clear phases, key initiatives, milestones, and a governance framework for implementation.
  • To analyze and recommend optimal models for ongoing IT service delivery, maintenance, and support, evaluating the balance between in-house capacity development and strategic outsourcing.
  • To deliver a comprehensive financial analysis, including detailed capital and operational expenditure projections, a compelling cost-benefit analysis, and a clear projection of the anticipated Return on Investment (ROI) for the proposed digital transformation.

The total duration for this comprehensive assignment shall be sixteen (16) weeks from the date of contract signing.

The Terms of Reference (TOR) for the primary procurement stage for the assignment can be obtained at the following link.

https://www.moh.gov.et/ToR_Consultancy_Services_for_DH_EFDA

The Ministry of Health now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. Core business and years in business.
  2. Relevant project experience in executing similar assignments (experience in Africa is an advantage).
  3. Technical and managerial capacity of the firm.

The Qualifications and Experience of Key Experts shall not be included in the shortlisting

  • Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The shortlist will contain Five to Eight shortlisted firms.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” September 2025  (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

In addition, please refer to the following specific information on conflict of interest related to this assignment: as per paragraph 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours at the morning from 09:00 am to 12:30 pm and in the afternoon from 01:30 pm to 05:00 pm at the address stated below.

APPEL A MANIFESTATION D'INTERETS (SERVICES DE CONSULTANTS : SELECTION DE FIRMES/CABINETS)

Pays

: République du Burundi

Nom du Projet 

: Projet d’Urgence sur la Résilience Urbaine (PRU) 

Numéro de Don

: IDA Nº E3520

N° du projet               

: P177146 

Titre de la mission

Termes de référence pour le recrutement d’un cabinet/firme pour l’élaboration des études d’impact environnemental et social ( EIES) des infrastructures à faible regret et audit environnemental et social du mur en gabion et   des travaux d’aménagement et de réhabilitation de la station de pompage d’eau de la Regideso

 

 

N° de référence (selon le Plan de Passation de Marchés dans STEP)

: BI-MIELS-PIU-571282-CS-QCBS

 

Le Gouvernement du Burundi a obtenu un don de 113 millions de dollars de la Banque mondiale pour financer le Projet d’Urgence sur la Résilience Urbaine (PRU, P177146), qui vise à renforcer la résilience face aux inondations et à améliorer la gestion urbaine résiliente au climat à Bujumbura sur cinq ans.

Il est prévu qu’une partie des ressources de cette avance soit utiliser pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat de services suivant : « termes de référence pour le recrutement d’un cabinet/firme pour l’élaboration des études d’impact environnemental et social (EIES) des infrastructures à faible regret et audit environnemental et social du mur en gabion et   des travaux d’aménagement et de réhabilitation de la station de pompage d’eau de la REGIDESO

La mission a pour objectif global l’élaboration des Etudes d’Impacts Environnementaux et Sociaux détaillées des infrastructures à faible regret dans les six (6) bassins versants du Projet d’Urgence sur la Résilience Urbaine à savoir Kanyosha-Kizingwe, Mugere, Mutimbuzi, Muha, Ntahangwa et Rusizi. Les objectifs spécifiques de la mission sont les suivants :

  • Évaluer les risques environnementaux et sociaux liés aux infrastructures à faibles regret ;
  • Proposer les mesures d’adaptation pour les infrastructures à faible regret ;
  • Déterminer les coûts des mesures nécessaires pour prévenir, minimiser, atténuer ou compenser les nuisances et optimiser les impacts positifs.

 Pour le volet l’Audit La présente évaluation poursuit un double objectif. D'une part, elle vise à examiner de manière rétrospective la mise en œuvre des activités déjà réalisées dans le cadre du sous-projet, afin de vérifier leur conformité avec le Code de l'Environnement du Burundi ainsi qu'avec les Normes Environnementales et Sociales (NES) de la Banque mondiale applicables (voir Section V infra). D'autre part, elle a pour objet d'évaluer de manière prospective les impacts environnementaux et sociaux des nouveaux travaux prévus sur le site, et de proposer les mesures d'atténuation et de suivi nécessaires pour en assurer la durabilité.

Les compétences recherchées et qui constituent les critères de présélection sont les suivantes :

  • Avoir huit (8) ans d’expérience avérée dans les prestations analogues à la mission actuelle
  • Avoir mené, en tant que firme, au moins trois (03) consultances d'importance similaire et élaboré des documents similaires approuvés préférentiellement par la Banque mondiale

N.B : Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués à ce stade.

Les Consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour renforcer leurs qualifications, mais doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’une coentreprise et/ou d’une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d’une coentreprise, tous les partenaires de la coentreprise seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de l’ensemble du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés.

Le bureau d'études sera sélectionné selon la méthode de Sélection fondée qualité le coût (SFQC) conformément au Règlement applicable aux Emprunteurs-Passation des Marchés dans le cadre de Financement de Projets d’Investissement de la Banque Mondiale et conformément aux critères exigés au regard des termes de référence.

De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l'adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau : Lundi à jeudi de 08h00 à 12h00 et de 13h00 à 17h00 et vendredi de 8h à 12h.

Les manifestations d'intérêt rédigées en français portant la mention « Termes de référence pour le recrutement d’un cabinet/firme pour l’élaboration des études d’impact environnemental et social ( EIES) des infrastructures à faible regret et audit environnemental et social du mur en gabion et   des travaux d’aménagement et de réhabilitation de la station de pompage d’eau de la Reguides doivent être transmises par écrit à l'adresse ci-dessous (en personne, par la poste ou par courriel) au plus tard le 28/09/2026 à 10 heures, heure de Bujumbura (GMT+2)

À l’attention de : Monsieur le Coordonnateur du PRT & PRU Bujumbura, 101 Avenue MUMIRWA, Quartier ZeimetE-mail : info@prt.bi  avec copie à rmpawenayo@prt.bi, mpawenayoregis@yahoo.fr et tbahori@pru.bi, theodorebahori71@gmail.com

Pour publication

Dr. Ir. Régis MPAWENAYO

COORDONNATEUR DE L’UGP-PRT & PRU
