      5. Os empreiteiros podem apresentar propostas para um ou mais lotes. Um contrato será assinado para cada lote. Dada a dispersão dos lotes, a adjudicação de dois (2) lotes ao mesmo proponente (empreiteiro) poderá ser admitida, desde que           este demonstra a capacidade técnica e financeira para assegurar a execução simultânea dos lotes, nos prazos e condições estabelecidos no Documento do Concurso. Date of publication:    09-09-2026

Deadline for applications:    23-09-2026

 

As part of the implementation of the Primary Health Care Quality Improvement Operation (PHCQIO) Additional Financing Project, financed by the World Bank, the Ministry of Health of the Kyrgyz Republic announces a competition for the following vacant position:

 

Contract Management consultant

Qualification Requirements:

  • Higher education in law, economics, management, procurement, or related disciplines (copy of diploma to be attached);
  • At least 3 years of professional experience in contract administration/procurement, including work with international contracts (goods/works/consulting);
  • Knowledge of the legal and regulatory framework on public procurement of the Kyrgyz Republic, World Bank Procurement Regulations, standard contract forms/conditions, experience with STEP, basic knowledge of civil/budget law of the Kyrgyz Republic, PIM/POM rules (for clearances and reporting); skills in the contract cycle: drafting ToR/specifications, participation in evaluation, negotiations and contract signing; administration (guarantees, advances, insurance), amendments/addenda, claims management, contract closure;
  • Knowledge and skills in verification of acts/IPC, payment schedules and retentions, control of deadlines and penalties, reconciliation with the procurement plan/budget, and functionality of the Public Procurement Portal;
  • Fluency in Kyrgyz and Russian is mandatory; working knowledge of English is an advantage;
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) is mandatory.

 

Interested candidates are invited to send their CV, indicating their contact telephone number and position in English and Russian, letters of recommendation from their place of work, copies of relevant diplomas and certificates, as well as the contact details of at least two referees for verification of references, by 18:00 on September 23, 2026, by email: puimzkr@gmail.com; saltanat1281@mail.ru; a_turgunalieva@mz.med.kg; or by mail to Kyrgyzstan, Bishkek, Togolok-Moldo 1a St, 1nd floor, No. 12. Documents must be submitted in PDF format, and resumes must be signed.

Applications without the job title, containing an incomplete set of documents, or received after the deadline will not be considered.

Country: Republic of Mozambique

Name of Project:  Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER SOP2)

Grant number:    IDA-E4810

Job title: Preparation of the Procedures Manual of the Project Portfolio Coordination Unit

Reference Number: MZ-MTL-558090-CS-INDV

The Government of Mozambique, represented by the Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL), has received funding from the World Bank for the Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER SOP2) project and intends to apply part of the resources to consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") involve development of a Portfolio Procedures Manual (PM) for Management of projects financed by the World Bank, and implemented by the Portfolio Coordination Unit (PMU, PIUs and TACF), which systematically documents the policies, procedures and operational practices to be followed in implementation, monitoring, financial management, procurement, socio-environmental safeguards, execution of works, quality control, communication and involvement of stakeholders, as well as reporting and/or accountability to the ministerial tutelage and the financier.

The PM shall also establish standardized procedures and workflows aimed at improving coordination across the portfolio, strengthening implementation efficiency, accelerating decision-making and project execution, reducing administrative bottlenecks, and promoting the cost-effective use of resources. In this regard, the Manual shall include procedures and arrangements that facilitate resource optimization, economies of scale, streamlined business processes, and effective portfolio oversight while ensuring full compliance with Government regulations and World Bank requirements. In addition, the PM should also review and update the indicators and criteria for evaluating the performance of the PMU and PIUs. The duration of the assignment is estimated to be four (4) months.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be obtained from the address provided below.

The Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL) now invites qualified individuals ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing the Services. Expressions of interest must include the following: (i) a CV detailing qualifications, work experience and achievements in comparable work and (ii) a cover letter, specifically addressing how the applicant fulfills each of the mandatory selection criteria. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn  to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Rules for IPF Borrowers of September 2025 ("the Rules"), which sets forth the Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

 

FEDERAL DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF ETHIOPIA

ADELE PROJECT (P171742)

 

Credit No.: IDA 68570

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for the Design and Establishment of a Wholesale (Apex) Development Finance Framework

Reference No. ET-DBE-571276-CS-QCBS

  1. The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia has received World Bank financing for the Access to Distributed Electricity and Lighting in Ethiopia (ADELE) Project. It intends to apply part of the proceeds to consulting services.

The Development Bank of Ethiopia (DBE) is one of the state-owned financial institutions providing project finance and lease financing for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to support the country's overall economic development. In addition to financing projects, the bank serves as a financial intermediary that administers funds and appraises and monitors participating financial institutions through its wholesale financing program, ensuring successful project implementation.

2. DBE invites expressions of interest (EOIs) from legally formed consulting firms to provide consultancy services for the Design and Establishment of a Wholesale (Apex) Development Finance Framework.

3. The consulting services (“the Services”) comprise technical assistance to the Development Bank of Ethiopia (DBE) to design, document, and prepare for implementation a wholesale (apex) development finance capability as an institutional pillar of the Bank. The services include the design of a wholesale banking framework covering the lending model and the intermediary engagement model; an assessment of the institutional, legal, and delivery structure options for housing the wholesale function; the development of a Wholesale Lending Policy and Operational Manual and of a credit guarantee and de-risking framework grounded in an explicit additionality framework; the design of a technical advisory and capacity-building program for participating financial institutions, including a dedicated module on expanding outreach to women entrepreneurs and women consumers; the integration of environmental and social risk management into intermediary accreditation and supervision; and support to DBE in preparing pilot wholesale arrangements and the associated portfolio segregation and ring-fencing arrangements. The assignment is financed under Sub-component 5.3 of the project. The implementation period is approximately twenty (20) weeks from contract signature, with the consultant based primarily in Addis Ababa for the core design and approval phases.

4. The Development Bank of Ethiopia now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested consultants should provide information demonstrating the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the services. The shortlisting criteria are:

       4.1. Relevant experience of the firm

Assignments count only if completed within the last ten (10) years and only where the consultant acted as lead firm or joint venture member – sub-consultancy roles do not count. A single assignment may satisfy more than one of the requirements listed below.

  • At least three (3) completed assignments involving the design of wholesale or apex lending frameworks, on-lending or refinancing facilities, blended-finance or credit-guarantee structures, or DFI institutional design.
  • Of these, at least one (1) was carried out for a development finance institution, state-owned development bank or apex financial institution.
  • At least one (1) assignment involving the design or operationalization of a credit guarantee, first-loss, risk-sharing or partial credit guarantee instrument, including its pricing, eligibility and claims arrangements.
  • At least one (1) assignment on a World Bank or other multilateral-financed line of credit, apex facility or financial intermediary lending operation.
  • At least two (2) assignments delivered in Sub-Saharan Africa or comparable frontier and emerging markets. For this purpose, a country is a comparable frontier or emerging market if, as at the date of the EOI submission deadline, it is (a) eligible for IDA financing (including blend countries), (b) classified by the World Bank as a low-income or lower-middle-income economy, or (c) a constituent of the MSCI Frontier Markets Index. Consultants must state, for each assignment relied upon, the country and the limb (a), (b) or (c) relied upon.

 

Assignments consisting solely of the following do not count under this sub-section 4.1: general management or organizational consulting; audit, tax or accounting services; IT or core-banking system implementation; training delivery without design content; market or feasibility studies without design of a lending framework or instrument; retail or corporate lending work with no financial-intermediary component.

       4.2. Technical and Managerial Capability of the Firm

  • The consultant demonstrates in-house coverage of the following disciplines through named permanent professional staff: development finance/apex lending; credit risk; financial modeling; institutional or organizational design; inclusive/gender-responsive finance. An organogram and headcount by discipline are required. There is no minimum total headcount; the in-country mobilization requirement set out below tests capacity to deliver at the scale of this assignment.
  • The Consultant has a documented quality assurance and project management system (ISO 9001 certification or an equivalent internal QA manual, described in no more than one page).
  • The Consultant has completed at least one (1) assignment in the last seven (7) years in which it mobilized and sustained a team of five (5) or more international and national experts in-country for a period of four (4) months or more, demonstrating capacity to deploy in Addis Ababa for an engagement of approximately 20 weeks. Evidence: client name and contact, assignment dates, team size and composition, and country of deployment.

      4.3. Core Business and Organizational Experience

  • The Consultant is a legally registered firm and has at least ten (10) years of organizational experience in development finance, financial sector development or financial institution advisory. Evidence: certificate of incorporation or registration, together with the experience record submitted under the following bullet.
  • Development finance, financial sector development, or financial institution advisory is a core business line of the Consultant, evidenced by at least five (5) completed consulting assignments in this field in the last ten (10) years.

5. The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016, revised November 2017, August 2018, November 2020 and September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. In addition, the following specific information on conflict of interest applies to this assignment: a firm that DBE has engaged to prepare or implement activities that would place it in conflict with the obligations of this assignment, or that would confer an unfair advantage, is not eligible. Consultants shall disclose any current or prior advisory or contractual relationship with DBE within the last five (5) years.

6. The selection process will be conducted using Quality and Cost Based Method of Selection (QCBS) as laid out in the World Bank Procurement Regulation.

7. The consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected. Where the consultant is a joint venture, the core business requirement in sub-section 4.3 and at least two (2) of the three (3) assignments required under the first bullet of sub-section 4.1 shall be met by the lead member alone; the remaining requirements may be met by the members combined; and each member individually shall be eligible under Section III of the Procurement Regulations and shall not be subject to World Bank suspension or debarment. A joint venture shall submit a joint venture agreement or a letter of intent signed by all members, identifying the lead member. The qualifications, experience, and resources of sub-consultants are not taken into account in shortlisting.

8. Consultants/Applicants shall submit the required documents for the EOI consideration, including the business registration certificate, renewed trade license, VAT registration certificate (for local consulting firm only), and tax clearance certificate (for local consulting firm only). The EOI must not exceed twenty (20) pages, excluding the cover letter, registration certificate, and financial statements.

9. Interested applicants may obtain further information and clarification from DBE Head Office, Procurement Directorate, in front of DBE head office (Kiyamed Building, 1st floor), Tel. +251 11 5578088, ext. 364; Fax +251 11 553 7982 or via email attention to Mr. Kirubel Girma, Procurement Director, kirubelg@dbe.com.et and copy to tesfahunge@dbe.com.et

10. The Expression of Interest/ EoIs shall be submitted in English, one original and one copy, EoIs shall be submitted into the tender box prepared for the purpose on or before September 22, 2026 at 4:00 P.M (in the afternoon) at the Development Bank of Ethiopia, in front of DBE head office (Kiyamed Building 1st floor) or via email to Mr. Kirubel Girma, Procurement Director, kirubelg@dbe.com.et

DBE reserves the right to accept or reject a part/all of the entire bid.

PROJET DE DÉVELOPPEMENT DES CHAINES DE VALEURS VIVRIÈRES EN CÔTE D’IVOIRE – PDC2V

 

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERETS

------------------------------

N° 02/IDA/PDC2V/2026

------------------------------

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT/FIRME POUR LA RÉALISATION D’UNE MISSION DE SUIVI ET CONTROLE DES TRAVAUX DE REHABILITATION DES STATIONS D'ALEVINAGE DE ABENGOUROU ET MOPOYEM

 

REPUBLIQUE DE CÔTE D’IVOIRE

 

PROJET DE DEVELOPPEMENT DES CHAINES DE VALEURS VIVRIERS

 

Numéro de Crédit : 69080

 

Intitulé de la Mission : Recrutement d’un consultant/firme pour la réalisation d’une mission de suivi et contrôle des travaux de réhabilitation des stations d'alevinage de Abengourou et Mopoyem.

 

N° de référence STEP : CI-PDC2V-558241-CS-CQS

 

1. La République de Côte d’Ivoire a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet de Développement des Chaînes de Valeurs Vivrières (PDC2V) et a l’intention d’affecter une partie du produit à des services de consultant.

 

2. Les services de consultant (« les Services ») consisteront à assister l’unité de coordination du projet dans le suivi et contrôle des travaux de réhabilitation des stations d'alevinage de Abengourou et Mopoyem.

 

3. La mission se déroulera sur une durée maximale de huit (08) mois calendaires à compter de la réception de l’ordre de service de démarrage.

 

4. Les Termes De Référence (TDR) détaillés de la mission peuvent être téléchargés gratuitement via le lien suivant : www.pdc2v.ci ou à la demande à l’adresse : edwige.solou@pdc2v.ci avec copie à maurel.zede@pdc2v.ci.  Les adresses électroniques fournies seront utilisées pour toute communication ultérieures (clarification etc.).

 

5. Le Projet de Développement des Chaînes de Valeurs Vivrières invite dès à présent les consultants Firmes admissibles (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Firmes intéressées doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services.

 

6. Compétences et qualifications du consultant firme :

 

Le Consultant recherché est une firme ou un groupement de Cabinets exerçant dans le domaine du génie civil et ayant réalisé en maitrise d’œuvre de suivi et contrôle au cours des dix (10) dernières années, au moins un ou plusieurs projets de réhabilitation ou construction de bâtiments ERP (Etablissement Recevant des Travailleurs) et aménagement hydro piscicole/ agricole d’un montant de travaux minimum de 25 000 000 FCFA par mission.

Les expériences similaires doivent être respectivement justifiées par des attestations de bonne exécution (ABE) délivrées par les Maitres d’Ouvrage.

 

La firme devra disposer des experts suivants :

Désignation

Expérience spécifique

•              Deux (02) Ingénieurs en Bâtiment, Chef de mission

Ingénieur de Conception en Bâtiment ou Génie Civil de niveau minimum (BAC +5) ou tout autre diplôme équivalent

Au moins sept (7) ans d’expérience en étude, exécution ou contrôle de travaux bâtiments ou de génie civil

Avoir réalisé au moins trois (03) missions de maitrise d’œuvre de travaux de bâtiment recevant du public ERP

Deux (02) Ingénieurs en Génie Rural ou Aménagement Hydro-piscicole

Au moins cinq (5) ans d’expérience en étude, exécution ou contrôle de travaux d’aménagements Hydro-piscicole

Avoir réalisé au moins trois (03) missions de maitrise d’œuvre de travaux d’aménagement Hydro-piscicole

Deux (02) Ingénieurs en Equipements Techniques

Ingénieur de conception en Electrotechnique ou Electromécanique ou Automatisme (BAC+05) ou tout autre niveau équivalent

Au moins cinq (05) ans en étude ou contrôle dans la conception, l’exécution et la maintenance de systèmes électroniques, électriques mais aussi de systèmes mécaniques.

Avoir réalisé au moins trois (03) missions de maitrise d’œuvre ou de contrôle technique des systèmes électrotechniques dédiés aux installations hydro piscicoles dont l’électricité, de plomberie et de climatisation des bâtiments ou des laboratoires

Deux (02) Environnementalistes ou spécialistes en HSE

Maitrise en Sciences de l’Environnement ou équivalent de formation scientifique ou technique (BAC + 4 minimum).

Au moins trois (3) ans d'expériences professionnelles acquises dans la conduite d’activités en rapport avec les questions environnementales, sociales et/ou SSHE (Santé, Sécurité Hygiène Environnement).

Avoir déjà réalisé le suivi environnemental et social d’au moins quatre 4) projets distincts de réhabilitation ou construction d’infrastructures dans le domaine du génie civil.

Deux (02) Surveillants de travaux

Technicien supérieur

Technicien supérieur en Bâtiment (DTS, DUT ou BTS au moins BAC +2)

Au moins cinq (5) ans d'expériences professionnelles acquises dans le domaine du bâtiment ou du génie civil.

Avoir déjà participé à la réalisation de travaux et/ou au contrôle/supervision de travaux portant sur deux (02) projets de construction de bâtiments ERP.

 

7. Pièces constitutives du dossier de manifestation d’intérêts

Les candidats éligibles et intéressés sont invités à soumettre un dossier de manifestation d’intérêts comportant les informations pertinentes indiquant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour exécuter la mission. Ce dossier doit contenir les informations suivantes :

  • Une lettre de manifestation d’intérêt signée par le soumissionnaire ou le groupement de soumissionnaires ; 
  • Une copie du Registre de Commerce et de Crédit Mobilier (RCCM) ou tout autre document équivalent pour les entreprises étrangères ;
  •  Une copie de l’accord de groupement ou celle de la lettre d’intention de regroupement, si le Candidat est constitué en groupement ; 
  • Une attestation de non-faillite pour les entreprises étrangères datant de moins de 6 mois à la date limite de dépôt des offres ; 
  • La présentation du candidat (son existence légale, organigramme, personnel) ; 
  • Les références pertinentes relatives à l’exécution de missions similaires (fiche projets)

Toute expérience non justifiée par une Attestation de Bonne Exécution (ABE) pour la structure ne sera pas prise en compte. Les ABE rédigées dans une langue étrangère doivent être accompagnées d’une traduction en langue française, auquel cas elles ne seront pas prises en compte.

NB : « Ne sont admis à participer à la procédure de passation du marché public que les candidats à jour de leurs cotisations fiscales et sociales ainsi que de la redevance de régulation. Le quitus de non-redevance délivré par l’ARCOP, l’attestation de régularité fiscale et l’attestation de régularité sociale seront exigés de l’attributaire du marché avant la signature du contrat ».

 

Le Consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la Sélection Fondée sur Qualifications du Consultant (SQC) telle que décrite dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant de la Banque mondiale le financement de projets d’investissement (FPI) de juillet 2016 mis à jour en septembre 2025.

 

8. Des informations supplémentaires peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau :

 

Unité de Coordination du Projet des Chaînes de Valeurs Vivrières (UC-PDC2V), Abidjan Cocody, Rue de la Cannebière, Non loin de l’ambassade d’Italie de 8 heures à 12 heures et de 14 heures à 17 heures, Temps Universel.

 

9. Invitation for Bids for Non-Consulting Services for Organizing a Series of One Health Science Popularization and Publicity Activities under the World Bank Loan Project for Prevention, Preparedness and Response to Emerging Infectious Diseases – Hainan Province Project (Global “One Health” Hainan Demonstration Project) (Contract No. HN-NS-14)

1The Government of the People’s Republic of China has received a loan from the World Bank toward the cost of the World Bank Loan Project for Prevention, Preparedness and Response to Emerging Infectious Diseases – Hainan Province Project (Global “One Health” Hainan Demonstration Project) and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan to eligible payments under the contract for Non-Consulting Services for Organizing a Series of One Health Science Popularization and Publicity Activities (Contract No. HN-NS-14).

2China International Tendering Co., Ltd. (the Procurement Agent), on behalf of Hainan University (the Purchaser), now invites eligible and qualified Bidders to submit sealed bids for the following non-consulting services:

Contract No.

HN-NS-14

Contract Title

Non-Consulting Services for Organizing a Series of One Health Science Popularization and Publicity Activities

Number of Contract Packages

One

Delivery Period

From the date of contract signing until the World Bank loan closing date of December 31, 2027

3This procurement will be conducted through National Competitive Procurement using the Request for Bids (RFB) method in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (the “Procurement Regulations”). Eligible Bidders meeting the requirements set forth in the Procurement Regulations are eligible to participate.

4Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from the address specified in this Invitation for Bids and inspect or purchase the Bidding Documents from August 13, 2026 until the bid submission deadline of September 14, 2026, during the following hours on working days (excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and statutory public holidays): 9:00–11:30 a.m. and 1:30–5:00 p.m. (Beijing Time).

5Prospective Bidders should note the provisions of Clause 4 of the Instructions to Bidders concerning eligibility and conflicts of interest. Any Bidder found to have a conflict of interest shall be ineligible.

6The qualification requirements for Bidders include:

Single Bid Submission

Bidders shall meet the following requirements:

(a) Be an independent legal entity, holding a valid business license, registration certificate of a social organization as a legal person, or other legally valid business registration certificate; be capable of independently assuming civil liability; have a valid and ongoing business status; and not be included in the list of enterprises with abnormal business operations or the list of seriously illegal and dishonest entities by the market regulatory authorities;

(b) Have a good commercial reputation and a sound financial and accounting system;

(f) Meet other conditions stipulated by laws and administrative regulations.

Joint Venture

Information required for submission of Bids by a Joint Venture (JV):

The maximum number of members in the Joint Venture (JV) shall be 2. Each member of the JV shall meet the following requirements:

(a) Be an independent legal entity, holding a valid business license, registration certificate of a social organization as a legal person, or other legally valid business registration certificate; be capable of independently assuming civil liability; have a valid and ongoing business status; and not be included in the list of enterprises with abnormal business operations or the list of seriously illegal and dishonest entities by the market regulatory authorities;

(b) Have a good commercial reputation and a sound financial and accounting system;

(c) Have the equipment and professional technical capabilities necessary for the performance of the Contract;

(d) Have a good record of paying taxes and social security contributions in accordance with the law;

(e) Have no record of major violations of laws or regulations or material breaches of contract in business activities during the three years preceding participation in government procurement activities; have a good social reputation; and have not been subject to any administrative penalty imposed by an administrative authority at or above the county level for violations of laws or regulations;

(f) Meet other conditions stipulated by laws and administrative regulations.

Each JV member shall provide the corresponding supporting documents or a Letter of Commitment (in a self-prepared format) to demonstrate compliance with the above requirements.

Average Annual TurnoverThe minimum average annual turnover for the years 2023 to 2025 shall be no less than RMB 500,000. (In the case of a Joint Venture, each member of the Joint Venture shall meet this requirement.)
Contract Experience

Contract Experience

(1) During the past three years (i.e., from January 1, 2023 to the Bid submission deadline), the Bidder shall have successfully completed at least one case involving the organization and selection of university students. The Bidder shall provide relevant supporting or evidentiary materials meeting the requirements, including any one of the following: screenshots of media reports at the university level or above, photographs of the project implementation site, a list of recruited personnel, or a performance certificate issued by the project owner.

(2) During the past three years (i.e., from January 1, 2023 to the Bid submission deadline), the Bidder shall have completed at least one project involving the organization and planning of a public science popularization or campus cultural activity. The Bidder shall provide a copy of the key pages of the relevant contract. The contract copy included in the Bid shall contain, at a minimum, pages clearly showing the following: the cover page indicating the project name, service scope, contract signing date, contract amount, and the signature and seal page.

(3) During the past three years (i.e., from January 1, 2023 to the Bid submission deadline), the Bidder shall have completed at least one set of science popularization and publicity materials. The Bidder shall provide at least one self-created bilingual (Chinese-English) science popularization and publicity material, including the complete bilingual science popularization content and the corresponding layout/design draft. In addition, the Bidder shall provide any one traceability document, such as the relevant page of the delivery contract, project acceptance certificate, or acknowledgment of deliverables issued by the Client. Such document shall clearly indicate the project name, service scope, date of issuance, and the Bidder’s entity information.

(4) During the past three years (i.e., from January 1, 2023 to the Bid submission deadline), the Bidder shall have at least one completed and implemented science popularization visual product. The Bidder shall provide one or more of the following: a science popularization leaflet, poster, brochure, or completed script for a science popularization short video, together with supporting acceptance and delivery documentation for the implemented visual product, such as the relevant page of the delivery contract, project acceptance certificate, or acknowledgment of deliverables issued by the Client.

(For a Joint Venture, the requirements above may be met collectively by all JV members.)

Key Personnel

The Bidder shall provide the relevant supporting documents in its Bid in accordance with the Key Personnel requirements specified below. The Bidder shall provide curriculum vitae (CVs) of the relevant Key Personnel (in a self-prepared format) in its Bid. For the experience required below, the Bidder shall provide copies of the key pages of the relevant contracts, including the contract cover page showing the project name, the name of the personnel, the scope of services, the contract signing date, and the signature and seal page, or other supporting documents demonstrating the relevant work experience (such as a certificate issued by the Client or a Letter of Commitment issued by the Bidder), duly affixed with the Bidder’s official seal.

In addition, the Project Manager shall provide a copy of his/her graduation certificate and a copy of his/her degree certificate or other supporting document evidencing the degree qualification.

GENERAL PROCUREMENT NOTICE

Lao People’s Democratic Republic

Second Lao PDR Competitiveness and Trade Project (LCTP2)

Finance, Competitiveness, and Investment, EAP

PROCUREMENT NOTICE Grant No. TF No. D2315

Project ID No.  P512702

The Ministry of Industry and Commerce (MOIC) of the Government of Lao PDR has received financing in the amount of US$1,980,296 equivalent from the World Bank toward the cost of the Second Lao PDR Competitiveness and Trade Project (LCTP2), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds to payments for goods, works, non-consulting services and consulting services to be procured under this project. This project is financed by the Australian Government through its Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade.

The project will include the following components: Component A – Trade Facilitation: strengthening institutional trade capacity (non-tariff measures and transit facilitation) and supporting customs ICT capacity building; Component B – Business Environment: enhancement of business entry digitalization and strengthening public and private dialogue; and Component C – Project Management. International competitive procurement may include consulting services for business information portal, and for policy, technical, advisory support to the project.

Procurement of contracts financed by the World Bank will be conducted through the procedures as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (February 2025) (Procurement Regulations), and is open to all eligible firms and individuals  as defined in the Procurement Regulations.[1] After project negotiations, the World Bank shall arrange the publication on its external website of the agreed initial procurement plan and all subsequent updates once it has provided a no objection.

Specific procurement notices for contracts subject to open international competitive procurement will be announced, as they become available, on the World Bank’s external website, MOIC’s website www.moic.gov.la, and the Ministry of Finance’s website http://ppmd.mof.gov.la/ and the Vientiane Times newspaper (national circulation).

Name of Project:  Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER SOP2)

Grant number:    IDA-E4810

Job title: Road Safety Officer

Reference Number: 45A000141/CP/08/2026

The Government of Mozambique, represented by the Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL), has received funding from the World Bank for the Transport Corridors for Economic Resilience (TRACER SOP2) project and intends to apply part of the resources to consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") involve serving as the primary focal point for site-level traffic safety management while directly assisting the PIU Coordinator in project administration, contract compliance, and tracking progress. The main objectives of the assignment are: Coordinating and monitoring the implementation of all road safety activities under the Project; Providing technical recommendations for the improvement of road safety studies, engineering designs, traffic management plans and construction works; Supporting the integration of international road safety best practices into project implementation; and Monitoring compliance with road safety requirements throughout the project lifecycle.

It is anticipated that the Officer should perform the scope of this consultancy over a duration of two years from contract signature. The contract may be extended based on satisfactory performance and work program requirements. There will be a 3-month probationary period from the contract signature date.The RSO will report directly to the Project Coordinator.

The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) for the assignment can be obtained from the email address provided below.

The Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL) now invites qualified individuals ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing the Services. Expressions of interest must include the following: (i) a CV detailing qualifications, work experience and achievements in comparable work and (ii) a cover letter, specifically addressing how the applicant fulfills each of the mandatory selection criteria listed below.

Mandatory Requirements

  • A Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field such as Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or an equivalent discipline.
  • At least 10 (ten) years of experience in road construction, including a minimum of 6 (six) years in the field of road safety;
  • Experience in at least two similar projects financed by the World Bank or other International Financial Institutions;
  • Proven experience in road safety design and construction;
  • Excellent command of the Portuguese language and knowledge of the English language will be considered an advantage.

Desired Requirements

  • Experience working with government entities in the field of road safety;
  • Experience in Work Zone Road Safety Assessments;
  • Demonstrated knowledge of international road safety standards and practices;
  • Familiarity with road safety audit procedures and road safety inspections and assessments

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn  to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Rules for IPF Borrowers of September 2025 ("the Rules"), which sets forth the Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

For more information, please visit the address below during office hours from 8:30 a.m. to 3 p.m.

Submissions of Interest in Portuguese and English must be sent in writing to the address below (by e-mail) by 15:00 hours on September 30, 2026, local time, CAT/UTC +2.

 

Ministry of Transport and Logistics,

Attention:Portfolio Coordinator

procnotices.notice_text:
REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

Country: Republic of Mozambique

Name of Project:  Mozambique Safer Roads for Socio-Economic Integration (SRSEI) PROGRAM

Grant number:    IDA-E0780

Job title: SRSEI Project Coordinator

Reference Number: MZ-PMU-561409-CS-INDV

The Government of Mozambique, represented by the Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL), has received funding from the World Bank for the Mozambique Safer Roads for Socio-Economic Integration (SRSEI) and intends to apply part of the resources to consulting services.

The consulting services ("the Services") involve accountability for day-to-day implementation oversight of assigned PIU activities in the designated province(s), serving as the primary operational interface between field execution and the PCU. The PIU Coordinator will ensure that all components are effectively executed, and in a timely manner in accordance with the implementation plan.

The Project Coordinator will be required to work in close liaison with the PCU, ANE, INATRO and other stakeholders and in accordance with the Legal Agreements, and various approved project implementation manuals. A high degree of initiative and a pro-active and consultative approach will be required from the Project Coordinator in order to achieve the outcomes of this assignment. The expected duration of the assignment is 24 months. There will be a probationary period of 3 months from the date of signing the contract. The contract will be renewed upon satisfactory performance. The Project Coordinator is required to report to the Portfolio Coordinator at the CPU of the MTL

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be obtained at the address given below.

The Ministry of Transport and Logistics (MTL) now invites qualified individuals ("Consultants") to express their interest in providing the Services. Expressions of interest must include the following: (i) a CV detailing qualifications, work experience and achievements in comparable work; (ii) a cover letter, no more than two pages long, specifically addressing how the applicant fulfills each of the mandatory selection criteria listed below.

The Project Coordinator should have the following minimum qualifications and skills:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, project management, construction management or related field. 
  • At least Fifteen (15) years general working experience, of which least 10 years of progressive experience in civil works project management specifically for roads of at least 50 km or other infrastructure of similar complexity to the program
  • Experience in contract administration and management of consultants/contractors, including tracking deliverables, reviewing outputs, facilitating acceptance, and supporting invoice certification processes.
  • Experience  in contract management based on FIDIC, including prevention and/or mitigation of claims that involve financial losses to the Employer.
  • Knowledge of the World Bank's Environmental and Social Framework (ESF), in particular ESS1, ESS2, ESS4, and ESS5..
  • Demonstrated ability to lead or coordinate teams and to work effectively with government counterparts at central and provincial levels, private sector, communities and other stakeholders.
  • Working experience in Mozambique.
  • Fluency in Portuguese and English (both written and spoken)

Desirable requirements

  • Master degree in Civil Engineering, project management, construction management or related field.
  • Familiarity with OPBRC and/or Design Build contract structures.
  • Familiarity with the latest project management techniques and tools is essential. Having professional accreditation for Project Management from a recognized body.
  • Proven experience coordinating procurement processes and supporting preparation of TORs/specifications/bidding documents, and following procurement steps through contract award.
  • Demonstrated experience in GBV/SEA/SH-sensitive programme environments.
  • Good knowledge of BOQ interpretation, Detailing, Specifications, Public Procurement, Project/Contract management, Quality Control and dispute resolution.
  • Experience in the road safety standards.
  • Familiarity with national policies, procedures, and government processes.
  • Experience coordinating field implementation and undertaking regular site visits, including documenting progress, risks, quality and safeguards issues.
  • Familiarity with STEP (World Bank's procurement tracking platform) and experience with e-SISTAFE or equivalent government financial management systems.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn  to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Rules for IPF Borrowers of September 2025 ("the Rules"), which sets forth the Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

For more information, please visit the address below during office hours from 8:30 a.m. to 3 p.m.

Submissions of Interest in English must be sent in writing to the address below (only by e-mail) up to 15:00 hours on September 30, 2026, local time, CAT/UTC +2.

Ministry of Transport and Logistics,

Attention: Portfolio Coordinator

Avenue: Martires of Inhaminga nr 336, floor 1st

Email:  procurement.ucp@mtl.gov.mz

Maputo – Mozambique

procnotices.notice_text:
MINISTRY OF TRANSPORT, HIGHWAYS AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

CONSULTANCY SERVICES (FIRMS)

Project: Regional Empowerment through Vibrant, Inclusive, and Viable Economies (REVIVE)

Project ID: P511605

Credit No.: 7985-LK

Contract Name: Consultancy Services for Detailed Design and Construction Supervision for Gurunagar Fisheries Village Cluster – Jaffna and Cod Bay Fisheries Harbour Cluster – Trincomalee

Contract No.: LK-UDA-PMU-551524-CS-QCBS, World Bank

1.    The Government of Sri Lanka has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Empowerment through Vibrant, Inclusive, and Viable Economies (REVIVE) Project. The Ministry of Transport, Highways and Urban Development (MoTHUD), serving as the Executing Agency, intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2. The consulting services (“the Services”) include the review and validation of conceptual master plans and feasibility studies; site surveys and engineering investigations; preparation of implementable, climate-resilient detailed designs, Good for Construction drawings, design calculations, technical specifications, bills of quantities, cost estimates and World Bank-compliant bidding documents; intermittent technical support during works procurement; full-time construction supervision and contract administration; and support during the Defects Liability Period for investments at the Gurunagar Fisheries Village Cluster in Jaffna and the Cod Bay Fisheries Harbour Cluster in Trincomalee.

3. The total duration of the assignment is expected to be approximately fifty-four (54) months: Phase A – Detailed Design, Bidding Documents and intermittent procurement support, twelve (12) months, including six (6) months for detailed design and up to six (6) months for procurement support; Phase B – Construction Supervision and Contract Administration, thirty (30) months; and Phase C – Defects Liability Period Support, twelve (12) months.

4. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://www.transport.gov.lk/ (Media > Procurement > TORs).

5. The Chairman of the Ministry Consultants Procurement Committee, on behalf of the REVIVE Project, now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required firm-level qualifications, relevant experience and institutional capacity to perform the assignment.

 The shortlisting criteria are as follows:

a. Legal status, core business and institutional experience: The Consultant shall be a legally registered consulting firm with at least ten (10) years of institutional experience in detailed engineering design and construction supervision or contract administration of fisheries harbours, ports, coastal or marine infrastructure, or integrated infrastructure assignments of comparable technical complexity.

b. Comparable assignment experience: Successful completion, during the last ten (10) years, of at least two (2) comparable consultancy assignments. At least one assignment shall have covered both detailed engineering design and construction supervision with contract administration, and at least one assignment shall have included a fisheries harbour, port, coastal or marine infrastructure component. The same assignment may satisfy both requirements.

c. Scale of consultancy experience: Successful completion of at least one (1) comparable consultancy contract with a consultancy services value of not less than USD 1 million or its equivalent. The value shall refer to consulting services and shall exclude the value of construction works. This assignment may also be counted under criterion (b).

d. Coastal and marine technical capability: Demonstrated institutional capability in conducting investigations and studies relating to coastal processes, harbour and coastal engineering and the detailed design of coastal or marine structures.

e. Multidisciplinary and multi-site delivery capability: Demonstrated organisational, technical and managerial capability to mobilise and coordinate a multidisciplinary design team and separate site-based construction supervision teams for two geographically separated project locations.

f. Relevant geographic experience: Experience in Sri Lanka, South Asia, or other coastal and island environments with similar physical, climatic, institutional and implementation conditions will be considered an advantage during shortlisting.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the EOI stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised September 2025), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

6. Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but shall indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

7. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality Cost Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised September 2025).

8. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 0900 to 1600 hours, except Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays.

9. Expressions of Interest must be delivered in written form, in person, by mail or by e-mail, to the address below on or before 14.00hrs on September 22, 2026.

procnotices.notice_text:
Request for Proposals Information Systems

 (Single Stage-Two Envelope Process)

Purchaser: National Information Technology Authority-Uganda

Name of Project: Uganda Digital Acceleration Project (UDAP)

Project ID: P171305             Credit No.: 6898-UG            Country: Uganda

Contract Title:  Design, Development and Deployment of The Refugee Partnership Coordination and Monitoring System.
 

Reference No.: NITA-U/UDAP/SUPLS/2026-2027/00010

Issued on: 7th September, 2026                                       

1.The Government of Uganda represented by the National Information Technology Authority Uganda (NITA-U) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the: Uganda Digital Acceleration Project-Government Network (UDAP-GOVNET), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under the contract for Design, Development and Deployment of the Refugee Partnership Coordination and Monitoring System.
 

2.National Information Technology Authority-Uganda (NITA-U) now invites sealed Bids from eligible Proposers for Design, Development and Deployment of the Refugee Partnership Coordination and Monitoring System.

3. The procurement process will be conducted through International competitive procurement using Request for Proposals (RFP) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers - Procurement in Investment Projects Financing” (July 2016, revised February 2025) and is open to all eligible proposers as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

4. Interested eligible Proposers may obtain further information from National Information Technology Authority-Uganda and inspect the request for proposal document during office hours 0800 to 1700 hours from Monday to Friday at the address given below.

5.A pre-proposal meeting will be held 22nd September, 2026 at NITA-U Head Office, Palm Courts, Plot 7A, Rotary Avenue at 1100 Hours East Africa Time with an Online Virtual Meeting .A link will be shared with all registered proposers prior to the date of the meeting. The proposers who wish to attend the meeting shall register and submit their official email addresses not later than one (1) day to the date of the meeting to jacqueline.musimenta@nita.go.ug.

6.The request for proposal document in English may be purchased by interested eligible Proposers upon the submission of a written application to the address below and upon payment of a nonrefundable fee of Ugx.200,000 (Two Hundred Thousand Uganda Shillings Only) or equivalent in a freely convertible currency. The method of payment will be the Electronic Funds Transfer (EFT) Bank account number: 006550058000001, Customer name: National Information Technology Authority, Uganda (NITA-U), Account title: NITA-U Local Revenue Expenditure Account, Bank Name: Bank of Uganda Swift Code: UGBAUGKA. A PDF bidding document shall be sent to the potential bidder electronically upon receipt of confirmation of payment.

7.Proposals must be delivered to the address below on or before 22nd October, 2026 at 1100 Hours East Africa Time Electronic procurement will not be permitted. Late Proposals will be rejected. Proposals will be publicly opened in the presence of the Proposers’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend, at the address below on 1st Floor Boardroom, 1105 Hours East Africa Time 22nd October, 2026.  All envelopes marked “FINANCIAL PART” shall remain unopened and will be held in safe custody of the Purchaser until the second public Proposals opening.

 8.Proposals must be accompanied by a Proposal Security of ;

 UGX 100,000,000/= (Uganda Shillings, One Hundred Million) or an equivalent amount in a freely convertible currency.

 

The Proposal Security shall be valid in accordance with Section II-Proposal Data Sheet (PDS); ITP 20.1

9.Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring the Borrower to disclose information on the successful proposer’s beneficial ownership, as part of the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form as included in the proposal document.

10.The address referred to above is:

    The Procurement Specialist

    National Information Technology Authority-Uganda

    Plot 7A, Palm Courts, Rotary Avenue,1st Floor Room 1

    Kampala-Uganda

procnotices.notice_text:
Invitation for Bids for Capacity-Building Training on One Health Governance for Key Government Departments, One Health Seed Talent, and One Health Grassroots Practitioners under the World Bank Loan Project for Prevention, Preparedness and Response to Emerging Infectious Diseases – Hainan Province Project (Global “One Health” Hainan Demonstration Project) (Contract No. HN-NS-15)

Date: August 13, 2026

Invitation for Bids No.: 0733-26093611

1The Government of the People’s Republic of China has received a loan from the World Bank toward the cost of the World Bank Loan Project for Prevention, Preparedness and Response to Emerging Infectious Diseases – Hainan Province Project (Global “One Health” Hainan Demonstration Project) and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan to eligible payments under the contract for Capacity-Building Training on One Health Governance for Key Government Departments, One Health Seed Talent, and One Health Grassroots Practitioners (Contract No. HN-NS-15).

2China International Tendering Co., Ltd. (the Procurement Agent), on behalf of Hainan University (the Purchaser), now invites eligible and qualified Bidders to submit sealed bids for the following non-consulting services:

Contract No.HN-NS-15
Contract NameCapacity-Building Training on One Health Governance for Key Government Departments, One Health Seed Talent, and One Health Grassroots Practitioners
Number of Contract Packagesone
Service PeriodFrom the date of contract signing until the World Bank loan closing date of December 31, 2027

4This procurement will be conducted through National Competitive Procurement using the Request for Bids (RFB) method in accordance with the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (the “Procurement Regulations”). Eligible Bidders meeting the requirements set forth in the Procurement Regulations are eligible to participate.

5Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from the address specified in this Invitation for Bids and inspect or purchase the Bidding Documents from August 13, 2026 until the bid submission deadline of September 15, 2026, during the following hours on working days (excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and statutory public holidays): 9:00–11:30 a.m. and 1:30–5:00 p.m. (Beijing Time).

6Prospective Bidders should note the provisions of Clause 4 of the Instructions to Bidders concerning eligibility and conflicts of interest. Any Bidder found to have a conflict of interest shall be ineligible.

7The qualification requirements for Bidders include:

Single Bid Submission

The Bidder shall have a good record and reputation, with no record of major violations of laws or regulations or material breaches of contract in its business activities during the three years preceding participation in government procurement activities, a good social reputation, and no administrative penalties imposed by any administrative authority at or above the county level for violations of laws or regulations.

The Bidder shall provide the corresponding supporting documents or a Letter of Commitment (in a self-prepared format) to demonstrate compliance with the above requirements.

Joint Venture (JV)

Information required for submission of Bids by a Joint Venture (JV): The maximum number of members in the Joint Venture (JV) shall be 2. Each member of the JV shall meet the following requirement:

During the three years preceding participation in government procurement activities, the JV member shall have no record of major violations of laws or regulations or material breaches of contract in its business activities, shall have a good social reputation, and shall not have been subject to any administrative penalty imposed by an administrative authority at or above the county level for violations of laws or regulations.

The Bidder shall provide the corresponding supporting documents or a Letter of Commitment (in a self-prepared format) to demonstrate compliance with the above requirement.

Average Annual Turnover

The Bidder’s minimum average annual turnover for the years 2023 to 2025 shall be no less than RMB 7.5 million.

Note: In the case of a Joint Venture, the lead member and other JV member(s) shall collectively meet the above requirement, provided that the lead member shall meet at least 50% of the above requirement (i.e., an average annual turnover of no less than RMB 3.75 million over the most recent three years).

Contract Experience

During the past three years (from January 1, 2023 to the Bid submission deadline), the Bidder shall have experience in providing professional services or training in fields related to One Health, such as zoonotic disease prevention and control, antimicrobial resistance, food safety risk monitoring, environment and health, occupational health, emergency management, and other relevant areas. The Bidder shall have completed at least two contracts for professional services or training in One Health-related fields commissioned by relevant government departments at or above the county level, with each contract having a value of no less than RMB 100,000.

The Bidder shall provide scanned copies of the key pages of the relevant commission contracts or agreements, including the contract cover page, page specifying the procurement/service content (clearly demonstrating that the services fall within a One Health-related field), contract amount page, signature and seal page, and contract signing date page.

Note: In the case of a Joint Venture, the lead member and other JV member(s) shall collectively meet the above requirements.

Key Personnel

The Bidder shall provide the corresponding supporting documents in its Bid in accordance with the requirements for the relevant Key Personnel specified below.

NOPositionQualification RequirementsTasks and ResponsibilitiesMan-MonthsSupporting Documents
1Project Director (Project Manager)A bachelor’s degree or above, with a senior-level professional and technical title in public health or a relevant One Health field. Experience in overall project coordination and management, with strong capabilities in cross-departmental coordination, budget control, and emergency response.Overall coordination of the implementation of the project and development of the overall work plan for training implementation;
Liaising with Hainan University and other partner organizations and coordinating the resolution of various issues arising during project implementation;
Monitoring and controlling the quality, progress, and use of project funds;
Reviewing various deliverables and materials and taking the lead in preparing the overall project report.		1 person, 15 months

(1) Copy of the graduation certificate and copy of the degree certificate or other supporting document evidencing the degree qualification;

(2) Copy of the professional and technical title certificate;

(3) Curriculum Vitae (CV) (in a self-prepared format);

(4) Letter of Commitment issued by the Bidder regarding the qualifications and capabilities of the proposed Project Manager, duly affixed with the Bidder’s official seal;

(5) For currently employed personnel, proof of social security contributions for the most recent six months shall be provided; for retired personnel re-employed by the Bidder, proof of salary payment for the most recent six months shall be provided.

2Project Management PersonnelBachelor’s degree or above, with an intermediate-level or higher professional and technical title in public health or a relevant One Health field. Good communication and organizational skills, with strong capabilities in managing various project records and documentation. Proficient in the use of office automation software, with extensive experience in training planning, organization, coordination and control, and emergency response.Responsible for the daily work assignment and performance assessment of the team; coordinating registration information for various training programs and establishing and maintaining records such as participant rosters and the One Health seed talent database; coordinating the work interfaces among personnel in different positions, following up on task implementation progress, and monitoring the effectiveness of the training programs.3 persons, 5 months each

(1) Copy of the graduation certificate and copy of the degree certificate or other supporting document evidencing the degree qualification;

(2) Copy of the professional and technical title certificate;

(3) Curriculum Vitae (CV) (in a self-prepared format);

(4) Letter of Commitment issued by the Bidder regarding the qualifications and capabilities of the proposed Project Management Personnel, duly affixed with the Bidder’s official seal;

(5) For currently employed personnel, proof of social security contributions for the most recent six months shall be provided; for retired personnel re-employed by the Bidder, proof of salary payment for the most recent six months shall be provided.

3Materials Design Specialist

College degree or above, with experience in graphic design and materials production; proficient in design software such as Adobe Photoshop (PS) and Adobe Illustrator (AI); capable of enhancing and designing training materials and presentation materials; and familiar with the visual design requirements in the field of One Health.

Responsible for the design and printing coordination of training manuals, certificates, directional signage, and other materials; completing the layout, visual enhancement, and revision of 12 One Health-themed PowerPoint presentations; and designing publicity materials and visual resources related to the training.1 person, 15 months

(1) Copy of the graduation certificate and copy of the degree certificate or other supporting document evidencing the degree qualification;

(2) Curriculum Vitae (CV) (in a self-prepared format);

(3) Letter of Commitment issued by the Bidder regarding the qualifications and capabilities of the proposed Materials Design Specialist, duly affixed with the Bidder’s official seal;

(4) For currently employed personnel, proof of social security contributions for the most recent six months shall be provided; for retired personnel re-employed by the Bidder, proof of salary payment for the most recent six months shall be provided.

4On-Site Event Execution PersonnelProficient in employee training and day-to-day management, with strong capabilities in project organization, efficient execution, and training satisfaction management.Responsible for the venue setup, equipment testing, registration arrangements, on-site order maintenance, refreshment arrangements, and other event coordination and execution activities for various training sessions; maintaining photographic and video records throughout the training sessions and organizing on-site implementation materials.3 persons, 5 months each

(1) Curriculum Vitae (CV) (in a self-prepared format);

(2) Letter of Commitment issued by the Bidder regarding the qualifications and capabilities of the proposed On-Site Event Execution Personnel, duly affixed with the Bidder’s official seal;

(3) For currently employed personnel, proof of social security contributions for the most recent six months shall be provided; for retired personnel re-employed by the Bidder, proof of salary payment for the most recent six months shall be provided.

5

Logistics Support Personnel

The personnel shall have experience in project logistics support, be familiar with flight and hotel booking and transportation coordination procedures, have a good understanding of logistics service resources in Hainan and major cities across China, and strictly comply with financial management requirements.Responsible for purchasing round-trip air tickets for participants and experts, booking and paying for hotel accommodation, coordinating airport/train station transfers and local transportation, and other related arrangements; coordinating accommodation, meals, materials procurement, and other logistics support during the training; and organizing supporting documents and records for logistics-related expenses.3 persons, 5 months each

(1) Curriculum Vitae (CV) (in a self-prepared format);

(2) Letter of Commitment issued by the Bidder regarding the qualifications and capabilities of the proposed Logistics Support Personnel, duly affixed with the Bidder’s official seal;

(3) For currently employed personnel, proof of social security contributions for the most recent six months shall be provided; for retired personnel re-employed by the Bidder, proof of salary payment for the most recent six months shall be provided.

6Technical Support PersonnelThe personnel shall have at least 3 years of experience in computer and multimedia technical support, be proficient in the operation of equipment for online and offline training, video recording, and document archiving, and have basic capabilities in troubleshooting network failures.Responsible for providing technical support for audio, projection, and other equipment at training venues; organizing and compiling training video and photographic materials; establishing and maintaining an electronic archiving system for training materials; and ensuring the secure storage of various digital materials.

1 person, 15 months

(1) Curriculum Vitae (CV) (in a self-prepared format);

(2) Letter of Commitment issued by the Bidder regarding the qualifications and capabilities of the proposed Technical Support Personnel, duly affixed with the Bidder’s official seal;

(3) For currently employed personnel, proof of social security contributions for the most recent six months shall be provided; for retired personnel re-employed by the Bidder, proof of salary payment for the most recent six months shall be provided.

7Financial Support PersonnelAt least 3 years of accounting work experience; proficient in the use of various financial software and highly experienced in cost and expense management and accounting.Responsible for maintaining the project financial records and managing invoices, receipts, and other supporting documents.1 person, 15 months

(1) Curriculum Vitae (CV) (in a self-prepared format);

(2) Letter of Commitment issued by the Bidder regarding the qualifications and capabilities of the proposed Financial Support Personnel, duly affixed with the Bidder’s official seal;

(3) For currently employed personnel, proof of social security contributions for the most recent six months shall be provided; for retired personnel re-employed by the Bidder, proof of salary payment for the most recent six months shall be provided.

 

Current Assets

The minimum amount of current assets and/or credit facilities available after deducting commitments for other contracts shall be no less than RMB 1 million.

Note: In the case of a Joint Venture, the lead member and other JV member(s) shall collectively meet the above requirement, provided that the lead member shall meet at least 50% of the above amount requirement.

SubcontractorThe experience of Subcontractors shall not be taken into consideration.

Failure to meet any of the above qualification requirements shall result in rejection of the Bid.

Bids from Joint Ventures are acceptable. The maximum number of members in a Joint Venture shall be: 2.

Further details are provided in the Bidding Documents.

7Interested eligible Bidders may submit an application to purchase the Bidding Documents at the address specified in this Invitation for Bids and pay a non-refundable fee of RMB 1,000. Payment may be made in cash or by direct bank transfer to the account of the Procurement Agent (Account Name: China International Tendering Co., Ltd.; Bank: China CITIC Bank, Beijing Sanyuanqiao Sub-branch; Account No.: 8110701013102383606). The Bidding Documents will be delivered by mail. The Purchaser and the Procurement Agent shall not be responsible for any loss or delay of the Bidding Documents during delivery.

8All Bids shall be submitted to the address specified in this Invitation for Bids no later than 09:30 a.m. on September 15, 2026 (Beijing Time). Late Bids will be rejected. The opening of Bids will be conducted publicly at the address specified in this Invitation for Bids. Bidders may send representatives to attend the Bid opening.
