procnotices.notice_text:
BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA

REPUBLIKA SRPSKA

REPUBLIC ADMINISTRATION FOR GEODETIC AND PROPERTY AFFAIRS

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

CONSULTANT'S QUALIFICATIONS-BASED SELECTION (CQS)

Study and Analysis of Spatial Plans for All 64 Local Self-Government Units in Republika Srpska

Employer

Republic Administration for Geodetic and Property Affairs of Republika Srpska (RGA)

Project

Geospatial Infrastructure and Valuation Enhancement Project - Additional Financing (GIVE AF)

Loan No.

9956-BA

Assignment Title

Study and Analysis of Spatial Plans for All 64 Local Self-Government Units in Republika Srpska

Procurement Method

Consultant's Qualifications-Based Selection (CQS)

Bank Review

Post Review

Procurement Plan Ref. No.

BA-RGARS-570618-CS-CQS

Country

Bosnia and Herzegovina / Republika Srpska

Issue Date

01 September 2026

1. Project background

Bosnia and Herzegovina has entered into a Loan Agreement with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (World Bank) for the Additional Financing of the Geospatial Infrastructure and Valuation Enhancement Project (GIVE AF), part of the proceeds of which is allocated to Republika Srpska. The Republic Administration for Geodetic and Property Affairs of Republika Srpska intends to apply part of the proceeds of this financing to eligible payments under the contract for the consulting services described in this Request for Expressions of Interest.

The Project financing has not yet become effective. This selection process is being conducted as advance procurement and at the Client's own risk. Any review, clearance or no objection by the World Bank in relation to the selection process, documents or proposed contract award shall not constitute a commitment by the World Bank to finance the Project or the resulting contract.

Any contract award, signature or effectiveness shall be subject to the applicable provisions of the Financing Agreements and to the Project financing becoming effective, as applicable.

2. Description of the assignment

The consulting services (the “Services”) comprise the preparation of a comprehensive study and analysis of existing spatial-planning documentation for all 64 local self-government units in Republika Srpska. The assignment will examine the structure, content, quality, availability, level of digital readiness and applicability of spatial plans as an input source for the establishment and operation of the mass valuation system.

The Services will include, inter alia:

  • inventorying and systematizing spatial, urban, zoning, regulatory and other relevant planning documents for all 64 local self-government units;
  • assessing the availability, currency, consistency, quality and usability of the planning documentation;
  • identifying spatial and planning factors that may influence real estate value and legally permissible and economically optimal use;
  • preparing a preliminary classification of the territory according to characteristics relevant to mass valuation;
  • establishing a working GIS project and preparing standardized GIS layers, attribute structures, metadata, thematic maps and cartographic outputs;
  • assessing the possibility of linking planning data with cadastral, topographic, address, market and other relevant datasets;
  • providing recommendations for the use of planning attributes in value zoning, market segmentation, property classification and development of valuation model variables; and
  • proposing an institutional, functional and information model for the permanent storage, management, updating and use of the Study results, including an assessment of whether the results should be incorporated into the Real Estate Register for Mass Valuation, established as a separate module or maintained in another interoperable information system of the RGA.

Expected duration: four (4) months from the effective date of the contract.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment will be available free of charge on the RGA website at: https://www.rgurs.org/stranica/oglasi-give

3. Invitation to consultants

The Republic Administration for Geodetic and Property Affairs of Republika Srpska now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, September 2023, as amended from time to time (the “Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should clearly indicate whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

4. Qualification and Selection Criteria

The best qualified firm will be selected in accordance with the Consultant's Qualifications-Based Selection (CQS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations. Expressions of Interest will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:

No.

Criterion

Requirement

1

Relevant experience of the firm

During the last three (3) years, calculated from the date of publication of this REOI, or from the date of registration if the firm has operated for a shorter period, the Consultant shall have successfully completed at least one (1) contract of the same or similar nature and complexity, with a value of at least BAM 185,000.00 (including VAT) or the equivalent in another currency.

2

Definition of a similar assignment

A similar assignment means an assignment involving the analysis, processing and/or systematization of spatial-planning, cadastral, topographic or other relevant geospatial data for the purposes of mass property valuation, including the identification or analysis of spatial and property characteristics relevant to valuation.

3

Organizational and managerial capacity

The Consultant shall demonstrate adequate organizational, technical and managerial capacity to implement the assignment across all 64 local self-government units within the four-month implementation period.

4

Evidence

The Consultant shall provide a concise company profile and details of relevant assignments, including the client, assignment title, scope, contract value, implementation period, country/location and contact details for reference checks. Client certificates of satisfactory completion, where available, or other appropriate supporting evidence should be provided.

Key experts will not be evaluated at the EOI/qualification stage. Their qualifications and experience will be assessed at the proposal stage, in accordance with the Terms of Reference. The anticipated key expert positions are Team Leader, GIS Expert and Economist/Analyst.

5. Contents of the Expression of Interest

  1. cover letter signed by an authorized representative of the Consultant;
  2. company profile, legal name, address, registration details and contact information;
  3. description of the Consultant's core business and fields of expertise;
  4. details of assignments relevant to the qualification and selection criteria, presented in a clear reference table;
  5. client certificates of satisfactory completion, where available, or other appropriate supporting evidence for the cited assignments;
  6. description of the Consultant's organizational and managerial capacity for implementation of the assignment within the required period;
  7. information on any proposed association, joint venture or sub-consultancy, including the role of each party; and
  8. a statement confirming the absence of a conflict of interest in accordance with the Procurement Regulations.

Expressions of Interest should be concise and directly relevant to the above criteria. Brochures and general promotional materials that do not demonstrate relevant qualifications are not required.

All costs associated with the preparation and submission of the Expression of Interest, participation in any subsequent proposal process and contract negotiations shall be borne solely by the Consultant. The Client shall have no liability or obligation to reimburse any such costs, regardless of the outcome, suspension, cancellation or re-launch of the selection process.

The issuance of this REOI, receipt or evaluation of Expressions of Interest, selection of the best qualified Consultant, issuance of a request for proposal or conduct of negotiations shall not oblige the Client to award or sign a contract. The Client reserves the right to suspend, cancel or re-launch the selection process in accordance with the applicable Procurement Regulations and Project requirements, without liability for costs incurred by Consultants.

6. Submission of Expressions of Interest

Expressions of Interest must be delivered in written form, in English, by e-mail and/or in hard copy, no later than 16 September 2026 at 12:00 (noon), local time, to the address below. The subject line/envelope should state: “Expression of Interest - Study and Analysis of Spatial Plans for All 64 Local Self-Government Units in Republika Srpska - BA-RGARS-570618-CS-CQS”.

Republic Administration for Geodetic and Property Affairs of Republika Srpska
GIVE AF Project Implementation Unit (PIU)
Attn: Jasna Grubor, Senior Expert Associate for Monitoring International Projects
Trg Republike Srpske 8, 78000 Banja Luka, Bosnia and Herzegovina
Tel.: +387 51 338 000
E-mail: give@rgurs.org
Cc: tamara.vasilic@rgurs.org

Further information may be obtained at the above address during official working hours, from 07:30 to 15:30, local time.

The Client reserves the right to verify the information submitted and to request clarifications or additional supporting documents during the evaluation of Expressions of Interest.

 

BOSNIA AND HERZEGOVINA
REPUBLIKA SRPSKA
REPUBLIC ADMINISTRATION FOR GEODETIC AND PROPERTY AFFAIRS

ADDENDUM NO. 1

to the Request for Expressions of Interest (REOI)

Study and Analysis of Spatial Plans for All 64 Local Self-Government Units in Republika Srpska

Project

Geospatial Infrastructure and Valuation Enhancement Project – Additional Financing (GIVE AF)

Procurement Method

Consultant’s Qualifications Based Selection (CQS)

Procurement Plan Ref. No.

BA-RGARS-570618-CS-CQS

Original REOI Issue Date

01 September  2026

Addendum Issue Date

4 September 2026

 

Purpose of this Addendum. This Addendum supplements the published REOI by making explicit the comparative evaluation and numerical scoring methodology that will be applied to Expressions of Interest. The substantive qualification requirements already disclosed in the REOI remain unchanged.

1. Amendment to Section 4 – Shortlisting Criteria

Section 4 of the REOI is supplemented as follows:

The evaluation will be conducted in two stages.

Stage 1 – Minimum qualification requirements (Pass/Fail)

Only Consultants that satisfy the minimum requirements below will proceed to comparative scoring:

  • Relevant experience: during the last three (3) years, calculated from the date of publication of the REOI, or from the date of registration if the firm has operated for a shorter period, the Consultant must have successfully completed at least one (1) contract of the same or similar nature and complexity, with a value of at least BAM 185,000 or the equivalent in another currency.
  • Definition of a similar assignment: an assignment involving analysis of geospatial data – spatial-planning documentation, cadastral data and/or topographic data – for the purposes of mass valuation of real estate or state cadastral systems.
  • Organizational and managerial capacity: the Consultant must demonstrate adequate organizational, technical and managerial capacity to implement the assignment across all 64 local self-government units within the four-month implementation period.

A Consultant that does not satisfy the above minimum requirements will not be further evaluated.

Stage 2 – Comparative numerical scoring

Consultants that pass Stage 1 will be compared and ranked using the following scoring methodology:

No.

Evaluation criterion

Scoring guidance

Max. points

1

Core business and fields of expertise relevant to the assignment

Assessment of the extent to which the Consultant’s demonstrated core business and institutional experience are directly relevant to geospatial, cadastral, spatial-planning and/or mass valuation assignments of comparable nature. The assessment is comparative and does not introduce an additional minimum eligibility threshold.

30

2

Qualifications and experience relevant to the assignment

Assessment of the quality, relevance, depth and comparability of completed assignments demonstrated by the Consultant. Particular weight will be given to assignments involving analysis of spatial-planning, cadastral and/or topographic data for mass valuation purposes. Experience relating to state cadastral systems remains eligible in accordance with the published definition of a similar assignment, but will be assessed according to its actual relevance to the subject assignment.

60

3

Organizational, technical and managerial capacity of the firm

Assessment of the demonstrated capacity to organize and manage the assignment within the required four-month period and across all 64 local self-government units, including the firm’s organizational approach, internal coordination capacity and availability of relevant technical disciplines at firm level.

10

TOTAL

100

2. Clarification on Relevant Experience

The requirement for at least one qualifying similar contract remains a mandatory pass/fail requirement. Its purpose is to ensure that firms entering the comparative stage have demonstrated experience in assignments materially connected with the subject matter of the Study. In the comparative scoring stage, stronger and more directly relevant experience may receive a higher score, but no new minimum qualification requirement is introduced by this Addendum.

For the avoidance of doubt, direct experience in using or analysing geospatial, spatial-planning, cadastral or topographic data for mass valuation purposes will be considered more directly relevant to the present assignment than experience limited to general cadastral-system work, while both remain within the published definition of a similar assignment.

3. Key Experts

Key experts will not be evaluated at the Expression of Interest / shortlisting stage. The qualifications and experience of the proposed key experts will be considered only at the subsequent stage of the CQS process, in accordance with the Terms of Reference and the Request for Proposals. The anticipated key expert positions remain Team Leader, GIS Expert and Economist/Analyst.

4. Other Provisions

All other provisions, requirements and conditions of the original REOI remain unchanged. This Addendum forms an integral part of the REOI and shall be read together with it.

The deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest remains 16 September 2026 at 12:00 noon, local time in Banja Luka.

procnotices.notice_text:
Date: September 7, 2026

NCB Bid No.: 0701-262010070013

Invitation for Bids No.: 0701-262010070013

 

1. The People’s Republic of China has received the loan from the World Bank toward the cost of Shaanxi Energy Transition and Innovation Demonstration in the Heating Sector and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of this loan to payments under the Contract for Xi’an City Xincheng District Yangjiacun Comprehensive Renovation Mid-deep Geothermal Heating Project (Phase II) – DK1 Mid-deep Geothermal Heat Exchange Borehole Construction and Equipment Installation Project (Contract No.: XA-YJC-C01).

 

2. The Xi'an Xinye Industrial Co., Ltd. now invites sealed bids from all eligible and qualified bidders for Construction of mediumdeep geothermal heat exchange wells and installation works for heatexchange station building system. The installation works for heatsupply station building system include procurement of auxiliary equipment, installation of main units, pipelines and valves. The outdoor mediumdeep geothermal heating works cover drilling of geothermal heatexchange wells, excavation and backfilling of outdoor pipe trenches, masonry of inspection wells, installation of pipelines and valves, thermal insulation, pressure testing, flushing, overall system commissioning and other works.

The construction period for the abovementioned works shall be 3 months.

 

3. Bidding will be conducted through the National Competitive Bidding procedures.  The bidding is open to all eligible as defined in the Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers of the World Bank.

 

4.    Interested eligible bidders may obtain further information from China International Tendering Co., Ltd. and inspect the Bidding Documents at the address given below from September 7, 2026 to October 15, 2026.

 

5. The attention of prospective Bidders is drawn to the eligibility and conflict of interest provisions under ITB 4 of the Bidding Documents. All Bidders found to have a conflict of interest shall be disqualified.

 

6. Qualifications requirements include:

(1) Non-performance of a contract did not occur within the last FIVE (5) years prior to the deadline for bid submission, based on all information on fully settled disputes or litigation.  A fully settled dispute or litigation is one that has been resolved in accordance with the Dispute Resolution Mechanism under the respective contract, and where all appeal instances available to the bidder have been exhausted.

(2) All pending litigation shall in total not represent more than 50% of the Bidder’s net worth and shall be treated as resolved against the Bidder.

(3) Declare any civil work contracts that have been suspended or terminated and/or performance security called by an employer for reasons related to the non-compliance of any environmental, or social, or health or safety requirements or safeguard in the past five years.

(4) Submission of audited financial statements or if not required by the law of the bidder’s country, other financial statements acceptable to the Employer, for the last THREE [3] years (2023-2025) to demonstrate the current soundness of the bidders financial position and its prospective long term profitability. As a minimum, a Bidder’s net worth calculated as the difference between total assets and total liabilities for each of the three years should be positive.

(5) Minimum average annual turnover of CNY 52 million, calculated as total certified payments received for contracts in progress or completed, within the last THREE (3) years (2023-2025).

(6) The Bidder shall demonstrate access to, or availability of, financial resources such as liquid assets, lines of credit, and other financial means, other than any contractual advance payments to meet:

(i) the following cash-flow requirement of CNY 5.2 million; and

(ii) the overall cash flow requirements for this contract and its concurrent commitments.

(7) Experience under contracts in the role of contractor, subcontractor,  for at least the last FIVE [5] years prior to the applications submission deadline.

(8) (a) Participation as contractor, or subcontractor, in at least TWO (2) contracts within the last FIVE (5) years, each with a value of at least CNY 4.1 million, that have been successfully and substantially completed and that are similar to the proposed Works. i. Upon completion of geothermal well drilling, measurements shall be carried out for well depth, well diameter, hole deviation and borehole temperature. The borehole diameter shall not be less than 220mm, and the borehole spacing shall meet heat exchange requirements and shall not be less than 15m; ii. Installation works of heatexchange station building system, including installation of main units, pipelines and valves.

(9) The bidder shall possess valid GradeIII or higher General Contracting Qualification for Municipal Engineering Construction.

(10) The bidder shall hold a valid Safety Production License issued by the housingurbanrural development authority.

Additional details are provided in the Bidding Documents.

RÉPUBLIQUE DU BURUNDI

MINISTERE DES FINANCES, DU BUDGET ET DE L’ECONOMIE NUMERIQUE

PROJET D’APPUI AUX FONDATIONS DE L’ECONOMIE NUMERIQUE AU BURUNDI « PAFEN »

Pays : Burundi

N° du projet : P 1763967

Don N° : E0930-BI

Références : BI-PAFEN-PIU-2.1.1.6-CS-QCBS

Emis le : 08/9/2026

AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET

(SERVICES DE CONSULTANTS)

SÉLECTION DE FIRMES/CABINETS

RECRUTEMENT D’UN CABINET POUR L’ASSISTANCE TECHNIQUE À LA MISE EN PLACE D’UN SYSTÈME DE MANAGEMENT DE LA QUALITÉ CONFORME À LA NORME ISO 9001 :2015 AU SEIN DU SETIC

Le Gouvernement de la République du Burundi a reçu un don de 92 millions de dollar USD de la Banque mondiale pour financer le coût du Projet d’Appui aux Fondations de l’Economie Numérique dont l’objectif de développement est d’accroitre l’accès à l’internet haut débit en particulier pour les communautés mal desservies et d’améliorer la capacité du gouvernement à gérer les ressources plus efficacement et fournir les services publics par voie numérique.

Il a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour effectuer des paiements au titre du contrat pour « recrutement d’un cabinet pour l’assistance technique à la mise en place d’un système de management de la qualité conforme à la norme ISO 9001 :2015 au sein du SETIC ».

L’objectif global est d’accompagner le Secrétariat Exécutif des Technologies de l'Information et de la Communication (SETIC) dans la conception, la mise en œuvre, le déploiement, l'appropriation, l'évaluation et l'amélioration continue d'un Système de Management de la Qualité (SMQ) conforme aux exigences de la norme ISO 9001:2015, afin de renforcer durablement la qualité, l'efficacité, la fiabilité, la traçabilité et la performance de ses services, d'améliorer la satisfaction des parties intéressées et de préparer l'institution à l'obtention de la certification ISO 9001:2015.

Plus spécifiquement, il s’agit de :

  1. Réaliser un diagnostic organisationnel du SETIC et une analyse des écarts (Gap Analysis) entre les pratiques existantes et les exigences de la norme ISO 9001: 2015.
  2. Déterminer et faire valider le contexte de l'organisation, le périmètre du SMQ, les enjeux internes et externes ainsi que les parties intéressées pertinentes et leurs besoins et attentes.
  3. Identifier et analyser les exigences légales, réglementaires, contractuelles, normatives et techniques applicables aux activités du SETIC.
  4. Élaborer, en concertation avec la Direction, la politique qualité, les objectifs qualité, les indicateurs de performance et le cadre de gouvernance du SMQ, en cohérence avec les missions du SETIC et les objectifs du Projet d'Appui aux Fondations de l'Économie Numérique (PAFEN).
  5. Identifier, cartographier, documenter, standardiser, optimiser et déployer l'ensemble des processus de pilotage, des processus métiers et des processus supports, ainsi que leurs interactions.
  6. Définir les responsabilités, autorités, mécanismes de coordination et modalités de pilotage nécessaires au fonctionnement efficace du SMQ.
  7. Élaborer le système documentaire du SMQ comprenant notamment les procédures, les fiches processus, les instructions de travail, les formulaires, les modèles d'enregistrements et toute autre information documentée requise par la norme.
  8. Concevoir et mettre en œuvre une approche fondée sur les risques et les opportunités, incluant leur identification, leur évaluation, leur traitement et leur suivi.
  9. Mettre en place un dispositif de mesure et de suivi de la performance des processus reposant sur des indicateurs pertinents, des tableaux de bord et des mécanismes réguliers d'analyse.
  10. Mettre en place un système de gestion des non-conformités, des réclamations, des actions correctives, des actions d'amélioration et des retours d'expérience.
  11. Développer les compétences du personnel à travers des actions de sensibilisation, de formation et de transfert de compétences, notamment au profit des pilotes de processus, des responsables qualité et des auditeurs internes.
  12. Accompagner le SETIC dans la planification et la réalisation d'un cycle complet d'audits internes conformément aux lignes directrices de la norme ISO 19011.
  13. Assister la Direction dans la préparation et la tenue de la revue de direction, ainsi que dans le suivi des décisions et actions qui en découlent.
  14. Accompagner la conduite du changement afin de favoriser l'appropriation du SMQ par l'ensemble du personnel et d'assurer sa pérennisation.
  15. Réaliser un pré-audit (audit à blanc), élaborer un plan d'actions de levée des écarts éventuels et préparer le SETIC à l'audit de certification ISO 9001: 2015, sans créer de conflit d'intérêts avec l'organisme certificateur.

La durée indicative de la mission est de huit (8) mois, soit trente-deux (32) semaines, à compter de la notification de l’ordre de service. Le cabinet proposera une charge en jours-experts cohérente avec sa méthodologie et garantira une présence suffisante sur site durant le diagnostic, les ateliers, le déploiement, les audits internes et la revue de direction.

La mission se déroulera principalement à Bujumbura, dans les locaux du SETIC et du PAFEN, ainsi que sur les sites techniques concernés. Certaines tâches de préparation pourront être menées à distance après accord préalable, sans réduire les obligations de transfert de compétences ni la disponibilité des experts clés.

Les Termes de référence peuvent être téléchargés sur le site du PAFEN : https://pafen.gov.bi/appels-doffres/  ou obtenus aux adresses mentionnées ci-dessous.

L’Unité de Gestion du PAFEN invite les consultants (firmes)/institutions spécialisés, ayant une expérience et expertise dans le déploiement et le suivi des projets de déploiements de réseaux de télécommunications/TIC intéressés par la présente mission à fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils disposent des qualifications requises et de l'expérience pertinente pour l’exécution des services.

Critères d’établissement de la liste restreinte :  

  • Etre légalement constitué et justifier d’au moins dix (10) années d’expérience générale en conseil organisationnel, management de la qualité ou domaines connexes ;
  • Justifier d’au moins cinq (3) missions achevées de mise en place ou d’amélioration d’un SMQ ISO 9001, dont au moins deux (2) ayant conduit à une certification ;
  • Avoir réalisé au moins une (1) mission similaire dans une administration publique, une agence gouvernementale, un opérateur d’infrastructure ou une organisation fournissant des services numériques critiques ;

Pour être acceptables, les références doivent indiquer le projet, bailleur de fonds, l’année de réalisation, et le montant du contrat. Les références seront soutenues par des copies des contrats et des certificats de bonne fin de mission.

Les Experts clé ne sont pas évalués au stade de la présélection stade.

L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes 3.15, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement des Projets d’Investissement (FPI) de la Banque mondiale, édition de novembre 2020 (« Règlement de Passation des Marchés relatifs aux règles de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflit d’intérêt).

En outre, veuillez-vous référer aux informations spécifiques sur les conflits d’intérêts liées à cette mission comme énoncés au paragraphe 3.17 du Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

Les consultants peuvent s’associer à d’autres firmes pour renforcer leurs compétences, mais ils doivent indiquer clairement si l’association prend la forme d’un groupement solidaire (joint-venture) et / ou d’un accord de sous-traitant. Dans le cas d'un groupement solidaire (joint-venture), tous les partenaires du groupement solidaire (joint-venture) seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de la totalité du contrat, s’ils sont sélectionnés.

Un consultant sera sélectionné par la méthode de Sélection Fondée sur la Qualité et le Coût (SFQC) telle que décrite dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau: de 9H :00 à 12H :00 et de 15 H: 00 à 16H: 30 heure locale de lundi à jeudi et de 8H: 00 à 12H: 00 les vendredi (heure de Bujumbura: GMT+2)

Les manifestations d'intérêt écrites doivent être remises par écrit à l'adresse ci-dessous par courrier ordinaire ou par e-mail au plus tard le 25 Septembre 2026 à 12 heures (heure de Bujumbura, GMT+2) avec la mention :

  1. Pour avoir plus d’informations sur les services requis, les consultants pourront consulter les termes de références sur le site de l’Agence de Développement Municipal (http://www.adm.sn/)

APPEL A CANDIDATURES

Assistant régional en Agriculture, Élevage et Pêche – Région Atsimo Andrefana

AMI N° : 26/563414/AMI/UNGP/MIONJO

1. Le Gouvernement de la République de Madagascar a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale pour couvrir le coût du Projet soutien aux moyens de subsistance résilients dans le Sud de Madagascar « MIONJO » et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce fonds à des services de consultant.

2. Les services de consultant (« les Services ») viseront à fournir un appui technique et opérationnel au niveau des zones d’intervention du Projet dans la Région dans la réalisation des activités des sous-composantes 3A, 3C et 4C des Agriculture, élevage, pêche et moyens de subsistance.

3. Les Termes de Référence (TDR) pour la mission sont disponibles sur le site internet suivant : https://mionjo.mg ou sur demande à adresser à procurement@mionjo.mg.

4. L’Unité Nationale de Gestion du Projet (UNGP) MIONJO invite dès à présent les consultants admissibles (« Consultants ») à faire part de leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les Consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et l’expérience pertinente pour exécuter les Services. Les critères de sélection sont les suivants :

Qualifications et expériences :

  • Titulaire d’un diplôme d’Ingénieur Agronome ou Maîtrise Environnement, Sciences humaines et sociales, Géographie ou tout autre domaine en lien avec la mission ;
  • Avoir au moins 5 ans d’expériences professionnelles dans le domaine du développement Agricole, sécurité alimentaire ou développement local ;
  • Avoir au moins 3 expériences professionnelles réussies dans des projets de développement agricole ou de soutien aux moyens de subsistance ;
  • Présenter au moins 2 expériences de projets ou d’activités de développement dans la Région d’intervention postulée ;
  • Présenter au moins 1 expérience professionnelle dans un projet multisectoriel financé par un bailleur de fonds international.

Atouts :

  • Pratique courante de l’anglais (écrit et oral) ;
  • La pratique des dialectes locaux des zones d’intervention du Projet et connaissance du contexte.

Les candidats qualifiés seront convoqués à un entretien.

5. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la Section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs de FPI » de la Banque mondiale, Septième Edition Septembre 2025 (« Règlement de Passation des Marchés »), qui énonce la politique de la Banque mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêts. En outre, veuillez-vous reporter aux informations spécifiques suivantes sur les conflits d’intérêts liés à cette mission : « Le Consultant qui a une relation professionnelle ou familiale étroite avec tout cadre de l’Emprunteur, de l’organisme d’exécution du projet, d’un bénéficiaire d’une fraction du financement de la Banque ou de toute autre partie représentant l’Emprunteur ou agissant en son nom qui participe directement ou indirectement à tout segment : (i) de la préparation des Termes de référence de la mission ; (ii) du processus de sélection pour le contrat ; ou (iii) de la supervision du contrat, ne peut être attribuaire d’un contrat, sauf si le conflit résultant de ladite relation a été réglé d’une manière que la Banque juge satisfaisante tout au long du processus de sélection et de l’exécution du contrat »..

6. Un Consultant sera sélectionné conformément aux dispositions décrites dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés.

7. Des informations supplémentaires peuvent être obtenues à l’adresse ci-dessous pendant les heures de bureau de 09h00 à 17h00, heures locales.

8. Les manifestations d’intérêt contenant (i) une lettre de motivation avec prétention salariale rédigée en français, (ii) un CV détaillé mise à jour (modèle en annexe aux TDRs) et (iii) les copies des diplômes et le Certificats prouvant les expériences professionnelles, seront adressées au Coordonnateur du Projet MIONJO et envoyées à l’adresse ci-dessous (en personne, par la poste, ou par courriel) au plus tard le 20 septembre 2026.

Adresse : Lot II A 105 G Nanisana Iadiambola, Antananarivo 101

Courriel : procuremen@mionjo.mg  et rpm@mionjo.mg

Et portant la mention « AMI N° 563414/26/AMI/UNGP/MIONJO – Assistant régional en Agriculture, Élevage et Pêche – Région Atsimo Andrefana

procnotices.notice_text:
SADC SECRETARIAT

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANTS SELECTION)

 

 

COUNTRY:                       Botswana

 

NAME OF PROJECT:        REGIONAL STATISTICS PROJECT (RSP)

 

PROJECT ID:                     P175731

 

ASSIGNMENT TITLE:       INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANCY TO DEVELOP THE NATIONAL STRATEGY FOR DEVELOPMENT OF STATISTICS (NSDS) OF SOUTH AFRICA- BW-SADC-563161-CS-INDV

 

REFERENCE NUMBER:      SADC/3/5/2/460

 

DATE OF ISSUE: 9 September 2026

 

The SADC Secretariat, through the Regional Statistics Project (RSP) (P175731), has received grant financing from the International Development Association (IDA) of the World Bank. The Project Development Objective is to strengthen the institutional capacity of SADC to produce, disseminate and use quality statistics while increasing regional harmonisation and collaboration. Under the Project, SADC is implementing Component 1: Harmonisation, Quality and Dissemination of Core Social and Economic Statistics.

 

In view of the above, the SADC Secretariat is undertaking several interventions aimed at strengthening the SADC Regional Statistical System (SRSS) and enhancing the production, quality, harmonisation, dissemination and use of regional statistics. These interventions include technical assistance and capacity building activities in priority statistical areas, including poverty statistics, statistical software and data processing, survey methodologies, national accounts, environment and climate change statistics, statistical communication, quality assurance and harmonised regional statistical guidelines.

 

The SADC Secretariat intends to apply part of the proceeds of the grant towards the consulting services to coordinate and compile a National Strategy for the Development of Statistics (NSDS) for South Africa, in support of the objectives of the Regional Statistics Project.

 

The SADC Secretariate invites submissions from suitably qualified and interested individual consultants to conduct the training, recruited as individual consultants following World Bank Procurement Regulations dated September 2023.

 

Title             :  Individual Consultancy to Develop the National Strategy for Development of Statistics (NSDS) of South Africa (1 Position)

 

Accountable:  Senior Officer, Research and Statistics 

 

Duration of Assignment:  180 Calendar Days

 

  1. The Objectives of the Assignment

 

The overall objective of this consultancy is to support National Statistical offices (NSOs) on strategic and policy aspects pertaining to Official Statistics to strengthen governance and provide strategic direction ensuring fulfillment of its mandate in the development process at national and international level.

 

  1. Specific objectives

 

The specific objective of this consultancy is to develop a draft NSDS for South Africa as a guiding policy framework for coordination and implementation of statistics in support of national priorities and responsive to regional, continental and global agendas. The NSDS also need to cater for specific issues such as advocacy, communication, gender mainstreaming, cybersecurity, results-based framework, innovative data sources and others relevant.

 

  1. Expected results

 

The consultant is expected to achieve the following results in the following as part of drafting the NSDS:

 

  1. Assessment and review of the existing policy and strategic frameworks identifying gaps and challenges amongst others with a defined and well-structured stakeholders engagement plan;

ii.       Identification of specific and impactful recommendations with justification for implementation towards drafting of the NSDS and its strategic focus areas and discussion within the governance structure for consideration; and

iii.      Detailed explanation of the strategic focus areas with a results-based monitoring & evaluation framework aligned to national and international priorities/commitments.

  1. QUALIFICATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

 

This assignment is expected to be carried out by an individual consultant expert and should be an expert in strategic and policy formulation in Official Statistics.  The specific profile is provided below:

 

Qualifications and Skills

 

    • A minimum of a Degree in Statistics, Economics or related field. A Master’s Degree those having a PhD in the same field shall be an added advantage.

 

General Professional Experience

 

    • The Expert Must have at least ten (10) years of experience in statistical coordination of statistical systems at the highest level.

 

Specific Professional Experience

 

    • At least 5 years of experience of leading a statistics department at national, regional, continental or global level;
    • Demonstrated experience in at least 2 exercises of coordinating the development and implementation, of policy frameworks guiding statistical functions in statistics such as NSDS and related;
    • Demonstrated Experience on undertaking high-level activities pertaining to advocacy, gender mainstreaming, communication, innovative data sources, cybersecurity and applying results-based monitoring & evaluation within the national statistical system.
  2. Duration of the assignment

 

The Individual Consultant will be recruited for 180 Calander Days.

 

  1. Facilities to be provided by the Client

 

For the expert working on this consultancy, the Contracting Authority shall facilitate for visa entry in South Africa, if required.

 

  1. Location of Employment

 

The assignment may involve traveling to Pretoria, South Africa.

 

  1. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” dated September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

 

  1. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consultant Selection Method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

  1. Mode of Application

 

Interested Individuals Consultants meeting the stated requirements should submit their Expressions of interest including updated detailed curriculum vitae (CVs) and copies of professional certificates must be delivered in a written form using a drag and drop electronic tender box by Wednesday, 23rd September 2026 on or before 00:00 hours, Botswana local time. No public opening will be heard.

 

 

SADC Collab Link: https://collab.sadc.int/s/FEDjgEATZEdSNqJ

 

Kindly note that only highly technically scored bidder will be contacted for negotiations meeting.

 

  1. VALIDITY OF THE TECHINICAL PROPOSAL

Your Technical proposal should be valid for a period of 90 days from the date of deadline for submission.

procnotices.notice_text:
Government of Pakistan

Ministry of Energy

(Power Division)

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSION OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRM SELECTION)

 

Country: Pakistan

Name of Project: Electricity Distribution Efficiency Improvement Project (EDEIP)

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: IBRD-93180                                                                                                          

Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for Supporting the Operation and Development of the Competitive Trading Bilateral Contract Market (CTBCM) In Pakistan’s Power Sector.

Reference No. PK-MOE-566558-CS-QCBS-CTBCM

 

The Ministry of Energy (Power Division) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Electricity Distribution Efficiency Improvement Project (EDEIP) and intends to apply part of the proceeds for engagement of a consultancy firm for Independent System and Market Operator of Pakistan (ISMO) for supporting the operation and development of the Competitive Trading Bilateral Contract Market (CTBCM) in Pakistan’s power sector.

 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include key experts to undertake multiple tasks for supporting the operation and development of the CTBCM according to the scope provided in the detailed Terms of Reference (TOR). The TOR for the assignment can be downloaded from https://power.gov.pk/ or www.ismo.gov.pk.

 

The Program Implementing Unit (PIU), Ministry of Energy (Power Division) now invites EOI from eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants are required to provide information demonstrating their qualification and relevant experience to perform the Services described in the TOR. Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

 

Shortlisting criteria for the Consultants include:

  • The firm must have been duly incorporated and operational for a minimum period of ten (10) years as of the date of submission in the same business (documented evidence showing years in business such as certificate of incorporation etc. must be provided).
  • The firm shall provide evidence of at least two prior assignments of comparable nature, scope and complexity, demonstrating relevant experience.
  • The firm shall demonstrate that its proposed team, supported by adequate back-end resources, possesses the requisite qualifications and experience to effectively deliver the assignment.

                                                                                                                                              

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers February, 2025 (“the Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications, but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub- consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, whereas each partner within the JV shall meet the qualification and experience requirement for the assigned role, if selected.

 

The Consultant will be selected in accordance with the “Quality and Cost Based Selection (QCBS)” method set out in the Procurement Regulations of the World Bank for IPF Borrower February, 2025.

 

Expressions of Interest must be submitted as per given contact details by 14-Sep-2026 at 05:00 pm (PST). Electronic copy of EOI can also be submitted ahead of the couriered submission. Further information may be obtained using the contact details provided below.

 

 

Attention: Project Director, PIU-EDEIP Project (Component-IV)

Address: Office of the Project Director (EDEIP), ISMO Building,                 Pitras Bukhari Road, H-8/1, Islamabad

Email: danis6pk@gmail.com

Phone: +92-051-831-1557

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (REOI)

(INDIVIDUAL CONSULTING SERVICES)

PHILIPPINES

PHILIPPINES DIGITAL INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT

Loan No./Credit No./ Grant No.: IBRD Loan Number 9730-PH

Assignment Title: Engagement of Technical Consultant under the Project Implementation Unit - Communications Officer

 

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): PH-DICT-566516-CS-INDV

The Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Philippines Digital Infrastructure Project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. 

The consulting services (“the Services”) include the hiring of a Communications Officer who will directly report to the Project Manager and will be responsible for the design and implementation of a communication strategy to inform internal and external stakeholders, users of public facilities to be connected under the project, beneficiary departments, private sector stakeholders, and the wider public of the project activities to be implemented under the PDIP. The list of duties and responsibilities is provided in the detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) attached as “Annex A”. The engagement is a time-based contract for forty-eight (48) months period inclusive of a 6-month probation period. The Estimated Price Cost (EPC) per month is: ONE HUNDRED NINETY-NINE THOUSAND NINE HUNDRED NINETY-NINE PESOS AND 96/100 (Php199,999.96). The location for this position is at the designated office of the DICT in Quezon City, Philippines.

The DICT now invites eligible individuals (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services (attach curriculum vitae with description of experience in similar assignments, similar conditions, etc.). Firms’ staff may express interest through the employing firm for the assignment and, under such a situation, only the experience and qualifications of individuals shall be considered in the selection process. The criteria for selecting the Consultant are the following: 

REQUIRED COMPETENCIES & KNOWLEDGE

  1. Proficient in ICT-based office applications and tools, including word processing, spreadsheets, data processing, and PowerPoint.
  2. Excellent command of English and Tagalog, with strong interpersonal and communication skills.
  3. Sound understanding of the telecommunications sector and related policies and programs in the Philippines is an asset.
  4. Solid understanding of project planning, coordination, and implementation, with strong analytical capabilities.
  5. Applies critical thinking to improve current approaches and introduces new solutions that deliver results. Inspires and influences others to drive innovation.
  6. Takes personal and team responsibility to meet deadlines and achieve results. Continuously seeks improvement and acts as a strategic consultant to deliver impactful solutions.
  7. Contributes productively to team performance and ensures effective communication within and between teams. Resolves conflicts constructively and values diverse perspectives.
  8. Actively contributes to creating, applying, and sharing knowledge within the organization. Invests in personal development and builds professional networks.
  9. Analyzes facts, data, and lessons learned to support sound decision-making. Shows initiative and makes timely decisions when necessary.
  10. Demonstrates the ability to work both independently and within a team in an output-oriented environment. Takes initiative, works with minimal supervision, and adheres to strict timelines.
  11. Embraces learning new approaches and applies them effectively. Experience in health and social issues is an asset, along with strong analytical and cognitive skills.

ACADEMIC QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

  1. Degree (Masters or Bachelors) in Communications, Public Relations, Journalism or equivalent.
  2. At least 6 years’ work experience in the field of public information, media and communication.
  3. Experience with projects financed by international organizations will be an advantage.

The attention of interested Consultants (including firms) is drawn to paragraph 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of The World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Fifth Edition dated September 2023 (“the Regulations”), as per financing agreement, setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. 

Further information can be obtained at the address given below every Monday to Friday, 9:00 am to 4:00 pm. 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail) on or before  16 September 2026 at 4:00 PM 

 

For further information, please refer to:

procnotices.bid_description: Procurement of Equipment for Hainan One-health International Research Institution (Batch No. 2A)（3.3.1）
procnotices.contact_address: Hainan, China
procnotices.notice_text:
Invitation for Bids

Date: September 4, 2026

Bid No.: 0733-26092892

1The Government of the People’s Republic of China has received a loan from the World Bank to finance the Hainan Province Project under the World Bank Loan for Emerging Infectious Diseases Prevention, Preparedness and Response Project (Global “One Health” Hainan Demonstration Project), and intends to apply part of the proceeds of the loan to eligible payments under the contract for the Procurement of Equipment for the Hainan International One Health Research Institute – Second Batch, Package A (Contract No. HN-G-86).

2CITIC International Tendering Co., Ltd., as the Procurement Agent, on behalf of Hainan University, as the Purchaser, now invites sealed bids from eligible and qualified Bidders for the following Goods and related Services:

Contract No.

HN-G-86

Contract Title

Procurement of Equipment for the Hainan International One Health Research Institute – Second Batch, Package A

Main Types and Quantities of Goods

Equipment including High-Throughput Automated Nucleic Acid Fragmentation System, High-Throughput Microplate Liquid Handling System, Intelligent Storage System for Tropical Microorganisms, and Remote Inspection, Tracking and Traceability Management System for Special Items and Biological Materials, as well as related services. For details, please refer to Chapter VI – Schedule of Requirements for Goods of the Bidding Documents.

Delivery Period

Within 90 calendar days from the date of contract signing.

Note: The budget amount for this Contract Package is RMB 14.9720 million. This budget amount is provided for reference only and shall not constitute the maximum bid price (bid control price) for this procurement. The Evaluation Committee shall evaluate the Bids in accordance with the evaluation criteria and methods specified in the Bidding Documents. A Bid price exceeding the budget amount shall not, in itself, be deemed a non-responsive Bid or result in the rejection of the Bid.

3This procurement will be conducted through National Competitive Procurement using the Request for Bids (RFB) method, as specified in the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (the “Procurement Regulations”). All eligible Bidders meeting the requirements set forth in the Procurement Regulations are eligible to participate in the bidding.

4Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from the address specified in this Invitation for Bids and inspect or purchase the Bidding Documents from September 4, 2026, to October 13, 2026, the bid submission deadline, during the following hours: 9:00–11:30 a.m. and 1:30–5:00 p.m. (Beijing Time), Monday through Friday, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and statutory public holidays.

5Potential Bidders should note the provisions of Clause 4 of the Instructions to Bidders concerning eligibility and conflicts of interest. Any Bidder with a conflict of interest shall be deemed ineligible.

6The qualification requirements for Bidders include:

Business Scale

The Bidder’s average annual turnover for the most recent three years (2023–2025) shall be not less than RMB 10 million.

Contract Experience

Within the past ten years (from January 1, 2016 to the present), the Bidder, acting as a supplier, shall have successfully completed at least 15 contracts for the supply of laboratory instruments or equipment similar in nature and complexity to the products to be procured under this project, with the value of each individual contract being not less than RMB 3 million.

The Bidder shall provide supporting documents demonstrating compliance with the above requirements, which shall include, at a minimum, the contract agreement, acceptance certificate issued by the user, and proof of payment received under the supply contract. Copies of contracts included in the Bid shall contain, at a minimum, the pages showing the following information: the project name, scope/content of procurement, contract signing date, contract amount, and the contract signature and seal page. The Bidder shall also provide the name and contact details of the end-user contact person.

Technical Experience

The High-Throughput Automated Nucleic Acid Fragmentation System, High-Throughput Microplate Liquid Handling System, Intelligent Storage System for Tropical Microorganisms, and Remote Inspection, Tracking and Traceability Management System for Special Items and Biological Materials to be supplied shall each have at least five years of production experience. For each type of equipment, at least 10 units/sets shall have been sold and completed their warranty periods.

The Bidder shall provide supporting documents demonstrating compliance with the above requirements, including copies of key pages of sales contracts for similar goods and other relevant supporting documents.

Production Capacity

Not Applicable.

Financial Position

The Bidder’s audited annual financial statements for the most recent three years (2023, 2024, and 2025), including the balance sheets and income statements, shall demonstrate the Bidder’s sustained financial capacity and profitability. As a minimum requirement, the Bidder’s net assets, calculated as total assets less total liabilities, shall be positive in each of the three most recent financial years.

Cash Flow Capacity

The Bidder shall have sufficient readily available liquid assets, lines of credit, and other financing resources to meet the cash flow requirements for contract performance, taking into account the Bidder’s other ongoing contractual commitments. The minimum requirement shall be RMB 4 million.

Litigation History

The total amount of any pending claims, arbitration proceedings, or other litigation shall not exceed 50% of the Bidder’s net assets.

Joint Ventures are eligible to participate in the bidding. The maximum number of members in a Joint Venture shall be two (2). Either the Joint Venture Lead Member or the other Joint Venture Member shall meet the above qualification requirements.

For other detailed information, please refer to the Bidding Documents.

7Interested eligible Bidders may submit an application for the purchase of the Bidding Documents to the address specified in this Invitation for Bids and pay a non-refundable fee of RMB 1,000. Payment may be made in cash or by direct bank transfer to the account of the Procurement Agent as follows:

Account Name: CITIC International Tendering Co., Ltd.
Bank: China CITIC Bank, Beijing Sanyuanqiao Sub-branch
Account No.: 8110701013102383606

The Bidding Documents will be delivered by mail. The Purchaser and the Procurement Agent shall not be responsible for any loss of or delay in the delivery of the Bidding Documents during mailing.

All Bids shall be submitted to the address specified in this Invitation for Bids no later than 8:30 a.m. (Beijing Time) on October 13, 2026. Late Bids will be rejected. The Bid opening will be conducted publicly at the address specified in this Invitation for Bids. Bidders may send representatives to attend the Bid opening. The Bid opening will take place at 8:30 a.m. (Beijing Time) on October 13, 2026.

8All Bids must be accompanied by a Bid Security in the amount of RMB 290,000.00.

9The above addresses are as follows:

Address 1 – Address for Inspection of the Bidding Documents:
Room 1817, 18/F, Building 59, East Third Ring Middle Road, Chaoyang District, Beijing, China

Address 2 – Address for Purchase of the Bidding Documents:
Room 1817, 18/F, Building 59, East Third Ring Middle Road, Chaoyang District, Beijing, China

Address 3 – Address for Submission of Bids:
Bid Opening Room 206, Hainan Provincial Public Resources Trading Center, Government Affairs Phase II Building (formerly located on the north side of the former Provincial Government Government Service Center Building), West Dayingshan 2nd Street, Meilan District, Haikou, Hainan Province, China

Address 4 – Address for Bid Opening:
Bid Opening Room 206, Hainan Provincial Public Resources Trading Center, Government Affairs Phase II Building (formerly located on the north side of the former Provincial Government Government Service Center Building), West Dayingshan 2nd Street, Meilan District, Haikou, Hainan Province, China

10The Invitation for Bids for this procurement will be published on the following websites:

China Tendering and Bidding Public Service Platform

Hainan Provincial Public Resources Trading Service Platform

China Bidding and Tendering Network

Complaints related to the procurement process may be submitted to the email addresses of the Purchaser and the Procurement Agent specified above. Bidders may also copy their correspondence concerning complaints related to the procurement process to the Hainan Provincial Project Management Office of the World Bank Loan for Emerging Infectious Diseases Prevention, Preparedness and Response Project (Email: onehealth0898@163.com) and the World Bank (Emails: fyang2@worldbank.org; jguo@worldbank.org).

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – INDIVIDUAL CONSULTANT SELECTION)

Country: Eastern and Southern Africa (ESA)

Project: Regional Emergency Preparedness and Access to Inclusive Recovery (REPAIR)

Loan No./Credit No./Grant No.: TF0C5097-3E

Assignment Title: Recruitment of Seychelles Country Focal Point

Reference No.: MZ-REPAIR-495524-CS-INDV-2

African Risk Capacity Limited (ARC Ltd.) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Regional Emergency Preparedness and Access to Inclusive Recovery (REPAIR) Programme and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services include the recruitment of a Country Focal Point for Seychelles to support the implementation of the REPAIR Programme at country level. The Country Focal Point will serve as the principal in-country liaison officer between ARC Ltd. and national stakeholders, including the Ministry of Finance and representatives of various distribution channels, support project execution and stakeholder communication, ensure alignment of in-country activities with World Bank Environmental and Social Safeguards, support monitoring, evaluation and reporting, and contribute to the achievement of the Programme Development Objective of strengthening financial and operational preparedness to respond rapidly to climate and other shocks. The assignment is full-time for an initial period of one (1) year, renewable annually subject to satisfactory performance.

ARC Ltd. now invites eligible individual consultants ("Consultants") who are nationals of Seychelles and/or hold a valid work permit authorising employment in Seychelles to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should submit documentation demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://arcltd.org/opportunities/

The Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, Seventh Edition, September 2025, and will be evaluated based on the criteria indicated below.

The shortlisting criteria are:

· At least a Master's degree (or equivalent) in Project Management, Business Administration, Economics, Finance, Risk Management, Disaster Risk Management, Climate Change, Development Studies, Public Administration, or a related field.

· A minimum of ten (10) years of relevant professional experience in project or programme management, development programmes, disaster risk management, climate resilience, humanitarian response, insurance, disaster risk financing, public sector programmes, or related fields.

· At least five (5) years of experience coordinating and collaborating with government institutions, development partners, donors, financial institutions, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), United Nations agencies, or other relevant stakeholders.

· Demonstrated knowledge and practical experience in one or more of the following areas: disaster risk management, climate change adaptation, disaster risk financing, resilience programmes, humanitarian response, insurance, sovereign disaster risk financing, or related fields.

· Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with government counterparts, development partners, donors, financial institutions, and other key stakeholders.

· Demonstrated ability to manage competing priorities, coordinate multiple activities and stakeholders, identify implementation challenges, and propose practical solutions in a dynamic working environment.

· Fluency in English and French, both written and spoken, is mandatory.

· The Consultant must be a national of Seychelles.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, first published in July 2016 and revised in September 2025, Seventh Edition ("Procurement Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest. All inquiries should be sent to the following email address: procurementrepair@ltd.arc.int Expressions of Interest must be submitted by email to procurementrepair@ltd.arc.int no later than the 22nd of September 2026 at 17:00 hours (South Africa time). The email subject line should clearly state: “MZ-REPAIR-495524-CS-INDV-2 – Seychelles Country Focal Point".

TÜRKYE

TÜRKYE PREPAREDNESS FOR PUBLIC HEALTH EMERGENCIES PROJECT

Loan No.: 9754-TR

Assignment Title: Software Development, Updating, Maintenance and Support Services for the Infectious Disease Surveillance and Early Warning System (ZC) Web and Mobile Applications

Reference No. (as per Procurement Plan): TPPHEP/SBSGM/2026/CS/D.2.1.5.1/QCBS/1

1. The Republic of Türkiye has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the Türkiye Preparedness for Public Health Emergencies Project (TPPHEP), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

2. The consulting services (the “Services”) include the analysis, design, software development, testing, training, deployment, updating, maintenance and support of the Infectious Disease Surveillance and Early Warning System (ZC) Web Application and the development of a synchronized ZC Mobile Application. The assignment includes examination and migration of the existing systems; preparation of the Project Management Plan; analysis and requirements definition; UX/UI and technical design; development of disease-specific surveillance modules and an event management system; secure integrations with Ministry systems and external stakeholders; artificial-intelligence-supported early-warning and spatio-temporal analysis capabilities; testing, data migration, deployment and commissioning; training; and maintenance, operational support and additional development. The assignment is expected to be implemented over 30 (thirty) months and to require a multidisciplinary team of at least 16 personnel, as detailed in the TOR.

3. The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR), including the Minimum Requirements Document (MRD), can be found at the following websites.

https://sbsgm.saglik.gov.tr/

https://www.saglik.gov.tr/

4. The Ministry of Health, General Directorate of Health Information Systems now invites eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

5. A consulting firm is allowed to submit the Expression of Interest alone if it considers itself to be fully qualified on its own for the assignment, as it is not mandatory for Consultants to associate with any other firm(s), whether foreign or local. Alternatively, if Consultants choose to associate to enhance their qualifications and capability for the assignment, such associations may be in the form of a Joint Venture (in which all members shall be jointly and severally liable) and/or sub-consultants (for whose services the Consultant shall remain responsible). In the case of an association, the Consultants shall explain in the EOI submission: (a) the rationale for forming the association; and (b) the anticipated role and relevant qualifications of each Joint Venture member and/or each sub-consultant for carrying out the assignment. Failure to provide this explanation may result in the association not being shortlisted. For shortlisting purposes, only the qualifications of Joint Venture members will be taken into account; the qualifications of proposed sub-consultants will not be considered.

6. The shortlisting criteria are as follows, in which the specific experience of the Consultant relevant to the assignment will be considered of paramount importance:

i. General Experience of the Consultant (as a firm) in providing consulting services in the IT sector under contracts of comparable size. The Consultant shall demonstrate the successful completion, within the last five (5) years preceding the deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest, of at least one software development project under a single contract with a value of at least USD 6,000,000 or equivalent. The project shall have included a data warehouse, artificial intelligence (AI), and other related software components.

ii. Specific Experience of the Consultant (as a firm) relevant to the assignment in providing similar services under contracts of comparable size. The Consultant shall demonstrate the successful completion, within the last five (5) years preceding the deadline for submission of Expressions of Interest, of at least one software development project in the field of health information systems under a single contract with a value of at least USD 4,000,000 or equivalent. The project shall have included web-based and mobile applications, integration and interoperability with health information systems, data warehouse or high-volume health-data processing, Geographic Information Systems (GIS) or spatio-temporal analysis, artificial-intelligence-supported early-warning capabilities, data migration, information-security arrangements, testing, commissioning, maintenance and operational support.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the EOI shortlisting stage, and CVs of Key Experts should not be submitted with the EOI.

7. To demonstrate their qualifications and experience in meeting the above shortlisting criteria, Consultants are requested to submit, at a minimum, the supporting documentation listed below. A Consultant firm may use only its own qualifications and experience, and not those of its parent, sister or subsidiary companies or its employees:

i. The firm’s incorporation, trade or registration documents issued by the competent government authority in the country of the firm;

ii. The firm’s company brochure, including its core areas of business and years in business; and

iii. Completed Form-1 (attached to this REOI) providing information on similar contracts. The information shall include the contract name and reference number, a brief description of the scope and main deliverables, the contract value and the amount attributable to the firm, the contract period, the name of the Client and country of assignment, and the Consultant’s role. Copies of completion certificates or Client references for completed contracts are not required with the EOI. At the subsequent proposal stage, the Client may request shortlisted Consultants to submit supporting completion certificates.

8. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank’s Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers: Procurement in Investment Project Financing - Goods, Works, Non-Consulting and Consulting Services, Fifth Edition, September 2023 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

9. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

10. Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours from 10:00 to 17:30 (Türkiye time) on Business Days.

6.2 Contract Experience

From January 1, 2021 to the bid submission deadline, the bidder shall have successfully completed one similar contract (subject to the time of the overall contract acceptance report or the instrument acceptance report of the key equipment that meets the provisions of this project below), with a contract value of not less than RMB 40 million, and the contract content shall include at least one of the following 9 sets of equipment: Triple Quadrupole Liquid Chromatography Mass Spectrometer (or Ultra Performance Liquid Chromatography Mass Spectrometer), Liquid Chromatography Quadrupole Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometer, Gas Chromatography Tandem Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometer, Gas Chromatography Ultra-High Resolution Mass Spectrometer, Gas Chromatography Tandem Mass Spectrometer, Pyrolysis Gas Chromatography Mass Spectrometer (PY-GC/MS), Laser Ablation Inductively Coupled Plasma Tandem Mass Spectrometer (or either part of Laser Ablation or Inductively Coupled Plasma Tandem Mass Spectrometer), High Resolution Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometer, and High Performance Liquid Chromatograph.

  1. The value of each contract shall be not less than RMB 3 million, and the cumulative total value of the submitted contracts shall be not less than RMB 40 million;

The cumulative content of the submitted contracts shall include at least one of the following 9 sets of equipment: Triple Quadrupole Liquid Chromatography Mass Spectrometer (or Ultra Performance Liquid Chromatography Mass Spectrometer), Liquid Chromatography Quadrupole Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometer, Gas Chromatography Tandem Time-of-Flight Mass Spectrometer, Gas Chromatography Ultra-High Resolution Mass Spectrometer, Gas Chromatography Tandem Mass Spectrometer, Pyrolysis Gas Chromatography Mass Spectrometer (PY-GC/MS), Laser Ablation Inductively Coupled Plasma Tandem Mass Spectrometer (or either part of Laser Ablation or Inductively Coupled Plasma Tandem Mass Spectrometer), High Resolution Inductively Coupled Plasma Mass Spectrometer, and High Performance Liquid Chromatograph.

Meanwhile, the Bidder shall keep the relevant originals available for inspection.

6.3 Qualification Requirements

The Bidder shall hold valid and effective business license, tax registration certificate, and organization code certificate (for an entity that has integrated the three certificates into one, the business license shall be provided).

The Bidder shall provide copies thereof, stamped with the Bidder’s official seal.

6.4 Technical Experience

The Bidder shall demonstrate that the manufacturer of the key goods it offers meets the following requirements: (1) as of the deadline for submission of Bids for this project, the duration of mass production and market sale of the bid model or models of the same series of the key equipment shall be not less than 5 years; and (2) within the past 5 years (up to the deadline for submission of Bids for this project), at least 3 units of the bid model or models of the same series or of higher performance of the key equipment shall have been sold to analytical laboratories in the fields of agriculture, food safety, environment, medicine, scientific research and academic institutions, or similar testing fields, and such equipment shall have been in continuous and stable operation for more than 2 years. Triple Quadrupole Liquid Chromatography Mass Spectrometer (or Ultra Performance Liquid Chromatography Mass Spectrometer) and Gas Chromatography Tandem Mass Spectrometer.

The Bidder shall provide the manufacturer’s production history evidence for the key equipment, copies of the key pages of the sales contracts (at least including the contract name, the date of contract signing, the name and quantity of the goods, and the page bearing the signatures and seals), and a certificate of stable operation stamped by the user (which shall state the instrument model and the installation date and note that the equipment is in good operating condition).

The Bidder’s financial condition as reflected in its audited annual financial statements for the last 3 years (2023-2025) shall demonstrate long-term profitability. As a minimum, the Bidder’s net worth in each of the last three years (calculated as the difference between total assets and total liabilities) shall be positive.

The total amount of outstanding claims, arbitration or other litigation shall not exceed 50% of the Bidder’s net worth, and all pending litigation shall be accounted for on the assumption of an adverse outcome for the Bidder.

The Bidder shall provide a declaration issued by it (in a format prepared by the Bidder itself).

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST - CONSULTANT’S QUALIFICATIONS BASED SELECTION (CQS)

  

Name of Project

Fiji Energy Transformation Project Preparation (P515153)

Loan No/Credit No/Grant Number

GFPP Grant No. TF0D0728

Assignment Title

Gap analysis for National Control Center (NCC) with higher level of Variable Renewable Energy (VRE) systems, and propose initial design of the new NCC for EFL

Procurement Plan Ref Number

FJ-EFL-567211-CS-CQS

Reference No.

EOI-02/2026

Country of Delivery

Republic of Fiji

 

 

The Republic of Fiji, acting through Energy Fiji Limited (EFL), has received financing from the World Bank toward the costs of the Fiji Energy Transformation Project Preparation (P515153), and intends to apply part of the proceeds for the following consulting services.

 

The consulting services ("the Services") comprise a comprehensive gap analysis of EFL's National Control Centre (NCC) at Vuda Back Road, Nadi, and the definition of an initial design and modernisation roadmap for a future NCC capable of securely operating the Fiji grid at high levels of variable renewable energy penetration. EFL is the primary electricity provider in Fiji, serving Vitilevu, Vanualevu, Ovalau and Taveuni. Demand on the main VLIS grid currently exceeds 213 MW and is expected to exceed 300 MW within ten years, while EFL's Renewable Energy Roadmap targets the installation of 165 MW of solar capacity and over 40 MW of battery energy storage within five years. The NCC's current infrastructure, systems and operating procedures must be assessed against this future state.

 

The Services will cover:

  • assessment of the current SCADA/EMS infrastructure, data acquisition and analytics capability, and communications infrastructure (telemetry, fibre/OPGW, microwave, backup systems), including latency, signal loss and failover readiness;
  • evaluation of operational processes and readiness, including SOPs for normal and emergency conditions, demand and generation forecasting, grid security studies (contingency analysis, load flow, voltage stability), AVR and load frequency control performance, management of distributed energy resources and low-inertia conditions, disaster recovery and black-start coordination;
  • review of grid code and regulatory compliance against international standards and good practice, and delivery of a reviewed grid code document;
  • assessment of cybersecurity for operational technology and IT, and of physical security at the main and backup control centres, against Critical Infrastructure Protection standards;
  • assessment of staffing levels, competencies, training, control room ergonomics and human factors;
  • assessment of environmental and social aspects, including energy efficiency, waste management, sustainable procurement, disability inclusion and gender-appropriate facilities;
  • preparation of a Gap Analysis Report (inception, draft and final) mapping current versus desired "to-be" states, categorised by risk level, with a prioritised modernisation roadmap, action plan, timelines and cost estimates; and
  • support to EFL to define a fit-for-purpose procurement strategy — including packaging and contract type — and to prepare the corresponding draft bidding documents.

 

The assignment requires desktop review, stakeholder consultations, site visits and physical inspection of the control room and backup facilities, and benchmarking against international best practice (e.g. IEEE, IEC, ENTSO-E).

 

Implementation period: the assignment is expected to be completed within a maximum of seven (7) months from contract signature. Expected start date: October 2026.

 

Terms of Reference:  The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://www.tenderlink.com/efl(opens in new window) and is also attached to this REOI as Appendix 1.

 

Energy Fiji Limited now invites eligible consulting firms ("Consultants") to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

 

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to paragraphs 3.14, 3.16 and 3.17 of the World Bank's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers, latest’s edition, ("the Regulations"), setting forth the World Bank's policy on conflict of interest.

 

EOI Evaluation Criteria

20%

2. Relevant experience in SCADA/EMS and National/Regional Control Centre assignments, particularly gap assessments, modernization, design or upgrading of control centre systems

40%

3. Relevant experience in renewable energy integration and grid modernization, including high-VRE grids, BESS, grid stability and/or associated Grid Code work

20%
