Form and content of the Expression of Interest: Expressions of interest should not exceed 10 pages, excluding annexes, and should contain only the information necessary to assess the criteria set out above.  Consultants are not required to submit technical proposals, methodologies, work plans, staffing schedules, CVs of experts, or financial proposals at this stage. In accordance with the Regulations, the qualifications and experience of Key Experts do not form part of this evaluation, and any such material submitted will not be evaluated.

 

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but shall indicate clearly whether the association takes the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all members shall be jointly and severally liable, and the lead member shall be identified.

 

The firm assessed as best qualified against the above criteria will be invited to submit a technical and financial proposal and invited to negotiate a contract in accordance with the Regulations.

 

Submission

Further information can be obtained by emailing to tenders@efl.com.fj during office hours 8:00 AM to 4:30 PM (Fiji Time), Monday to Friday clear 3 days from the closing date of this EOI.

Expressions of interest must be uploaded to the EFL e-Tender Portal (TenderLink) at https://www.tenderlink.com/efl(opens in new window), by registering your company, by 4:00 PM (1600 hrs) Fiji Time on Tuesday, 22 September 2026.

Tender documents may be viewed and downloaded from www.efl.com.fj(opens in new window) or https://www.tenderlink.com/efl(opens in new window).

Submissions by email or facsimile will not be accepted and will be deemed null and void. Hard copy submissions to the tender box at EFL Head Office, Suva, will not be accepted.

The purpose is to assess the current state of infrastructure, technology, processes, and personnel against international best practices and future utility requirements , whilst adhering to the best environmental and social safeguard practices to ensure sustainable development.

1. Introduction & Background

Energy Fiji Limited (EFL) is the primary electricity provider in Fiji, responsible for the generation, transmission, and retail of electricity across the four (4) main islands of Vitilevu, Vanualevu, Ovalau & Taveuni. Formerly known as the Fiji Electricity Authority (FEA) which was established under the Electricity Act in 1966, it was corporatized in 2018 to operate as a public company limited by shares.

Energy Fiji Ltd (EFL) operates a National Control Centre in Vuda Back Road, Nadi  on the North-Western side of Vitilevu which is responsible for real-time monitoring and control of the national electricity grid. As demand grows, and renewable energy integration increases, the current NCC infrastructure and operational procedures require assessment to ensure efficiency, security, and reliability are not compromised and are operating well in optimum conditions.

1.1    The Renewable Energy Implementation Journey

EFL is currently embarking on a Renewable Energy Implementation Journey mainly focused on Variable Renewable Energy Sources (VRES) particularly, hydro, solar and wind which is intended over the next ten (10) years, majority of it will be solar.

  • Grid Demand Current demand for main VLIS grid currently sits at over 213MW which is expected to rise to over 300MW in the next ten years. As per the current Renewable Energy Roadmap,
  • Target Capacity: Under the current Renewable Energy Roadmap, EFL aims to install 165MW of solar capacity alongside 40MW+ of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) over the next 5 years

Modernized equipment is vital to ensure continuous forecasting, real-time grid stabilization, voltage management, and optimal battery dispatch to protect power grid inertia and prevent blackouts.

2. Objectives of the Assignment

The primary objective of this assignment is to identify technical, operational, and structural gaps between the NCC’s current capabilities and the required "future state". The future state must support a modern, secure grid running on 90% or more renewable energy as per EFL's national targets

3. Scope of Work

The selected consultant will complete the following tasks: 

  • Assessing current SCADA/EMS infrastructure.
  • Evaluating grid security and stability management practices.
  • Reviewing operational procedures, cybersecurity, and staffing availability & competence.
  • Providing a detailed roadmap to bridge identified gaps with an associated cost to carry this out – detailed list of hardware and software requirements, and required capacity for EFL (staffing and required certification)
  • Supporting EFL to define an appropriate procurement strategy and draft the procurement documents. The consultant will assess the available procurement options and recommend a fit-for-purpose procurement strategy, including packaging and contract type, based on the future-state architecture, market analysis and allocation of implementation risks. The appropriate bidding documents should then be prepared on the basis of the agreed strategy.

 

To complete above tasks, the consultant shall perform a comprehensive, multi-dimensional assessment covering the following areas:

 

3.1. Technical Infrastructure (SCADA/EMS/IT)

  • Review the age, reliability, and functional capacity of the current SCADA/Energy Management System (EMS).
  • Generator-side response performance, including whether or not it is automated.
  • Review existing data acquisition, data management, and analytics capabilities of the NCC, including the definition of future-state data and analytics requirements to support advanced EMS functions, operator situational awareness, and grid modernization.
  • Analyze communication infrastructure (telemetry, fiber optics, backup systems).
  • Assess integration capabilities for new technologies (smart grid, renewable energy management). 
  • Test for latency, signal loss, and failover readiness across fiber or microwave networks to ensure optimum communication links.

 

3.2. Operational Processes, Procedures & Readiness

  • Evaluate operating procedures (SOPs) for normal and emergency conditions.
  • Evaluate supply and demand management, including demand forecasts and generation forecasts, for normal and emergency conditions.
  • Assess grid security studies (contingency analysis, load flow, voltage stability).
  • Analyse compliance with grid codes and regulatory frameworks not only locally but to align to international standards and best practices
  • Analyze the center's ability to manage intermittent distributed energy resources (DERs) and low-inertia systems
  • Review automatic voltage regulation (AVR) and load frequency control (LFC) performance
  • Assess existing disaster recovery and black-start coordination procedures.
  • Identify state of the art weather forecasting tools to optimise generation mix in favour of our hydros and solar PVs

 

3.3. Cybersecurity & Physical Security

  • Review cybersecurity protocols for Operational Technology (OT) and IT infrastructure.
  • Assess physical security of the main NCC and disaster recovery/backup control center. 

Audit compliance with Critical Infrastructure Protection (CIP) standards, including electronic security perimeters and access controls

 

3.4. Human Resources & Competence

  • Assess staffing levels, skill sets, and training programs for operators and engineers.
  • Evaluate human factors, control room ergonomics, and mental workload. 
  •  Identify gaps in national energy policies or grid codes that hinder modern operations.
  • Evaluate the technical competency of operators in handling advanced grid planning and simulation tools.

 

3.5. Environmental & Social Safeguards

  • Assess current energy use, and waste management practices at NCC and
  • Evaluate energy-efficient technologies, waste reduction strategies and sustainable procurement practices aligned with Fiji’s National laws and Good International Industry Practice.
  • Assess infrastructure capacity for adequate disability inclusion and gender-based rest rooms/ablution facility.

4. Methodology

The consultant is expected to carry out the following as part of the Gap Analysis:

  1. Conduct Desktop Review: Review existing documentation (grid codes, annual reports, previous audits, processes & procedures).
  2. Stakeholder Consultations: Conduct interviews with NCC operators, management, IT, Telecom/SCADA staff.
  3. Site Visits: Perform physical inspection of the control room, hardware, and backup facilities.
  4. Review of current Grid Code
  5. Benchmarking: Compare findings against international best practices (e.g., IEEE, IEC, ENTSO-E). 
  1. Key Deliverables

The outputs expected during and at the end of this consultancy are specified below

  • Gap Analysis Report (Inception report, Draft, and Final) will be prepared to cover the following:
    • Current State Description and functionality
    • Desired Future State Definition and functionality
    • Gap Identification (Technical, Procedural, Human).
    • Explicit mapping of current vs. desired "To-Be" states, categorized by risk level.
    • Modernized Roadmap, Action Plan and Budget: Prioritized recommendations with estimated timelines and cost implications. 
    • Determine if the existing building will be able to cater for the proposed upgrades
  • Reviewed Grid Code Document
  • Procurement Strategy and Draft Bidding Documents will be prepared to cover the following:
    • Assessment report to recommend the appropriate procurement strategy; and
    • Draft bidding documents following above procurement strategy, in consultation with EFL.

6. Timeline

7. Required Expertise

The consultancy firm should be shown to have expertise in the following areas:

 

7.1. Power Systems Automation & SCADA/EMS Specialist

This core expert evaluates the existing NCC and defines the future-state operational technology.

  • SCADA/EMS/DMS Expertise: Deep knowledge of Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition, Energy Management Systems, and Distribution Management Systems.
  • Interoperability & Protocols: Mastery of legacy and modern utility communication protocols (IEC 60870-5-101/104, DNP3, and IEC 61850 for substation automation).
  • Grid Hierarchy: Experience managing control boundaries down to the 11kV feeder breaker level to ensure distribution grid visibility.

 

7.2. Power Systems Protection & Telecommunications Engineer

This domain ensures that control signals travel safely, reliably, and instantaneously across Fiji's geographical terrain.

  • Substation Integration: Expertise in integrating diverse thermal and hydro power stations with central SCADA.
  • Utility Telecommunications: Experience with power line carrier (PLC), fiber optic networks (OPGW), microwave links, and cellular fallback systems.
  • Protection Coordination: Understanding how modern EMS upgrades interact with existing line and transformer protection schemes.

 

7.3. Grid Code & Regulatory Specialist

This expert translates the technical capabilities of the new NCC into legal and operational compliance frameworks.

  • Grid Code Compliance: Experience drafting or reviewing national Grid Codes, specifically for small, isolated island grids with high hydro penetration.
  • Ancillary Services: Defining rules for frequency control, voltage regulation, and spinning reserves relevant to Fiji's power mix.
  • Renewable Integration: Knowledge of technical requirements for grid-connected solar, wind, or battery storage (BESS) into an existing grid code.

 

7.4. Cyber Security (OT/Critical Infrastructure) Specialist

Modernizing an NCC introduces digital vulnerabilities that must be mitigated from day one.

  • Operational Technology (OT) Security: Specific expertise in securing industrial control systems, distinct from standard corporate IT.
  • International Standards: Alignment of procurement requirements with global benchmarks like NERC CIP, ISO 27001, or IEC 62443.

 

7.5. International Procurement & Bidding Expert

This specialist converts the technical GAP analysis into an actionable, legally binding international tender.

  • MDB Procurement Rules: Deep familiarity with multilateral development bank frameworks (such as the Asian Development Bank (ADB) or World Bank), which frequently finance critical infrastructure updates for Energy Fiji Limited (EFL).
  • FIDIC / Turnkey Contracts: Expertise in drafting EPC (Engineering, Procurement, and Construction) or turnkey contracts for complex software and hardware integration.
  • SLA Drafting: Crafting long-term Service Level Agreements (SLAs) for software patches, system maintenance, and vendor support.

procnotices.notice_text:
AVIS A MANIFESTATION D’INTERET RELATIF AU RECRUTEMENT D’UN CONSULTANT INDIVIDUEL POUR L'ELABORATION DE TROIS (03) RAPPORTS SECTORIELS D'EVALUATION DE LA PERFORMANCE DES PROGRAMMES BUDGETAIRES

Avis N° : ________/2026/MEF/PGEDS/SPM du ___________________

Pays : République du Bénin

 Nom du Projet : Programme de Gouvernance Economique pour la Délivrance des Services (PGEDS)

Numéro du Crédit : IDA N°73570-BJ

Référence : STEP : BJ-USMEF-531669-CS-INDV / SIGMAP : PI_PGEDS_120279

 

  1. Le Gouvernement du Bénin a reçu un financement de l’Association Internationale de Développement (AID) pour couvrir le coût du Programme de Gouvernance Economique pour la Délivrance des Services (PGEDS) et, a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ces fonds pour effectuer des paiements au titre du marché relatif au recrutement d’un consultant individuel pour l'élaboration de trois (03) rapports sectoriels d'évaluation de la performance des programmes budgétaires.
  2. Les services à fournir par le consultant (personne physique) visent principalement à améliorer l’efficacité du cycle de gestion budgétaire des programmes des secteurs de l’éducation, de la santé et des infrastructures. A ce titre, le consultant devra de façon spécifique (i) améliorer l’efficacité et l’efficience des dépenses publiques d’investissements dans les 03 secteurs : éducation, santé et infrastructures ; (ii) renforcer la transparence et la redevabilité dans la gestion des ressources publiques allouées aux trois (03) secteurs évalués ; et (iii) orienter la prise de décision pour améliorer les processus de planification, d’exécution et de suivi des programmes budgétaires dans les trois secteurs.
  3. La durée prévisionnelle de la mission est de six (06) mois à compter de la date inscrite dans l’ordre de service de démarrage.
  4. Le Coordonnateur du Programme de Gouvernance Economique pour la Délivrance des Services (PGEDS), Autorité Contractante, invite par la présente sollicitation de manifestation d’intérêt, les consultants individuels (personne physique) admissibles à présenter leur candidature pour fournir les services décrits ci-dessus.
  5. 5. A ce titre, les consultants intéressés doivent fournir les informations indiquant qu’ils sont qualifiés pour exécuter les services (références concernant l’exécution de contrats similaires). Les consultants devront fournir les preuves relatives à leurs expériences (attestations de bonne fin d’exécution) et tout autre document jugé nécessaire. L'ensemble des documents constitutifs du dossier de manifestation d'intérêt doivent être rédigés en français et tout document rédigé dans une autre langue doit être accompagné d'une traduction certifiée conforme en français. En cas de divergence d'interprétation, la version française fera foi.
  6. 6. Le consultant individuel sera sélectionné par la méthode de « Sélection de Consultant Individuel » décrite aux paragraphes 7.34 et suivant du Règlement sur la passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale en date de juillet 2016 révisé en septembre 2025. A l’issue de l’évaluation des manifestations d’intérêt, le consultant présentant le meilleur niveau de qualification et d’expérience en rapport avec la mission sera invité à soumettre une proposition technique et financière.
  7. L’attention des consultants individuels intéressés est attirée sur les paragraphes 3.13, 3.15 et 3.16 de la Section III du Règlement sur la passation des marchés de la Banque mondiale qui décrivent la politique de la Banque en matière de conflits d’intérêts.
  8. Les manifestations d’intérêt rédigées en langue française et en quatre (04) exemplaires (1 original et 3 copies), portant la mention « Recrutement d’un consultant individuel pour l'élaboration de trois (03) rapports sectoriels d'évaluation de la performance des programmes budgétaires » seront déposées physiquement, à compter de la date de publication du présent avis jusqu’au _____________________ à 10 heures précises GMT + 1 (heure de Cotonou) au plus tard, au Secrétariat particulier du PGEDS sis à l’adresse ci-dessous. Toutefois, les consultants situés hors du territoire béninois peuvent transmettre leur manifestation d'intérêt par courrier électronique à l'adresse mail ci-dessous.

Les plis seront ouverts le _______________________ à 10 heures 30 min GMT+1 (heure de Cotonou) dans la salle de réunion du PGEDS en présence des consultants ou de leurs représentants qui désirent y assister.

Des informations complémentaires et les termes de références peuvent être obtenues auprès du Secrétariat particulier du PGEDS à l’adresse ci-dessous, les jours ouvrés, de 08 heures à 12 heures 30 minutes, et de 14 heures à 17 heures 30 minutes GMT+1 (heure de Cotonou). 

  1. L’adresse à laquelle il est fait référence est :

Quartier Awhanlèko, en venant de EREVAN vers le carrefour Fidjrossè Fin Pavé, dans la 2ème rue à gauche, après la salle de Gym Wellness Fitness Center, 2ème villa Blanche à gauche. 

Tél : 01 40 20 01 46 / 01 40 20 03 21

Courriel : procurement.gouvernanceplus@finances.bj

  1. Les critères d’évaluation des manifestations d’intérêt se présentent comme suit :

N°

Critères/Sous-critères

Note sur 100 points

Documentation à fournir

1

Qualifications générales du consultant

20

 

1.1

Diplôme

Avoir au minimum un BAC+5 en économie ou en planification : 10 points

La note zéro (0) sera attribuée à tout consultant ayant fourni un diplôme :

  • de niveau inférieur à celui exigé ou
  • dans un domaine autre que celui demandé

10

1.2

Années d’expériences professionnelles

Justifier d’au moins cinq (5) ans d’expériences professionnelles en planification, suivi-évaluation au sein de Projets / Programmes, Ministère ou structure parapublique : 10 points (A raison de deux (2) points par année d’expérience)

10

Le nombre d’année d’expérience sera déterminé en tenant compte de la plus ancienne expérience en planification, suivi-évaluation au sein de Projets / Programmes, Ministère ou structure parapublique prouvée par le consultant. Les preuves à fournir sont les copies des attestations de bonne fin d’exécution appuyées des pages de garde et de signature des contrats correspondants (Copies simples)

2

Expériences spécifiques du Consultant

80

 

2.1

Avoir réalisé au moins cinq (05) missions d’évaluation de la performance de politiques, stratégies ou Programme de développement publiques au plan national ou international : 50 points (8 points par mission pour un total de 5 missions)

40

Le consultant doit fournir la liste des références techniques en lien avec la présente mission.

Chacune des missions devra être accompagnée de :

  • une fiche descriptive conformément au modèle joint à l’AMI et
  • des preuves (Copies des attestations de bonne fin d’exécution accompagnées des extraits des contrats (page de garde et de signature)) et tout autre document jugé nécessaire par le consultant.

2.2

Avoir réalisé trois (03) missions d’élaboration de rapports sectoriels d’évaluation/ d’analyse de la performance au profit des structures de l’administration publique ou des organisations internationales : 30 points (10 points par mission pour un total de 3 missions)

30

2.3

Justifier d’expérience en matière de gestion des finances publiques, notamment sur les secteurs de l’éducation, de la santé et des infrastructures : 6 points (2 points pour une expérience dans le secteur de l’éducation, 2 points pour une expérience dans le secteur de la santé, 2 points pour une expérience dans le secteur des infrastructures)

6

2.4

Justifier d’une forte capacité à exploiter des bases de données budgétaires, à produire des indicateurs clés et à interpréter des données financières : 4 points (2 points par mission pour un total de 2 missions)

4

Total

100

 

NB :

  • En cas d’égalité de points, le consultant ayant réalisé plus de missions d’élaboration de rapports sectoriels d’évaluation/ d’analyse de la performance au profit des structures de l’administration publique ou des organisations internationales sera retenu. En cas d’égalité persistante, il sera retenu le consultant ayant réalisé plus de missions d’évaluation de la performance de politiques, stratégies ou Programme de développement publiques au plan national ou international.
  • Ne seront pas prises en compte pour les expériences spécifiques (critère 2) les missions réalisées au profit des entreprises privées, ONG, associations, fondations et fédérations …) ainsi que les missions en cours d’exécution.
  • Les attestations de bonne fin d’exécution ou de service fait accompagnées des extraits de contrat (page de garde et de signature) sont les moyens de preuve à fournir pour justifier chaque mission réalisée. A cet effet, les consultants sont invités à produire des attestations indiquant la période de mise en œuvre effective des prestations. A défaut, la date de signature de l’attestation sera considérée comme date de référence selon le cas.

Le programme se réserve le droit de demander des documents complémentaires en vue de disposer des preuves exhaustives avant la validation de chaque mission.

  • Les consultants sont invités à renseigner le formulaire de fiche descriptive ci-joint et de fournir toutes les informations demandées et autres informations si nécessaires, afin de garantir une meilleure appréciation de leur manifestation d’intérêt.

procnotices.notice_text:
Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

 

Unleashing the Blue Economy of the Caribbean (UBEC)

 

CREDIT no. 7089-VC

 

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Assignment Title: STRENGTHENING AN ENABLING ENVIRONMENT FOR SEAMOSS AQUACULTURE AND VALUE-ADDED BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT.

Reference No: SVGUBEC-C-IC-24

The Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines (GoSVG) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the SVG Unleashing the Blue Economy of the Caribbean (UBEC) project and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Government of SVG has established a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the Ministry of Tourism, Civil Aviation, and Sustainable Development (MoTCASD) responsible for implementing the UBEC project national-level activities and coordinating with relevant ministries.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include; to strengthen Saint Vincent and the Grenadines' seamoss sector by assessing its value chain, building capacity, and developing a roadmap for growth utilizing best practices across the value chain. Specifically, the consultancy will:

  1. Assess constraints and opportunities across the seamoss value chain, including production, processing, marketing, and institutional support systems;
  2. Deliver a structured two-track training programme to strengthen technical, regulatory and business capacity across the seamoss value chain, targeting private sector producers, processors and cooperatives, and public sector Fisheries Services and extension personnel.;
  3. Develop a pragmatic, investment-ready business case and strategic roadmap for scaling the seamoss sector; and
  4. Facilitate knowledge transfer and coordination among public-sector institutions, producers, and private-sector stakeholders.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://procurement.gov.vc/eprocure/index.php/current-bids

The MoTCASD in conjunction with the Central Water and Sewerage Authority (CWSA) now invite eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. A minimum of 5-7 years' professional experience in aquaculture, mariculture, seamoss or related sectors, with a demonstrated track record of delivering comparable assignments in developing country contexts.
  2. At least five years of experience working within the Caribbean region, with knowledge of Eastern Caribbean fisheries and aquaculture institutional frameworks, including the roles of Fisheries Services, CRFM, and relevant regional bodies.
  3. A degree (Bachelor's or higher) in aquaculture, fisheries, marine sciences, or a closely related field, with additional training or demonstrated experience in business management, value chain development, or marketing.
  4. Demonstrated expertise in value chain analysis, food safety management (HACCP and GMP), post-harvest handling, and export market compliance for fisheries or aquaculture products.
  5. Proven capacity to design and deliver effective training programmes for diverse audiences, including small-scale producers, cooperatives, and government extension personnel.
  6. Experience in business case development, investment analysis, and strategic planning for aquaculture or blue economy sectors.
  7. Demonstrated ability to engage effectively with a wide range of stakeholders, including government agencies, multilateral development partners (such as the World Bank, FAO, CRFM, and UNDP), private sector actors, cooperatives, NGOs, and community-based organisations.
  8. Knowledge of climate-smart and climate-resilient aquaculture technologies appropriate to small island developing states.
  9. Excellent written and oral communication skills in English, including the ability to prepare high-quality technical reports, policy documents, and strategic plans.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 [revised November 2017, August 2018 and November 2020, September 2023, February 2025] (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Individual Consulting method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 09:00 to 16:00 hours (Local time).

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by October 8, 2026:

- Lot n°2 : Piste Kigusu-Kavumu et pont Kayongozi (CNK-02), Piste Kirambi-Kigusu-Busoro-Kayongozi (RYG-02) et Pont reliant les collines Kayenzi et Nkoyoyo (MYN-02) ;
dans les communes de Ngozi, Tangara, Kiremba, Ruyigi et Muyinga.

Référence STEP : BI-TURIKUMWE PIU-549328-CS-QCBS

Date : le 02/09/2026

1. Le Gouvernement de la République du Burundi a reçu un financement de la Banque mondiale d’un montant de 60 millions de Dollars des Etats Unis d’Amériques pour financer le Projet  de Développement Communautaire Intégré au Burundi «PRODECI-TURIKUMWE» et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie du montant de ce Don pour effectuer les paiements au titre du contrat suivant: « les Etudes techniques y compris études séparées d'EIES et Surveillance et Contrôle des travaux de réhabilitation des pistes et ponts du Lot 1 (Pistes Gacekeri-Rugori-Caga (NGZ-05), Kavumu-Rwahirwa-Zone Makaba (NGZ-06), Nyarugunda-Ruyange (NGZ-07 et TNG-01) et Ruhama-Rurama (KRM-02)) et du Lot 2 (Piste Kigusu-Kavumu et pont Kayongozi (CNK-02), Piste Kirambi-Kigusu-Busoro-Kayongozi (RYG-02) et Pont reliant les collines Kayenzi et Nkoyoyo (MYN-02)), dans les communes de Ngozi, Tangara, Kiremba, Ruyigi et Muyinga»

2. Les services de consultants (« les services ») comprennent :

a. Pour les ETUDES TECHNIQUES Y COMPRIS LES ETUDES SEPAREES D'EIES/PGES

le relevé des itinéraires, l’évaluation environnementale et sociale et les diligences environnementales et sociales adéquates, soit l’EIES assortie de son PGES ou PGES et éventuellement la production des Plans particuliers Environnementaux et sociaux selon le niveau des risques environnementaux et sociaux, recherche des matériaux (en y impliquant le Laboratoire National du Bâtiment et des Travaux Publics « LNBTP» pour les essais), Avant-Projet Détaillé, Propositions pour l’entretien des pistes et Préparation du Dossier d’Appel d’Offres (DAO) pour l’exécution des travaux.

 

b. Pour la SURVEILLANCE ET CONTRÔLE DES TRAVAUX DE RÉHABILITATION DES PISTES ET PONTS DU LOT 1 ET DU LOT 2

La mission consiste à assurer les prestations de maîtrise d’œuvre comprenant la supervision et le contrôle des travaux d’infrastructures routières, le suivi des mesures environnementales, sociales, hygiènes et sécurité ainsi que la lutte contre les VGB pour le compte des communes de NGOZI, TANGARA, KIREMBA, RUYIGI et MUYINGA.

Les termes de références détaillés pour cette mission peuvent être obtenus à l’adresse indiquée ci-dessous.

3. L’Unité de Gestion du Projet PRODECI-TURIKUMWE invite pour le moment les Cabinets de consultants éligibles («Consultants») à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les Services. Les consultants intéressés doivent fournir des informations démontrant qu'ils possèdent les qualifications et l'expérience requises pour exécuter les services.

Le Cabinet recherché doit disposer des capacités techniques (équipements, matériel, personnel, etc.) et financières suffisantes pour l’accomplissement de la mission.

Les critères pour l’établissement de la liste restreinte sont :

Pour les deux phases, chaque Consultant (Bureau) recherché est un bureau spécialisé dans la conduite des études techniques, environnementales et sociales et dans la surveillance et contrôle des travaux des routes et pistes. Il devra justifier d’une expérience avérée d’au moins 10 ans dans le domaine et avoir :

  • Expérience générale : Avoir réalisée au moins trois (3) études techniques de pistes ou de routes dont trois (3) d’EIES durant les 10 dernières années ;
  • Expérience spécifique : avoir réalisée avec succès au moins 2 études techniques et d’EIES de pistes ou de routes pour des tronçons de 30 km et plus et des ponts durant les 10 dernières années.  
  • Spécialisé dans la conduite (i) des missions de surveillance et le contrôle et (ii) le suivi environnemental et social avec un accent particulier sur l’EAS-HS de ce type d’infrastructures routières.
  • Justifier d’une expérience avérée d’au moins 5 ans dans le domaine routier
  • Avoir réalisé au moins trois (3) missions réussies de surveillance et contrôle des travaux routiers et construction de ponts durant les 10 dernières années ;

 

NB : Les missions similaires réalisées doivent être accompagnées des preuves de réalisation.

Les experts clés ne seront pas évalués au stade de la présélection.

Aucun bureau ne sera attributaire de plus d’un lot

NB : Le PRODECI-TURIKUMWE se réserve le droit d’écarter de la liste restreinte tout cabinet pour lequel il dispose d’éléments documentés établissant, au cours des cinq (5) dernières années, un manquement avéré aux délais contractuels de remise des livrables ou une exécution jugée non satisfaisante par le PRODECI, dûment constatée et notifiée au cabinet.

4. L’attention des Consultants intéressés est attirée sur la section III, paragraphes, 3.14, 3.16 et 3.17 du « Règlement de Passation des Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement de Projets d’Investissement (FPI) datant de juillet 2016, révisé en novembre 2017, Août 2018, novembre 2020, septembre 2023, février et septembre 2025 ». En outre, veuillez-vous référer aux informations spécifiques suivantes sur les conflits d'intérêts liés à cette mission.

Les Consultants ne peuvent être engagés pour des missions qui seraient incompatibles avec leurs obligations présentes ou passées envers d’autres clients, ou qui risqueraient de les mettre dans l’impossibilité de remplir leur mandat au mieux des intérêts de l’Etat du Burundi.

Les consultants ne peuvent être engagés dans les circonstances ci-après :

  1. Aucun Consultant (y compris le personnel et les sous-traitants à son service) ni aucun prestataire affilié (qui le contrôle directement ou indirectement, qu’il contrôle lui-même ou qui est placé sous le contrôle commun) ne peut être engagé pour une mission qui, par sa nature, crée un conflit d’intérêt avec une autre de ses missions ;
  2. Aucun Consultant (y compris le personnel et les sous-consultants à son service) ni aucun prestataire affilié (qui le contrôle directement ou indirectement, qu’il contrôle lui-même ou qui est placé sous un contrôle commun) ne peut être engagé pour une mission qui, par sa nature, crée un conflit d’intérêts avec une autre de ses missions ;
  3. Les Consultants (y compris les experts, le personnel et les sous-consultants à leur service) qui ont une relation professionnelle ou familiale étroite avec tout cadre de l’Etat du Burundi, de l’organisme d’exécution du Projet, d’un bénéficiaire d’une fraction de financement de la Banque mondiale ou toute autre partie représentant l’Etat du Burundi ou agissant en son nom qui participe directement ou indirectement à tout segment :
  1. de la préparation des Termes de référence de la mission ;
  2. du processus de sélection pour le contrat ; ou
  3. de la supervision du contrat,  ne peuvent être attributaire d’un contrat, sauf si le conflit résultant de ladite relation a été réglé d’une manière que la Banque juge satisfaisante tout au long du processus de sélection ou de l’exécution du contrat.

5. Les cabinets de consultants peuvent s'associer avec d'autres cabinets pour améliorer leurs qualifications, mais doivent indiquer clairement si l'association se présente sous la forme d'une coentreprise et / ou d'une sous-traitance. Dans le cas d'une coentreprise, tous les partenaires de la coentreprise seront conjointement et solidairement responsables de la totalité du contrat, s'ils sont sélectionnés.

6. Un consultant sera sélectionné conformément à la méthode de sélection fondée sur la qualité et le coût (SFQC) énoncée dans le Règlement sur la Passation de Marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le Financement des Projets d’Investissement (FPI) version de Juillet 2016, révisée en novembre 2017, Août 2018, novembre 2020, septembre 2023, février et septembre 2025.

7. De plus amples informations peuvent être obtenues tous les jours ouvrables à l'adresse ci-dessous de 9 heures à 17 heures (heures de Bujumbura) du lundi au jeudi et de 9 heures à 14 heures (heures de Bujumbura) les vendredi.

8. Les manifestations d'intérêt doivent être livrées par écrit à l'adresse ci-dessous (en personne, par courrier, ou par e-mail) avant le 21/09/2026 au plus tard à 10 heures avec les mentions :

« Manifestation d’Intérêt pour la Sélection d’un Bureau pour les Etudes techniques y compris études séparées d'EIES et Surveillance et Contrôle des travaux de réhabilitation des pistes et ponts du Lot 1 (Pistes Gacekeri-Rugori-Caga (NGZ-05), Kavumu-Rwahirwa-Zone Makaba (NGZ-06), Nyarugunda-Ruyange (NGZ-07 et TNG-01) et Ruhama-Rurama (KRM-02)) et du Lot 2 (Piste Kigusu-Kavumu et pont Kayongozi (CNK-02), Piste Kirambi-Kigusu-Busoro-Kayongozi (RYG-02) et Pont reliant les collines Kayenzi et Nkoyoyo (MYN-02)), dans les communes de Ngozi, Tangara, Kiremba, Ruyigi et Muyinga».

procnotices.notice_text:
Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

Unleashing the Blue Economy of the Caribbean (UBEC)

CREDIT no. 7089-VC

REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST

(CONSULTING SERVICES – FIRMS SELECTION)

Consultancy Services for Site Assessment, Design, and Supervision of Upgrading Investments In Harvest and Post-Harvest Fisheries Infrastructure: Calliaqua Fisheries Centre.

Reference No: SVGUBEC-C-QCBS-8

The Government of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines (GoSVG) has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the SVG Unleashing the Blue Economy of the Caribbean (UBEC) project, and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The Government of SVG (GoSVG) has established a Project Implementation Unit (PIU) at the Ministry of Tourism, Civil Aviation, and Sustainable Development (MoTCASD) responsible for implementing the UBEC project national-level activities and coordinating with relevant ministries.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include; to provide the Government of SVG and the UBEC Project Implementation Unit (PIU) with the technical, financial, and operational evidence base required to make sound, sustainable investment decisions for the Calliaqua Fisheries Centre and, based on these decisions, to execute detailed design and construction supervision to the standard required for a durable, well-maintained public fisheries asset.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: https://procurement.gov.vc/eprocure/index.php/current-bids 

The MoTCASD, in conjunction with the Ministry of Fisheries, Marine and Land Conservation and Climate Resilience, now invite eligible consulting firms (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services.

The shortlisting criteria are:

  1. The consulting firm should have expertise in fisheries infrastructure development, assessment and rehabilitation, strong knowledge of marine and coastal engineering principles, proficiency in technical specifications writing including Bills of Quantities and Procurement documentation, and a demonstrated understanding of renewable energy integration in fisheries infrastructure.
  2. The team shall include professionals with experience in engineering design, the conduction of root cause analyses, and stakeholder engagement and training.

Key Experts will not be evaluated at the shortlisting stage.

The attention of interested Consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” July 2016 [revised November 2017, August 2018 and November 2020, September 2023, February 2025] (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest.

Consultants may associate with other firms to enhance their qualifications but should indicate clearly whether the association is in the form of a joint venture and/or a sub-consultancy. In the case of a joint venture, all the partners in the joint venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire contract, if selected.

A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Quality and Cost-Based Selection (QCBS) method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

Further information can be obtained at the address below during office hours 09:00 to 16:00 hours (Local time).

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by mail, or by e-mail) by October 14, 2026, at 4:00PM local time

 

Dr. Donna Joyette-Bascombe

Permanent Secretary

Ministry of Tourism, Civil Aviation and Sustainable Development

2nd Floor NIS Building

Upper Bay Street, Kingstown

Saint Vincent and the Grenadines

Copy to:  sobwocha.ubecsvg@gmail.com, michelemapp71@gmail.com.

The Government of Lao PDR (GOL) is implementing the Reducing Rural Poverty and Malnutrition Project II (RRPMP II) (P178883) from 2024 to 2029 with financing from the World Bank (WB).  The RRPMP II will implement a nutrition-sensitive social protection program or a Conditional Cash Transfer (CCT) Program to address issues of poverty and malnutrition and develop and implement mechanism to ensure multi-sectoral coordination, planning, monitoring, and evaluation of the nutrition convergence approach: the Reducing Rural Poverty and Malnutrition Project. The Project Management Unit (PMU) for the RRPMP II is the Department of Rural Development and Poverty Reduction (DRP) within the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment (MAE) in Vientiane Capital, which has overall responsibility for operational aspects of the project at the national and sub-national level including contract administration, financial management, procurement, and monitoring and evaluation, as well as overseeing implementation. 

 

RRPMP II intend to engage a full-time IT Consultant will provide technical operational support in the planning, design, development, integration, security, and maintenance of ICT solutions, ensuring efficient and reliable data management, as well as long-term system sustainability through capacity building for government officers for the national poverty assessment of new upgrading of wellbeing criteria and development criteria decree.

 

RRPMP II now invites eligible individual consultant to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested candidate should provide information (CV, Expression of Interest, other supporting information, if any) demonstrating that she/he has the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. In order to qualify for this position, the candidates shall meet the following experience and competence requirements:

 

  • At least Bachelor’s decree or higher in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or a related field. A master’s decree (MCA/ME/M.Tech or equivalent) is preferred.
  • At least five (5) years of professional experience in IT systems analysis, software development oversight, ICT infrastructure, or MIS implementation.
  • At least three (3) years’ experience of national poverty assessment and Statistical data analysis
  • Proven experience working as a Statistical data and System Analyst in at least one within public sector organizations.
  • Strong knowledge of database management systems (e.g., PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server), programming frameworks, and integration APIs.
  • Experience with mobile data collection platforms (e.g., CS Pro, ODK, Kobo, CAPI, Google Forms, Android, etc.).
  • Strong data analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills (English and Lao languages).
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet tight deadlines

 

The attention of interested consultants is drawn to Section III, paragraphs, 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” 4th edition of November 2020 (“Procurement Regulations”), setting forth the World Bank’s policy on conflict of interest. A Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method set out in the Procurement Regulations.

 

Expressions of interest must be delivered in a written form to the address below (in person, or by e-mail) by 18 September 2026, 16:00 o’clock Lao time (submissions via email are also acceptable). Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

 

Attention: Vongsavanh Vongkaysone,Ph.D. Deputy Director General, DRP – MAE

Email: rrpmp2023@gmail.com with Cc: phonesavanh.tms@gmail.com and insonesaysombath@yahoo.com

Address: Department of Rural Development and Poverty Reduction, Ministry of Agriculture and Environment, Ban Sibounheuang, Chanthabouly District, inside the Prime Minister complex office, Vientiane Capital, Lao P.D.R.

                                         Request for Expressions of Interest

                        Selection of Financial Management Specialist (Individual – National)

                                                 (Package No. SD-32)

1. The Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh has received a credit from the International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Technical Assistance Facility under the Learning Acceleration in Secondary Education (LAISE) Project, being implemented by the Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education (DSHE), and intends to apply part of the proceeds of this credit to engage the services of a Financial Management Specialist (Individual – National).

2. The scope of the consulting services includes, but is not limited to, supporting the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) in ensuring effective, efficient, and compliant financial management of the Project in accordance with the requirements of the World Bank and the Government of Bangladesh (GoB). The detailed Terms of Reference (ToR) are available at www.dshe.gov.bd or may be obtained from the address provided below. The duration of the assignment will be approximately twenty-four (24) months, and the assignment is expected to commence in November 2026. 

3. The required qualifications and experience for the assignment are as follows:

a) Education Qualification:

  •  M. Com/ MBA in Accounting/ Finance and related subjects.
  • Professional accounting qualifications such as Association of Chartered Certified Accountants (ACCA), Chartered Public Finance Accountant (CPFA), FCA (Fellow Chartered Accountant) or FCMA (Fellow Cost and Management Accountant) will be an added advantage.

 b) Experience:

  • 12 years of professional experience in financial management in government or semi-government institutions, or with international development partners implementing development projects, including 8 years of experience as a Financial Management Specialist or in a similar role under World Bank–financed projects and/or other development partner–funded projects or programs.
  • Extensive knowledge of Government budgeting, fund release, and reporting requirements.
  • In-depth knowledge of IDA/World Bank financial management and disbursement procedures.

 4. The Directorate of Secondary and Higher Education (DSHE) now invites eligible Individual Consultants (“Consultants”) to indicate their interest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should submit information demonstrating that they possess the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. Such information shall include a detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV), descriptions of similar assignments undertaken, experience in comparable positions and conditions, educational qualifications, professional certifications (if any), and any other information relevant to the assignment.

5. The attention of interested Consultants is drawn, in particular, to:

 (i) Section III, Paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised November 2020), setting forth the World Bank's policy on Conflict of Interest; and

(ii) Section III, Paragraphs 3.21 to 3.24 of the same Procurement Regulations, setting forth the World Bank's policy on Eligibility, including the exceptional conditions under which government officials and civil servants of the Borrower's country may be engaged as consultants under consulting contracts in the Borrower's country.

6. The interested Consultant shall submit, together with the Expression of Interest, a signed declaration confirming that he/she:

  •  has no actual, potential, or perceived conflict of interest in accordance with Section III, Paragraphs 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17 of the Procurement Regulations; and
  • agrees to comply with the World Bank's Anti-Corruption Guidelines applicable to the assignment.

7. The Individual Consultant will be selected in accordance with the Open Competitive Selection of Individual Consultants method set forth in the World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers (July 2016, revised November 2020) ("Procurement Regulations").

8. Expressions of Interest (EOIs) shall be submitted to the address below by 17:00 hours (BST) on 27 September 2026, either by e-mail, in person, or by mail. The subject line of the e-mail or the top of the sealed envelope shall clearly state: "Expression of Interest (EOI) for Selection of Financial Management Specialist (Package No. SD-32)."

 

(Professor Md. Asaduzzaman)

procnotices.notice_text:
PROJET DE TRANSFORMATION URBAINE ET L’EMPLOI A KINSHASA (KIN LA BELLE)

 

AVIS DE SOLLICITATION DE MANIFESTATIONS D’INTERETS

(SERVICE DE CONSULTANTS INDIVIDUELS)

Recrutement d’un Consultant individuel senior, expert en développement de WATERFRONT, pour l’élaboration de la vision stratégique et l’appui à la préparation du schéma directeur du WATERFRONT de Kinshasa.

 

Secteur                                                                       : Développement urbain

Source de financement                                             : Banque Mondiale – Crédit IDA 7996-ZR

N° d’identification du Projet                                    : P 512210

N° de référence PPM-STEP                                      : ZR-CI-567323-CS-INDV

N° AVIS                                                                    : 047/MITP/CI/KIN LA BELLE/2026

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Le Gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo a reçu un financement de l'Association Internationale pour le Développement (IDA) du Groupe de Banque mondiale, pour préparer le projet de transformation urbaine et l’emploi à Kinshasa (KIN LA BELLE), et a l’intention d’utiliser une partie de ce financement pour le recrutement d’un Consultant individuel senior, expert en développement de WATERFRONT, pour l’élaboration de la vision stratégique et l’appui à la préparation du schéma directeur du WATERFRONT de Kinshasa.

La présente mission a pour objectif d’appuyer le Projet Kin La Belle dans la définition d’une vision stratégique intégrée du waterfront de Kinshasa, articulant l’aménagement des berges, le développement du transport fluvial urbain, la résilience urbaine et la mobilisation des investissements publics et privés, ainsi que dans la préparation du futur Schéma Directeur.

De manière spécifique, la mission vise à :

  • Définir une vision stratégique du waterfront de Kinshasa intégrant, comme principes transversaux, la résilience climatique, la réduction des risques de catastrophe, l’inclusion sociale, la protection des écosystèmes et la valorisation économique des berges ;
  • Etablir les principes clé d’aménagement et d’organisation spatiale des berges, en tenant compte de la sensibilité aux aléas, des zones écologiques à préserver, de l’accessibilité universelle et de l’intégration avec le tissu urbain existant ;
  • Formuler des orientations stratégiques pour le développement d’un transport fluvial sûr, accessible, résilient et intégré au système global de mobilité urbaine, en tenant compte de la variabilité saisonnière des débits, des conditions de navigabilité et de la continuité du service ;
  • Identifier les projets susceptibles d’être développés avec la participation du secteur privé et proposer des orientations préliminaires pour leur structuration en partenariat public-privé, conformément au cadre juridique applicable en République démocratique du Congo ;
  • Appuyer la structuration et la finalisation des Termes de Référence du Schéma Directeur du waterfront, en précisant les objectifs, le périmètre, les composantes techniques, les livrables attendus et les modalités de mise en œuvre ;
  • En collaboration avec le consultant local, identifier et prioriser des projets structurants, des actions à court terme ou « quick wins » et des interventions « sans regret », après analyse de leur faisabilité, de leur exposition aux risques climatiques, sociaux et fonciers, ainsi que de leur potentiel de sécurisation des emprises et d’attraction des investissements.

Les termes de référence complets sont disponibles sur le site de la Cellule Infrastructures www.celluleinfra.org sous l’onglet : « Appel d’offres ».

La durée totale de la mission du consultant est estimée à six (6) mois et demi étalés sur neuf (9) mois. La mission se déroulera à Kinshasa.

La mission sera confiée à un consultant individuel senior disposant d’une expertise confirmée en planification urbaine, en développement de waterfronts et en projets urbains intégrés en lien avec les infrastructures de transport, avec le profil minimum suivant :

  • Avoir un diplôme de niveau Master (Bac+5) ou équivalent en urbanisme et aménagement du territoire, architecture, ingénierie urbaine ou territoriale, géographie urbaine, ou dans tout autre domaine pertinent lié à la planification urbaine et au développement territorial ; Une spécialisation en mobilité urbaine/transport fluvial serait un atout.
  • Justifier d’au moins quinze (15) années d’expérience professionnelle dans les domaines de la planification urbaine, de l’aménagement urbain, de la planification territoriale ou du développement de projets urbains structurants.
  • Avoir réalisé au moins deux (2) missions d’élaboration des schémas directeurs d’urbanisme, de plans stratégiques urbains ou de documents de planification territoriale à l’échelle d’une ville.
  • Avoir réalisé ou contribué de manière significative à au moins deux (2) projets de planification ou d’aménagement de waterfronts ou de berges fluviales ou côtières, intégrant le transport fluvial ainsi que des approches d’adaptation climatique, de réduction des risques ou de solutions fondées sur la nature.
  • Avoir une expérience avérée dans la mise en œuvre de projets financés par des bailleurs de fonds internationaux, tels que la Banque mondiale, l’AFD, la JICA, la Banque africaine de développement ou d’autres institutions similaires.
  • Avoir une bonne maîtrise des outils de cartographie et d’analyse spatiale (SIG), y compris la télédétection, la cartographie des aléas et l’interprétation des données climatiques et environnementales.
  • Avoir une excellente maîtrise du français écrit et oral. La connaissance de l’anglais constitue un atout.

La Cellule Infrastructures invite les Candidats admissibles, Consultants Individuels internationaux, à manifester leur intérêt à fournir les services décrits ci-dessus. Les Candidats potentiels intéressés doivent fournir les informations démontrant qu’ils possèdent les qualifications requises et une expérience pertinente pour l’exécution  des Services (un CV détaillé indiquant l’exécution des prestations analogues, expériences dans des conditions semblables, disponibilité des connaissances nécessaires, une lettre de motivation - 2 pages maximum - expliquant les motivations profondes d’intérêts pour la mission, les qualifications et expériences spécifiques pertinentes et similaires à prendre en compte pour l’examen des expressions d’intérêts en vue de la sélection, etc.).

Il est porté à l’attention des Consultants que les dispositions du paragraphe 3.17 du « Règlement de passation des marchés pour les Emprunteurs sollicitant le financement de projets d’investissement par la Banque Mondiale de Septembre 2025 (Règlement de passation des marchés relatives aux règles de la Banque Mondiale en matière de conflits d’intérêt) sont applicables.

Un Consultant sera sélectionné, suivant la méthode de « Sélection de Consultants Individuels », telle que décrite dans le Règlement de Passation des Marchés susmentionné.

Les Consultants intéressés peuvent obtenir des informations supplémentaires à l’adresse physique ci-dessous de la Cellule Infrastructures, chaque jour ouvrable de 9 heures à 16 heures locales ou à son adresse électronique info@celluleinfra.org.

Les manifestations d’intérêt, écrites en langue française, doivent être déposées à l’adresse ci-dessous en personne, par courrier ou par courrier électronique au plus tard le 22 septembre 2026 à 14h00’ heures locales (TU+1) et porter clairement la mention : AMI n° 047/MITP/CI/KIN LA BELLE/2026 « Recrutement d’un Consultant individuel senior, expert en développement de WATERFRONT, pour l’élaboration de la vision stratégique et l’appui à la préparation du schéma directeur du WATERFRONT de Kinshasa».

Main Types and Quantities of Goods

Equipment including a cell stretch and traction control system, portable multifunctional metabolic measurement instrument, behavioral trajectory tracking and analysis system, and computing cluster servers, as well as related services. 5Potential Bidders should note the provisions of Clause 4 of the Instructions to Bidders concerning eligibility and conflicts of interest. Any Bidder with a conflict of interest shall be deemed ineligible.

6The qualification requirements for Bidders include:

The Bidder shall have sufficient readily available liquid assets, lines of credit, and other financing resources to meet the cash flow requirements for contract performance, taking into account the Bidder’s other ongoing contractual commitments. The minimum requirement shall be RMB 2 million.

procnotices.notice_text:
Special Procurement Notice

Request for Bids

Small Works

(Two-Envelope Bidding Process)

 

Country: Kyrgyz Republic

Employer: Ministry of Emergency Situations of the Kyrgyz Republic within the framework of the "Kyrgyz Republic Resilient Landscape Restoration project" (KG RESILAND)

Project: "Kyrgyz Republic Resilient Landscape Restoration project" (KG RESILAND)

Contract title: Construction of a protective dam on the northern bank of the Gulcha River in the town of Gulcha, Alay District, Osh Region.

Credit No.: 74900-IDA

RFB No: KG/CW/RESILAND/MoES/RF-03/2026-1

Issued on: September 7, 2026

The Kyrgyz Republic has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of the "Kyrgyz Republic Resilient Landscape Restoration project" (KG RESILAND), and intends to apply part of the proceeds toward payments under contracts KG/CW/RESILAND/MoES/RF-03/2026-1 for Construction of a protective dam on the northern bank of the Gulcha River in the town of Gulcha, Alay District, Osh Region.

The Ministry of Emergency Situations of the Kyrgyz Republic now invites sealed Bids from eligible Bidders for: procurement of civil works for construction construction of a protective dam on the northern bank of the Gulcha River in the town of Gulcha, Alay District, Osh Region.

The contract realization period for will be 12 months.

In case of participation, the Bidder shall provide the appropriate License for performing construction and installation work in the field of construction of hydraulic structures of at least level II responsibility (copies), issued by the State Agency for Architecture and Construction and Housing and Communal Services under the Cabinet of Ministers of the Kyrgyz Republic.

Bidding will be conducted through national competitive bidding using Request for Bids (RFB) as specified in the World Bank’s “Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers” issued on July 2016 (“Procurement Regulations”), and is open to all eligible Bidders as defined in the Procurement Regulations.

Interested eligible Bidders may obtain further information from the Project Implementation Unit under the Ministry of Emergency Situations of the Kyrgyz Republic, Deputy Director of the PIU Berbaeva Chinara, e-mail: tender.resiland@gmail.com and inspect the bidding document during office hours from 09-00 to 17:00 hours (Bishkek time) at the address given below.

The bidding document in Russian language may be obtained by interested eligible Bidders upon the submission of a written application to the e-mail: tender.resiland@gmail.com. Documents will be sent through e-mail.

Bids must be delivered to the address below on or before 16-00 hours (Bishkek time) October 07, 2026. Electronic bidding will not be permitted. Late Bids will be rejected. The outer Bid envelopes marked “ORIGINAL BID”, and the inner envelopes marked “TECHNICAL PART” will be publicly opened in the presence of the Bidders’ designated representatives and anyone who chooses to attend, on 16:00 hrs. (Bishkek time) October 07, 2026 at the address below.

All envelopes marked “FINANCIAL PART” shall remain unopened and will be held in safe custody of the Employer until the second public Bid opening.

All Bids must be accompanied by a Bid-Securing Declaration;

Attention is drawn to the Procurement Regulations requiring the Borrower to disclose information on the successful bidder’s beneficial ownership, as part of the Contract Award Notice, using the Beneficial Ownership Disclosure Form as included in the bidding document.

procnotices.project_name: Eswatini Youth Employment Opportunities Project
procnotices.bid_description: Recruitment of Value Chains Specialist
procnotices.contact_address: EWADE Building - Along MR8, Siphofaneni
procnotices.contact_organization: Eswatini Water and Agricultural Development Enterprise
procnotices.notice_text:
VALUE CHAINS SPECIALIST

Reporting directly to the Project Manager, the Value Chains Specialist will lead and coordinate interventions that strengthen agricultural and agribusiness value chains, promote youth engagement and enhance income earning opportunities through improved production, marketing, access to finance and related services.

 

KEY PERFORMANCE AREAS:

  • Develop value chain development strategies and action plans focusing on inclusivity, sustainability, and market orientation.
  • Facilitate the integration of youth into agricultural value chains including both on-farm and off-farm activities.
  • Strengthen linkages among value chain actors, including producers, aggregators, input suppliers, processors, buyers, extension services and financial institutions.
  • Conduct selection and provide oversight to training providers, ensuring that youth receive practical, market-relevant technical and business skills.
  • Facilitate community sensitization and awareness and mobilization campaigns to attract and prepare youth beneficiaries.
  • Coordinate the recruitment, selection and enrolment of youth beneficiaries into value chain and enterprise programs.
  • Support the design and delivery of training programs on mindset change, value chain development, agribusiness management and entrepreneurship.
  • Support the clustering of youth enterprises to promote economies of scale, collective marketing and improved access to services.
  • Support youth-led enterprises with seed capital disbursement and ensure effective utilization through mentoring and follow-up.
  • Establish and strengthen market linkages between youth agripreneurs and buyers, processors and exporters.
  • Establish and strengthen market linkages between youth agripreneurs and buyers, processors and exporters.
  • Facilitate partnerships with private sector entities to support off-take agreements, contract farming and supply chain inclusion.
  • Support youth to participate in trade fairs, exhibitions and B2B events to increase market visibility.
  • Promote the development of ancillary and off-farm youth-led businesses (e.g. input supply, post-harvest handling, logistics, agroprocessing/cottage industries and digital services).
  • Work closely with the M&E Officer to track progress and outcomes of value chain interventions using defined indicators.
  • Compile monthly, quarterly, semi-annual and annual project progress reports.
  • Document lessons learned, success stories and best practices from value chain initiatives.
  • Contribute to knowledge exchange and policy dialogue on youth integration into value chains.

 

EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES:   

  • Bachelor’s degree in Agribusiness, Agricultural Economics, Agronomy, Animal Sciences, Rural Development, or a related field. Master’s degree preferred.
  • Minimum of 7 years’ experience in value chain development, agribusiness promotion or youth entrepreneurship support.
  • Proven experience working on international donor-funded projects. Experience with World Bank financed projects is an added advantage.
  • Strong understanding of agricultural production systems, market systems development (MSD) and private sector engagement.
  • Demonstrated ability to facilitate multi-stakeholder partnerships and coordinate across public and private sectors.
  • Experience in training, mentoring and capacity building of youth and community-based organizations.
  • Good knowledge of Eswatini’s agricultural landscape and youth development context
  • High level of integrity

Conformar el repositorio físico y digital del EIP.

Los Términos de Referencia detallados para la presente consultoría se podrán examinar en la página web: https://www.mit.gob.ec/postulaciones/

El Ministerio de Infraestructura y Tecnología (MIT), invita a los profesionales interesados a manifestar su interés en la consultoría arriba mencionada. Los consultores interesados deberán proporcionar información que demuestre que tienen las calificaciones requeridas y la experiencia relevante para llevar a cabo la consultoría.

Los criterios para la selección son los siguientes:

Nivel Académico: Se requiere título de tercer nivel.

Experiencia General: Acreditar al menos tres (3) años de experiencia profesional general, contabilizada a partir de la emisión del título universitario. Conocimiento y manejo de Quipux.

Experiencia Específica: Acreditar experiencia profesional específica de al menos un (1) año como asistente administrativo/a.

Habilidades: Coordinación de actividades con grupos multidisciplinarios de las instituciones involucradas en el proceso del trabajo a realizar, trabajo bajo presión, comunicación y poder de negociación.

Los profesionales con perfiles que más se ajusten a lo requerido serán entrevistados.

Los profesionales interesados en participar deberán enviar sus expresiones de interés acompañadas de una carta que especifique el cargo y número de referencia del proceso para el que está aplicando, junto con su hoja de vida actualizada que contenga las calificaciones para realizar el trabajo mencionado, y una copia de los títulos y diplomas obtenidos.

Las expresiones de interés se presentarán por escrito, o podrán ser enviadas a los correos electrónicos: documentosbm@mit.gob.ec; o, entregadas en físico hasta el día 10 de septiembre de 2026, en la dirección del Ministerio de Infraestructura y Tecnología, Subsecretaría de la Infraestructura del Transporte piso 17, en el horario de 09h00 a 16h00hs.

procnotices.contact_address: EWADE Building - Along MR8, Siphofaneni
procnotices.contact_organization: Eswatini Water and Agricultural Development Enterprise
procnotices.notice_text:
MONITORING AND EVALUATION OFFICER

Reporting directly to the Project Manager, the Monitoring and Evaluation Officer will design and implement the project's M&E framework, collect and analyze performance data and provide reports and feedback to enhance project effectiveness and support informed decision-making.

KEY PERFORMANCE AREAS:

  • Design and implement the project’s M&E framework, including indicators, baselines, targets and data collection tools.
  • Develop and maintain databases and systems to track project inputs, outputs, outcomes and impacts in alignment with the project’s theory of change.
  • Collect, analyze and synthesize quantitative and qualitative data to monitor project performance.
  • Undertake data analysis and reporting for all relevant purposes, including monthly, quarterly, semi-annual and annual reports, donor reports and policy reporting.
  • Prepare timely, accurate and comprehensive reports on project performance for the PMU, donors and other stakeholders.
  • Ensure timely compilation and reporting on the project Log-frame in accordance with World Bank reporting guidelines and Government of Eswatini (GoE) reporting procedures.
  • Provide feedback and recommendations to the project management team and EWADE to inform adaptive management and decision-making.
  • Conduct regular field visits and coordinate with implementing partners to ensure data quality, consistency and reliability.
  • Support capacity building of project staff and partners on M&E practices, tools and reporting requirements.
  • Ensure compliance with World Bank M&E policies, guidelines, and reporting standards.
  • Contribute to learning and knowledge management by documenting best practices, lessons learned and success stories.
  • Support the design and conduct of tracer studies, mid-term and end-of-project evaluations, including impact assessments.

 

EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES:   

  • Holder of a Bachelor’s Degree in any of the following fields: Monitoring and Evaluation, Demography, Population Studies, Statistics, Economics, rural development or any other related subjects from a reputable University.
  • Demonstrated experience in designing and implementing M&E systems in a multi- faceted rural development project.
  • Demonstrated experience in data processing and management of large-scale surveys.
  • Demonstrated experience of at least 3 years of application of Computer statistical packages and/ or data analysis software (e.g. SAS, SPSS, and Advanced Excel) and basic computer skills (word-processing, power point, and databases) are a must.
  • At least five (5) years direct experience in a position of monitoring and evaluation of rural development and national projects
  • Possession of additional training in impact evaluation, familiarity with the operations and use of IT in monitoring and evaluation are added advantages.
  • Strong experience in conducting research studies including the entire evaluation cycle, from design and formulation to implementation, analysis and presentation of results and recommendations.
  • Good oral and written communication skills. Should be fluent in English.
  • Proven high level of integrity in handling public resources and in executing duties.
  • A high level of interpersonal and management skills and ability to work with teams.
  • Must be result focused and be able to work under pressure and tight deadlines.
  • High level of integrity.

procnotices.notice_text:
REOI

Country: The People's Republic of China
Project Name: IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project

Loan No.: 9213-CN

Assignment Name: Project Publicity

Contract No.: GDCS-030

Bidding No.: 0733-26083817

The Government of the People's Republic of China has received a loan from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development to improve food safety management at the national and sub-national levels and to reduce food safety risks in selected value chains. The project is being implemented by the State Administration for Market Regulation, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, Guangdong Province, and Shandong Province (Yantai City).

As part of the China Food Safety Project, Guangdong Province is responsible for the implementation of the World Bank-financed Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project. The project comprises four sub-components: Food Safety Supervision Process, Institution Building and Regulatory Performance, Whole Value Chain Food Safety Control, and Project Implementation Support.

This Contract, namely the Project Publicity Contract (Contract No.: GDCS-030), utilizes World Bank loan funds to procure a Project Publicity Consulting Advisor (hereinafter referred to as the 'Consulting Advisor') to carry out promotional activities for the World Bank-financed Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project. Through a matrix-based publicity strategy across short video platforms, newspapers, official social media accounts, and news media, the project will showcase and promote its implementation outcomes and achievements from multiple perspectives and through diverse channels.

The estimated start date for the tasks under this Contract is October 2026, with an anticipated implementation period of 27 months

Guangdong Provincial Center of Agro-product Safety and Quality (Guangdong Green Food Development Center) hereby invites eligible and interested consulting advisors to provide publicity services. The main scope of work includes, but is not limited to, the following:

1.Formulate the publicity plan for the World Bank-financed Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project;

2.Convergent media publicity for the project;

3.Live-streaming promotion;

4.Design and production of promotional materials, such as posters and brochures;

5.Conceptual promotion and branding;

6.Photography and videography for project events;

7.Collect and organize publicity outcomes, draft summary reports, and assist with project acceptance and verification.

The detailed scope of services and other requirements are specified in the attached Terms of Reference (TOR) for the Consulting Services on the Project Publicity under the IBRD Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality Safety Improvement (Demonstration) Project

 

I.Selection Criteria for the Consultants' Shortlist:

1.Capability to independently bear civil liability (Must provide a copy of the Business License or the Certificate of Legal Person for Public Institutions);

2.Sound financial accounting system (Must provide audited financial reports for the past 3 years);

3.Possess the professional and technical capabilities necessary to fulfill the Contract (Applicants must provide: A Letter of Commitment demonstrating media publicity capabilities. Format to be determined by the applicant);

4.Good record of tax and social security payment in accordance with the law (Must provide proof of tax payment and social security contribution for the past 3 months);

5.Good business credit and sound business performance (Must provide a statement certifying no major illegal or irregular business activities in the past 3 years, and that the applicant is not listed on the "Credit China" website as a "person subject to enforcement for dishonesty," "major tax violation entity," or "entity with serious illegal acts in government procurement");

6.Have a minimum of five (5) years of experience in publicity and promotional work related to agriculture, food, and other relevant sectors (Applicants must provide: A Company Profile. The profile must include at least the company's history and experience in publicity, promotion, planning, advertising, and brand building related to agriculture or food. The Company Profile must be stamped with the official company seal);

7.Have successfully completed at least one (1) similar project publicity service contract within the past five (5) years (from January 1, 2021, up to the deadline for submission of the Letter of Intent). The completion date shall be determined based on the contract completion date, the acceptance certificate date, or the completion date specified in the owner's certificate.

Similar project publicity service contracts refer to government project publicity, international project publicity, and convergent media publicity projects that are similar in scope of services to this Contract.

Applicants must provide: Photocopies of relevant supporting documents, including key pages of the contract that clearly indicate the contract name, scope of services, service period, date of signature, and the signatures and seals of both contracting parties. If the contract does not specify a service period, an acceptance certificate or a Client's Certificate may be provided. The Client's Certificate must explicitly state that the project has been completed in accordance with the contract and specify the date of completion, and it must be stamped with the official seal of the client.

 

Please note that the Consultant must provide all the supporting materials stipulated in the above "Selection Criteria for the Consultants' Shortlist," along with detailed contact information (including contact person, address, telephone number, email address, etc.). The Consultant shall solely bear the relevant responsibilities and consequences for any issues arising from incomplete submission or failure to meet the requirements.

II.Interested Consultants are advised to refer to the provisions regarding Conflict of Interest policy in Sections 3.14, 3.16, and 3.17, and the provisions regarding Eligibility in Sections 3.21, 3.22, 3.23, and 3.24 of the "World Bank Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers" (November 2020). The Consulting Advisor shall proactively disclose whether it has any affiliation with the following entities. If such an affiliation exists, the Consulting Advisor must provide a statement explaining the relationship (format to be determined by the applicant, including but not limited to the shareholding structure and shareholding ratio). If no such affiliation exists, the Consulting Advisor must provide a Letter of Commitment (format to be determined by the applicant):

Client: Guangdong Agricultural Product Quality and Safety Center (Guangdong Green Food Development Center)

Procurement Agent: CITIC International Tendering Co., Ltd.

Feasibility Study Report Preparation Unit: Institute of Agricultural Economics and Information, Guangdong Academy of Agricultural Sciences

Preliminary Design Unit: Guangzhou Urban Planning and Surveying Research Institute

 

III.Consulting firms may form an association with other firms, but it must be clearly indicated whether the arrangement is in the form of a Joint Venture or Subcontracting. If the Joint Venture form is chosen, each member of the Joint Venture shall be jointly and severally liable for the entire Contract. Please note that every member of the Joint Venture must meet the requirements of the above "Selection Criteria for the Consultants' Shortlist".

IV.The Consultant will be selected through the Consultant Qualification Selection (CQS) method as specified in the Procurement Regulations.

V.This Request for Expressions of Interest (REOI) is published on the "World Bank Section of China Tendering and Bidding Public Service Platform" (https://bulletin.cebpubservice.com/bank/index.html) and "China Tendering and Bidding Network" (https://www.chinabidding.cn/).

VI.For further information, please contact the Procurement Agent during working hours from September 7, 2026, to September 20, 2026, between 9:00-11:30 AM and 1:00-5:00 PM (Beijing Time).

VII.The number of hard copies of the Expression of Interest (including: specified supporting materials, a brief introduction of the company's basic information and business scope, and any other materials the Consultant deems necessary) shall be: one original and four copies in Chinese. Each copy must be perfect bound. In addition, the Consultant shall submit an electronic version separately on a USB flash drive at the same time as the submission of the Expression of Interest. The USB flash drive must be labeled with the Contract Number and the full name of the Consultant. The USB flash drive shall be sealed together with the original Expression of Interest.
